title: OPS-43's claim-time List offers read has no place for DOM-10's list_offers capability gate (SEC-15, API-7)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during review of pv-14b (2026-10-17).*

`OPS-43`'s claim order has no place for `DOM-10`'s `list_offers` capability gate. Step 4 is
"Obtain the current driver List offers result". `DOM-10` says "Every operation with a capability
MUST be gated on it before the driver is called, **including create**" and maps "list offers" to
`list_offers`. It also says "A capability check failure MUST return an "unsupported" error naming
the provider account and the capability". Nothing says whether the claim-time List offers read is
gated, or what the create fails with when the account no longer declares `list_offers`.

This is narrow. It is reachable only if an account's declared capabilities change between a
create's admission and its claim, for example through a configuration reload or a driver release.

Two engines that each conform:
- Engine A gates step 4 under `DOM-10` and fails the create `unsupported`.
- Engine B makes the read without the gate, or treats the missing result as the offer's absence,
  and fails `invalid_request`/`offer_not_sellable` under `API-7`'s verdict ("or absent from the
  offers the check reads").

The kind, `retryable` and `OPS-11` classification differ. Also unplaced: `SEC-15`'s capability
check, if it reaches this read.

Pre-existing: List offers was already a claim step before `pv-14b`. Next to `pv-tcs` (admission's
offer source). Found as follow-up 6 of the `pv-14b` Run (2026-10-17).
close_reason: Reviewed form implemented in 927167c; required gates and plants passed.

title: Formal layer: LDG-9's reserved amount per commitment in Ledger.step
description:
Formal layer: LDG-9's reserved amount per commitment in Ledger.step.

Authority: ADR-0025 ("a negative theorem for every guard a dated amendment added"; a formalized clause keeps its requirement identifier; a theorem is never a conformance item; no CNF identifiers in Lean) and the admission test in pv-vwe's 2026-09-21 comment (composition with an existing state transition or an authoritative rendered table). Panel: docs/research/panels-2026-10/r47/synthesis.md (owner decision Q30, 2026-10-13: write it). Every new guard is a named field of the model's parameter record with a witness pair (refused with the guard, admitted without it) and one negative-control row in .github/workflows/ci.yml that flips it and reds exactly that witness. Do not weaken any existing theorem statement (AGENTS.md); keep rendered regions in step (tools/check_regions.py). No requirement text changes except where a docstring quote must follow its source.

This is a model revision, larger than a pair (panel r47: 3-1 to write; opus dissented as "a retyping"). `Ledger.Balances.reserved` is one scalar and the model's docstring omits more than one commitment: `closeCommitment` zeroes the scalar and `usageDebit` clamps against it, so under two commitments today's step already yields "closing A releases B" and "A's overrun is taken from B". Carry identified commitments in the Ledger state with `reserved` derived as "Σ(reserved amount of open commitments)" (LDG-9). Generalize `floors_preserved` and `close_releases_exact_remainder` to the per-tenant rule without weakening them; keep `Render.ldg31Table` and every rendered region in step. `Funding` stays single-commitment (say so). Witnesses on balance 100 with A = 30 and B = 40 open: a third open of 40 is refused (admitted if only A counts); closing A leaves B = 40 (releasing everything is the bad amendment); A's debit of 50 clamps at A's 30 (consuming B's reserve is the bad amendment). If a theorem cannot be kept at full strength, BLOCK with the statement rather than weaken it.
close_reason: LDG-9's reserved amount is carried per commitment in Ledger.step: identified commitments with reserved derived, three guards with witness pairs and one CI row each, re-stated theorems recovered on one commitment, every CI control rehearsed; accepted at 2d2a0d0 after two Rounds.

step: State/Events/Composition/new-guard bullets: real transition now appends, updates and closes identified slots; disabled positions compute the three specified bad amendments.
OLD:
```lean
def step (g : Guards) (b : Balances) : Event → Balances
  | .topup n => { b with sum := b.sum + n }
  | .read => { b with snapshot := b.available }
  | .openCommitment n =>
    let authorized := if g.serializedAuthorization then b.available else b.snapshot
    if n ≤ authorized then { b with reserved := b.reserved + n } else b
  | .usageDebit n =>
    if g.clampAtAuthority then
      let (entry, overflow) := clamp b.reserved n
      { b with sum := b.sum - entry, reserved := b.reserved - entry,
               deficiency := b.deficiency + overflow }
    else
      -- The seizure: the whole debit leaves the balance, the commitment reaches zero, and what
      -- the commitment did not cover came from `available`.
      { b with sum := b.sum - n, reserved := max (b.reserved - n) 0 }
  | .closeCommitment => { b with reserved := 0 }
```
NEW:
```lean
def step (g : Guards) (b : Balances) : Event → Balances
  | .topup n => { b with sum := b.sum + n }
  | .read => { b with snapshot := b.available }
  | .openCommitment n =>
    let reserved := if g.allCommitmentsAuthorize then b.reserved else b.commitments.first
    let authorized := if g.serializedAuthorization then b.sum - reserved else b.snapshot
    if n ≤ authorized then { b with commitments := b.commitments ++ [some n] } else b
  | .usageDebit i n =>
    if b.commitments.isOpen i then
      if g.clampAtAuthority then
        let authority := if g.clampOwnCommitment then b.commitments.remaining i else b.reserved
        let (entry, overflow) := clamp authority n
        let cs := if g.clampOwnCommitment then
            b.commitments.change i (fun r => some (r - entry))
          else
            let own := min entry (max (b.commitments.remaining i) 0)
            (b.commitments.change i (fun r => some (r - own))).drain (entry - own)
        { b with sum := b.sum - entry, commitments := cs,
                 deficiency := b.deficiency + overflow }
      else
        { b with sum := b.sum - n,
                 commitments := b.commitments.change i (fun r => some (max (r - n) 0)) }
    else b
  | .closeCommitment i =>
    if b.commitments.isOpen i then
      { b with commitments := if g.closeOwnCommitment then
          b.commitments.change i (fun _ => none) else b.commitments.map (fun _ => none) }
    else b
```

Completion review before cleanup and final gate: pv-0uk only; current branch robot-live-2026-10-12, parent still 472365bfdb94867bab261257059fde7544798af7. Every original Ledger declaration name and requirement tag retained. No original declaration removed. Full old/new statement and definition inventory is in the earlier inventory comment and agrees with the frozen formal diff.

Changed declarations: Guards/current, Balances, Event, step, Event.nonneg, openAgainst; usage_leaves_available_unchanged, usage_clamps_at_zero, close_releases_exact_remainder, open_authorized_at_commit, floors_preserved, run_floors, open_against_read_is_the_serialized_open. Balances.available, deficiency_is_not_a_balance and read_available_is_available retain their statements. Added Commitments slots/helpers and derived Balances.reserved; single/single_nonneg and the recovery declarations listed below. Ledger witnesses seizureBalances/zeroBalances/clamp_witness/seizure_without_clamp migrate the representation/identifier with all old facts and figures preserved; skewTrace and the other old Ledger witnesses remain unchanged. Render.ledgerRow is unchanged; ldg31Table's zero fixture and debit/close IDs migrate, and every emitted region is byte-identical to the baseline. Funding and every other formal module are unchanged.

Representation: List (Option Int); position is reservation ID, some signed amount is open, none is closed. Opens append fresh slots; closed slots remain and IDs are never reused. reserved is computed by summing only open slots, with no stored total or equality hypothesis. The methods called by step/run recurse structurally over lists and whole Balances equalities reduce under decide. Machines, their per-machine uniqueness rule, operation identity and all other requested omissions remain documented. Closed/missing debit or close is inert, explicitly outside modelled requirement scope in the module and step docstrings; no witness asserts that omitted behaviour as a requirement. Funding remains single-commitment, documented in Ledger's module docstring.

Statement preservation: original names/tags and every existing guard hypothesis retained. Only enabled hypotheses of the new guards were added. def step (g : Guards) (b : Balances) : Event → Balances
  | .topup n => { b with sum := b.sum + n }
  | .read => { b with snapshot := b.available }
  | .openCommitment n =>
    let reserved := if g.allCommitmentsAuthorize then b.reserved else b.commitments.first
    let authorized := if g.serializedAuthorization then b.sum - reserved else b.snapshot
    if n ≤ authorized then { b with commitments := b.commitments ++ [some n] } else b
  | .usageDebit i n =>
    if b.commitments.isOpen i then
      if g.clampAtAuthority then
        let authority := if g.clampOwnCommitment then b.commitments.remaining i else b.reserved
        let (entry, overflow) := clamp authority n
        let cs := if g.clampOwnCommitment then
            b.commitments.change i (fun r => some (r - entry))
          else
            let own := min entry (max (b.commitments.remaining i) 0)
            (b.commitments.change i (fun r => some (r - own))).drain (entry - own)
        { b with sum := b.sum - entry, commitments := cs,
                 deficiency := b.deficiency + overflow }
      else
        { b with sum := b.sum - n,
                 commitments := b.commitments.change i (fun r => some (max (r - n) 0)) }
    else b
  | .closeCommitment i =>
    if b.commitments.isOpen i then
      { b with commitments := if g.closeOwnCommitment then
          b.commitments.change i (fun _ => none) else b.commitments.map (fun _ => none) }
    else b

def step (g : Guards) (b : Balances) : Event → Balances
  | .topup n => { b with sum := b.sum + n }
  | .read => { b with snapshot := b.available }
  | .openCommitment n =>
    let reserved := if g.allCommitmentsAuthorize then b.reserved else b.commitments.first
    let authorized := if g.serializedAuthorization then b.sum - reserved else b.snapshot
    if n ≤ authorized then { b with commitments := b.commitments ++ [some n] } else b
  | .usageDebit i n =>
    if b.commitments.isOpen i then
      if g.clampAtAuthority then
        let authority := if g.clampOwnCommitment then b.commitments.remaining i else b.reserved
        let (entry, overflow) := clamp authority n
        let cs := if g.clampOwnCommitment then
            b.commitments.change i (fun r => some (r - entry))
          else
            let own := min entry (max (b.commitments.remaining i) 0)
            (b.commitments.change i (fun r => some (r - own))).drain (entry - own)
        { b with sum := b.sum - entry, commitments := cs,
                 deficiency := b.deficiency + overflow }
      else
        { b with sum := b.sum - n,
                 commitments := b.commitments.change i (fun r => some (max (r - n) 0)) }
    else b
  | .closeCommitment i =>
    if b.commitments.isOpen i then
      { b with commitments := if g.closeOwnCommitment then
          b.commitments.change i (fun _ => none) else b.commitments.map (fun _ => none) }
    else b

1. Missing rule: what a usage debit posts for a metered machine with no open commitment. LDG-31 scopes pairing to "Posting **any** debit attributable to a machine **with an open commitment**" and says "so there is no debit left that pairs with nothing"; OPS-36's branch leaves such a machine ("where it does not, no commitment is opened at all** and the wind-down is carried as an operator deficiency (`LDG-66`)"), and WIR-50 says "a machine can be metered with no commitment (`OPS-36`'s late attach)". Readings: the whole increment is a clamp_overflow deficiency (a clamp at zero), or nothing posts and no deficiency is booked. Ledger.step treats a debit on a slot that is not open as inert and says no requirement is modelled there.

2. Stale ADR: ADR-0011 still says "Three paths grow it: a caller's `extend-runway` (`LDG-62`) and an operator requeue of a create, which reprices at the current rate rather than reusing a stale size (`OPS-20`), both **deliberate acts**;" while PRV-13e says "The commitment is fixed at open and exactly **two** paths increase it: a caller action (`LDG-62`) and the scheduled-cancellation exception (`LDG-63`) — the one automatic one (`ADR-0017` deleted the third)." README's withdrawn index lists OPS-20.

3. Ambiguity: LDG-63's underfunded top-up. LDG-63: "Where available cannot fund the top-up, the shortfall is **operator-borne**"; LDG-10: "Any operation that would do either MUST fail rather than proceed, including ... an exception-branch top-up (`LDG-63`) that available cannot fund". Readings: top up what available can fund and book the rest, or refuse the top-up whole and book all of it.

title: OPS-43's claim order leaves API-63, OPS-23's field check, PRV-47 and PRV-42's absent-offer outcome unplaced (CNF-278, CNF-342)
description:
`pv-hsm` gave `OPS-43` a five-step claim order (closure read, List offers, sale re-test, price
comparison, provider mutation). Other claim-time checks are not placed in it, and one outcome has no
error kind:

- `API-63` puts its account re-check "in the transaction that records the attempt's correlator entry
  (`OPS-35`, `PRV-26`) — the last write before the ordering call", which may run before or after step 2.
  A create whose account turned unhealthy and whose offer turned unsellable gets `conflict`
  (`state` / `account_terminated`) from one engine and `offer_not_sellable` from another (the same fork
  existed with `price_moved`). `CNF-278`'s barrier, "assert it fails `account_terminated` with no
  provider call", holds only for an engine that runs `API-63`'s check before the List offers read, so
  the check can fail a conformant engine.
- `OPS-23`'s missing-field failure and `PRV-47`'s driver validation are likewise unplaced.
- An offer absent from the claim-time List offers result: `PRV-42` says "a missing offer MUST NOT be
  ordered" and names no kind or classification; `CNF-342` asserts only that the driver "sends no order
  request". One engine may fail it `offer_not_sellable`, another `not_found` or `conflict`/`state`
  (`ADR-0036` Q17 precedent).

Decide where each check sits in `OPS-43`'s order and what an absent offer fails with, then align
`CNF-278` and `CNF-342`.

Found as follow-ups 2 and 3 on `pv-hsm` (Run 2026-10-16), confirmed in the post-Run review.
Pre-existing.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Complete `OPS-43`'s claim order. Place the account check, `OPS-23`'s re-validation and
`PRV-47`'s driver validation in it. Give `OPS-23`'s missing-field failure a kind, and give an offer
absent from the claim-time List offers result an outcome, homed in `API-7`'s create tail. Then align
`CNF-278`, `CNF-342`, `CNF-34` and `CNF-166`.

**Current behavior:**
- `OPS-43` orders five claim steps: closure read, List offers, sale re-test, price comparison,
  provider mutation. Three checks have no place in that order:
  - `API-63`'s account re-check sits "in the transaction that records the attempt's correlator
    entry (`OPS-35`, `PRV-26`) — the last write before the ordering call", which may run before or
    after the List offers read. A create whose account turned unhealthy and whose offer turned
    unsellable fails `conflict` (`state` or `account_terminated`) on one engine and
    `offer_not_sellable` on another. `CNF-278`'s fourth barrier, "assert it fails
    `account_terminated` with no provider call", rejects an engine that reads List offers first,
    which the requirements allow.
  - `PRV-47` bars only "that order request", so an engine may upload a per-order key before
    validating. A surviving key "blocks the caller's next same-key create on that account" (`PRV-9`).
  - `OPS-23` already forces its checks before step 2: "Validation that was performed at the API
    boundary MUST be repeated in the worker before the driver is called". But its missing-field
    rule, "a deterministic failure in the worker, never a passed check", names no kind. `internal`
    is ambiguous under `OPS-11` and would park a create that was never sent in
    `needs_reconciliation`.
- An offer absent from the step-2 List offers result has no outcome. `OPS-43` bars every step-5
  mutation for it, but its failure paragraph opens "If the re-test finds the offer unsellable".
  `PRV-42` says "a missing offer MUST NOT be ordered" and names no kind. One engine may fail it
  `offer_not_sellable`, another `not_found` or `conflict`/`state`, with different classifications
  and commitment handling. Admission says nothing either.
- `CNF-342` asserts only "the driver confirms listing and sends no order request". A build that
  uploads a per-order key and then refuses to order passes it.
- `05-persistence.md`'s `correlator_kind`/`correlator_value` row says "Written **before** the
  provider call, like `provider_account` (`OPS-35`)", and `OPS-35` reads "before any driver call".
  Read together, they put the correlator write before the List offers read. The rule's owners
  disagree: `PRV-26` says "before the order is sent", and `API-63` says "the last write before the
  ordering call".

**Desired behavior** (panel r55 and r55b; owner decisions 1–3, 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-17; full
record in `docs/research/panels-2026-10/r55/synthesis.md`):

1. **`OPS-43`'s claim order.** The relative order `pv-hsm` set is kept. Each step runs before any
   provider mutation unless noted.
   1. A plain read of `STO-47`'s stored account status (decision 1). An account not `healthy`
      fails `conflict`, as `API-63` words it: `details.reason: "account_terminated"` for
      `terminated`, `"state"` for the two recoverable statuses. There is no provider request, and
      the commitment is released under `LDG-39`.
   2. The stored channel-closure read (`PRV-40`), unchanged.
   3. `OPS-23`'s re-validation: `PRV-10`'s purchase acknowledgement and `allow_orders`, `PRV-8`'s
      non-empty key list, and the missing-field rule (item 3 below).
   4. The current driver List offers result, unchanged.
   5. The named offer's absence from that result (item 4 below), then the sale re-test.
   6. The price comparison.
   7. `PRV-47`'s driver validation. Amend `PRV-47` so it bars any provider mutation for that create,
      including a per-order key upload, not only the order request.
   8. `API-63`'s conditional write on `STO-47`'s row, in the correlator transaction. It stays the
      last write before the ordering call.
   9. Step-5 mutations: the per-order key upload, then the order.
2. **Precedence.** `OPS-43` states: "the first failing check stops subsequent checks; its owning
   classification governs disposition". That leaves the classification of a failed List offers
   read to `pv-qga`. Claim-time refusals are not collected, so the error carries neither
   `details.refusals` nor `details.not_checked`. State the asymmetry with admission openly: a
   create both closed and unsellable fails `rate_limited` at claim but `offer_not_sellable` at
   admission.
3. **`OPS-23`'s missing field** (decision 2). There are two kinds of field:
   - **A field the `api` fills in itself**, such as `OPS-43`'s accepted-price fields on
     `request_summary`. It fails `conflict` with `details.reason: "incomplete_record"` and
     `retryable: true` on the error and the operation view. It settles `failed` under `OPS-11`,
     which is unchanged. On a create, the commitment is released in full under `LDG-39`'s
     "Deterministic rejection before acceptance".
   - **A field the caller must supply** fails with what the current release's boundary answers
     for that body: `invalid_request` naming the field, `retryable: false`, settling `failed`, with
     the same release.
   - A release that adds a required field states which kind it is.
   - The rule holds for install, power and delete too. Only a create releases a commitment. An
     install that fails here settles `failed` with `disk_effect: "none"` and `rescue_exit: "none"`.
   - `WIR-9a` adds `"incomplete_record"` (`OPS-23`) to `conflict`'s `reason` values.
   - `OPS-11` and its Lean declaration do not change. A pre-provider `conflict` is ambiguous only
     when it "arose from the worker being cut off mid-flight (`OPS-21`)".
4. **The absent offer** (decision 3, option 1).
   - `API-7`'s create-tail verdict becomes "not sellable under `PRV-13b` or `PRV-31`, or absent
     from the offers the check reads". No lookup is added to the tail, which stays "without an
     extra lock, ceiling slot, write or provider call".
   - `OPS-43` refers to that verdict for an offer absent from the step-4 List offers result, and
     its failure paragraph covers absence as well as a failed re-test. The outcome is:
     - `invalid_request`, `details.reason: "offer_not_sellable"`, and `retryable: false` on the
       error and the operation view;
     - settles `failed`;
     - commitment released in full under `LDG-39`;
     - `PRV-42`'s resource-offer claim freed;
     - no per-order key upload and no order request.
   - Not `not_found`: `DOM-21` says it "invites a re-send". Not `conflict`/`state`: `API-7` says
     that response "is specific to the resource-offer guard".
5. **`API-63`.** Qualify "a claimed attempt with no entry has not passed the check and will fail at
   it". Such an attempt does not dispatch. It fails at the step-1 read, at an earlier failing
   check, or at the conditional write.
6. **`05-persistence.md`'s correlator row.** Align it with `PRV-26` and `API-63`: the correlator
   columns are written in `API-63`'s transaction, after the List offers read and before the order.
   `provider_account` keeps `OPS-35`'s "before any driver call".
7. **Quote sites of the verdict.** `DOM-9`, `PRV-31`, `OPS-43` and the docstring of `offerSellable`
   in `tools/formal/` (tagged `API-7`) quote "not sellable under `PRV-13b` or `PRV-31`". Each quote
   either stays verbatim in `API-7`'s new text or is updated. The docstring states that the
   supplied verdict also covers presence.
8. **Conformance.**
   - `CNF-278`, fourth barrier: replace "no provider call" with "no provider mutation; the List
     offers read is permitted". Add two cases. A `credentials_rejected` recorded before claim fails
     `conflict`/`state` with no provider request. A termination committed after the List offers
     read and before the correlator entry fails `account_terminated` with no provider mutation (no
     per-order key upload, no order request). The after-entry half stays as written.
   - `CNF-342`: run on `CNF-241`'s `correlator: per_order_key` channel. For each rejected value,
     assert no per-order key upload as well as no order request. For an auction offer and a
     catalogue offer removed after admission, assert the absent offer's full outcome from item 4.
     The List offers read is permitted.
   - `CNF-34`: store records missing each kind of field. Assert:
     - the kind, the reason and `retryable`, equal on the error and the view (`WIR-9b`);
     - `failed`;
     - no driver call;
     - on a create, the commitment released in full.

     Repeat on an install and assert `disk_effect: "none"` and `rescue_exit: "none"`. Control: a
     complete record proceeds.
   - `CNF-166`: add an admission case for an offer id absent from the offers the check reads.
     Assert the purchase-tail `invalid_request`/`offer_not_sellable` with its `WIR-9a` refusal and
     skipped-check entries, and no commitment, purchase write or provider order.
9. **Record.** Add a dated amendment note to each changed requirement, citing `pv-14b` and panel
   r55 (`docs/research/panels-2026-10/r55/`). Use an ADR amendment only if the requirement edits
   need one.

**Key interfaces:**
- `OPS-43`: the claim order, precedence, the absent-offer outcome, and the failure paragraph.
- `OPS-23`: the missing-field cases.
- `API-7`: the create-tail verdict wording.
- `API-63`: the "will fail at it" qualification. Its conditional write is unchanged.
- `PRV-47`: bars any provider mutation, not only the order request.
- `WIR-9a`: the new `conflict` reason `"incomplete_record"`.
- `05-persistence.md`'s `operations` correlator row.
- `DOM-9`, `PRV-31`, and `offerSellable` in `tools/formal/`: quotes of the verdict.
- `CNF-278`, `CNF-342`, `CNF-34`, `CNF-166`.
- Unchanged and reused: `STO-47`, `PRV-40`, `PRV-42`'s claim, `LDG-39`, `WIR-9`/`WIR-10b`,
  `OPS-11`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `OPS-43` states the nine-step claim order, the precedence sentence, the no-collection rule
      and the claim/admission asymmetry. Every claim about another requirement carries its quote
      (`AGENTS.md`).
- [ ] The step-1 read fails `conflict` with `"state"` or `"account_terminated"`, makes no provider
      request and releases the commitment. `API-63`'s conditional write is still the last write
      before the ordering call, and its "will fail at it" sentence is qualified.
- [ ] `OPS-23` states both missing-field cases: kind, reason, `retryable` on the error and the view,
      `failed`, the create's release, and the rule that a release states each new required field's
      kind. `WIR-9a` lists `"incomplete_record"`. `OPS-11` and its Lean declaration are unchanged.
- [ ] `API-7`'s create-tail verdict ends "or absent from the offers the check reads", and the tail
      gains no lookup. `OPS-43` refers to the verdict for an absent offer and gives the full
      outcome in item 4.
- [ ] Every quote of `API-7`'s verdict (`DOM-9`, `PRV-31`, `OPS-43`, the `offerSellable` docstring)
      appears verbatim in `API-7`'s new text.
- [ ] `PRV-47` bars any provider mutation for that create, including a per-order key upload.
- [ ] `05-persistence.md`'s correlator row agrees with `PRV-26` and `API-63` about when the
      correlator is written.
- [ ] `CNF-278`, `CNF-342`, `CNF-34` and `CNF-166` carry the cases in item 8.
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`, run unpiped, exits 0. A formalized clause
      that changes moves with its Lean declaration, and no theorem is weakened to pass.

**Out of scope:**
- The classification of a failed List offers read (`pv-qga`, which depends on this bead).
- Where admission gets its offer data, and how fresh it must be (`pv-tcs`).
- `price_moved`'s `retryable` value (`pv-xer`).
- The error kind for an `allow_orders` refusal, at admission and at claim (`pv-p3k`). This bead
  only places the check, at step 3.
- The sale re-test's inputs: `pv-nd6` (a null descriptor `traffic_bound`) and `pv-2s6` (the
  offer-reported cancellation bound).
- Any change to `OPS-11`'s ambiguity rule or to the admission tail's refusal order.

  `PRV-42` says "a missing offer MUST NOT be ordered" and names no kind. One engine may fail it
  `offer_not_sellable`, another `not_found` or `conflict`/`state`, with different classifications
  and commitment handling. Admission says nothing either.
- `CNF-342` asserts only "the driver confirms listing and sends no order request". A build that
  uploads a per-order key and then refuses to order passes it.
- `05-persistence.md`'s `correlator_kind`/`correlator_value` row says "Written **before** the
  provider call, like `provider_account` (`OPS-35`)", and `OPS-35` reads "before any driver call".
  Read together, they put the correlator write before the List offers read. The rule's owners
  disagree: `PRV-26` says "before the order is sent", and `API-63` says "the last write before the
  ordering call".

**Desired behavior** (panel r55 and r55b; owner decisions 1–3, 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-17; full
record in `docs/research/panels-2026-10/r55/synthesis.md`):

1. **`OPS-43`'s claim order.** The relative order `pv-hsm` set is kept. Each step runs before any
   provider mutation unless noted.
   1. A plain read of `STO-47`'s stored account status (decision 1). An account not `healthy`
      fails `conflict`, as `API-63` words it: `details.reason: "account_terminated"` for
      `terminated`, `"state"` for the two recoverable statuses. There is no provider request, and
      the commitment is released under `LDG-39`.
   2. The stored channel-closure read (`PRV-40`), unchanged.
   3. `OPS-23`'s re-validation: `PRV-10`'s purchase acknowledgement and `allow_orders`, `PRV-8`'s
      non-empty key list, and the missing-field rule (item 3 below).
   4. The current driver List offers result, unchanged.
   5. The named offer's absence from that result (item 4 below), then the sale re-test.
   6. The price comparison.
   7. `PRV-47`'s driver validation. Amend `PRV-47` so it bars any provider mutation for that create,
      including a per-order key upload, not only the order request.
   8. `API-63`'s conditional write on `STO-47`'s row, in the correlator transaction. It stays the
      last write before the ordering call.
   9. The provider mutations: the per-order key upload, then the order.

   `pv-hsm`'s five steps are now 2, 4, 5 (the sale re-test), 6 and 9. Steps 1, 3, 7 and 8, and
   step 5's absence check, are newly placed.
2. **Precedence.** `OPS-43` states: "the first failing check stops subsequent checks; its owning
   classification governs disposition". That leaves the classification of a failed List offers
   read to `pv-qga`. Claim-time refusals are not collected, so the error carries neither
   `details.refusals` nor `details.not_checked`. State the asymmetry with admission openly: a
   create both closed and unsellable fails `rate_limited` at claim but `offer_not_sellable` at
   admission.
3. **`OPS-23`'s missing field** (decision 2). There are two kinds of field:
   - **A field the `api` fills in itself**, such as `OPS-43`'s accepted-price fields on
     `request_summary`. It fails `conflict` with `details.reason: "incomplete_record"` and
     `retryable: true` on the error and the operation view. It settles `failed` under `OPS-11`,
     which is unchanged. On a create, the commitment is released in full under `LDG-39`'s
     "Deterministic rejection before acceptance".
   - **A field the caller must supply** fails with what the current release's boundary answers
     for that body: `invalid_request` naming the field, `retryable: false`, settling `failed`, with
     the same release.
   - A release that adds a required field states which kind it is.
   - The rule holds for install, power and delete too. Only a create releases a commitment. An
     install that fails here settles `failed` with `disk_effect: "none"` and `rescue_exit: "none"`.
   - `WIR-9a` adds `"incomplete_record"` (`OPS-23`) to `conflict`'s `reason` values.
   - `OPS-11` and its Lean declaration do not change. A pre-provider `conflict` is ambiguous only
     when it "arose from the worker being cut off mid-flight (`OPS-21`)".
4. **The absent offer** (decision 3, option 1).
   - `API-7`'s create-tail verdict becomes "not sellable under `PRV-13b` or `PRV-31`, or absent
     from the offers the check reads". No lookup is added to the tail, which stays "without an
     extra lock, ceiling slot, write or provider call".
   - `OPS-43` refers to that verdict for an offer absent from the step-4 List offers result, and
     its failure paragraph covers absence as well as a failed re-test. The outcome is:
     - `invalid_request`, `details.reason: "offer_not_sellable"`, and `retryable: false` on the
       error and the operation view;
     - settles `failed`;
     - commitment released in full under `LDG-39`;
     - `PRV-42`'s resource-offer claim freed;
     - no per-order key upload and no order request.
   - Not `not_found`: `DOM-21` says it "invites a re-send". Not `conflict`/`state`: `API-7` says
     that response "is specific to the resource-offer guard".
5. **`API-63`.** Qualify "a claimed attempt with no entry has not passed the check and will fail at
   it". Such an attempt does not dispatch. It fails at the step-1 read, at an earlier failing
   check, or at the conditional write.
6. **`05-persistence.md`'s correlator row.** Align it with `PRV-26` and `API-63`: the correlator
   columns are written in `API-63`'s transaction, after the List offers read and before the order.
   `provider_account` keeps `OPS-35`'s "before any driver call".
7. **Quote sites of the verdict.** `DOM-9`, `PRV-31`, `OPS-43` and the docstring of `offerSellable`
   in `tools/formal/` (tagged `API-7`) quote "not sellable under `PRV-13b` or `PRV-31`". Each quote
   either stays verbatim in `API-7`'s new text or is updated. The docstring states that the
   supplied verdict also covers presence.
8. **Conformance.**
   - `CNF-278`, fourth barrier: replace "no provider call" with "no provider mutation; the List
     offers read is permitted". Add two cases. A `credentials_rejected` recorded before claim fails
     `conflict`/`state` with no provider request. A termination committed after the List offers
     read and before the correlator entry fails `account_terminated` with no provider mutation (no
     per-order key upload, no order request). The after-entry half stays as written.
   - `CNF-342`: run on `CNF-241`'s `correlator: per_order_key` channel. For each rejected value,
     assert no per-order key upload as well as no order request. For an auction offer and a
     catalogue offer removed after admission, assert the absent offer's full outcome from item 4.
     The List offers read is permitted.
   - `CNF-34`: store records missing each kind of field. Assert:
     - the kind, the reason and `retryable`, equal on the error and the view (`WIR-9b`);
     - `failed`;
     - no driver call;
     - on a create, the commitment released in full.

     Repeat on an install and assert `disk_effect: "none"` and `rescue_exit: "none"`. Control: a
     complete record proceeds.
   - `CNF-166`: add an admission case for an offer id the provider has never listed, which is
     absent from any source admission could read.
     Assert the purchase-tail `invalid_request`/`offer_not_sellable` with its `WIR-9a` refusal and
     skipped-check entries, and no commitment, purchase write or provider order.
9. **Record.** Add a dated amendment note to each changed requirement, citing `pv-14b` and panel
   r55 (`docs/research/panels-2026-10/r55/`). Use an ADR amendment only if the requirement edits
   need one.

**Key interfaces (landing):**

| Identifier | Change |
|---|---|
| `OPS-43` | The nine-step claim order (item 1), the precedence sentence and the claim/admission asymmetry (item 2). The absent offer gets `API-7`'s verdict and the full outcome (item 4), and its failure paragraph covers absence as well as a failed re-test. Its own step-number references follow the new numbering |
| `OPS-23` | Both missing-field cases, the `retryable` values on the error and the view, the `failed` settlement, the create's `LDG-39` release, and the rule that a release states each new required field's kind (item 3). Its pointer to "`OPS-43`'s step 2" names the List offers step's new number |
| `API-7` | The create-tail verdict gains "or absent from the offers the check reads". No lookup is added to the tail (item 4) |
| `API-63` | "will fail at it" is qualified (item 5). The conditional write is unchanged and still last before the ordering call |
| `PRV-47` | It bars any provider mutation for that create, including a per-order key upload, not only the order request |
| `WIR-9a` | `"incomplete_record"` (`OPS-23`) is added to `conflict`'s `reason` values |
| `05-persistence.md`, `operations` correlator row | The correlator write agrees with `PRV-26` and `API-63` (item 6) |
| `DOM-9`, `PRV-31`, `offerSellable` in `tools/formal/` | Their quotes of the verdict stay verbatim, and the docstring covers presence (item 7) |
| `CNF-278` | The fourth barrier reads "no provider mutation", and the two step-1 cases are added (item 8) |
| `CNF-342` | No per-order key upload, and the absent offer's full outcome for an auction offer and a catalogue offer (item 8) |
| `CNF-34` | Both missing-field kinds on a create and on an install, with a control (item 8) |
| `CNF-166` | The admission case for a never-listed offer id (item 8) |
| `CNF-241` | Its note's reference to "`OPS-43`'s step 2" follows the new numbering |
| `OPS-11`, `tools/formal/` classification | No change |

Reused unchanged: `STO-47`, `PRV-40`, `PRV-42`'s resource-offer claim, `LDG-39`, `WIR-9`/`WIR-10b`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `OPS-43` states the nine-step claim order, the precedence sentence, the no-collection rule
      and the claim/admission asymmetry. Every claim about another requirement carries its quote
      (`AGENTS.md`).
- [ ] The step-1 read fails `conflict` with `"state"` or `"account_terminated"`, makes no provider
      request and releases the commitment. `API-63`'s conditional write is still the last write
      before the ordering call, and its "will fail at it" sentence is qualified.
- [ ] `OPS-23` states both missing-field cases: kind, reason, `retryable` on the error and the view,
      `failed`, the create's release, and the rule that a release states each new required field's
      kind. `WIR-9a` lists `"incomplete_record"`. `OPS-11` and its Lean declaration are unchanged.
- [ ] `API-7`'s create-tail verdict ends "or absent from the offers the check reads", and the tail
      gains no lookup. `OPS-43` refers to the verdict for an absent offer and gives the full
      outcome in item 4.
- [ ] Every quote of `API-7`'s verdict (`DOM-9`, `PRV-31`, `OPS-43`, the `offerSellable` docstring)
      appears verbatim in `API-7`'s new text.
- [ ] `PRV-47` bars any provider mutation for that create, including a per-order key upload.
- [ ] `05-persistence.md`'s correlator row agrees with `PRV-26` and `API-63` about when the
      correlator is written.
- [ ] `CNF-278`, `CNF-342`, `CNF-34` and `CNF-166` carry the cases in item 8.
- [ ] Every live reference to an `OPS-43` step number names the step it meant. Grep for "step 2",
      "step-2", "step 5" and "step-5" next to `OPS-43`; `OPS-23`'s pointer and `CNF-241`'s note are
      known sites. Dated amendment notes keep their history.
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`, run unpiped, exits 0. A formalized clause
      that changes moves with its Lean declaration, and no theorem is weakened to pass.

**Out of scope:**
- The classification of a failed List offers read (`pv-qga`, which depends on this bead).
- Where admission gets its offer data, and how fresh it must be (`pv-tcs`).
- The `retryable` value of `price_moved` and of the step-1 and `API-63` account failures
  (`pv-xer`). State none for them here. Don't copy `WIR-9a`'s purchase-tail values either: they
  apply to an account "whose collection-snapshot `STO-47` status" is read at admission.

title: STO-54 can read promoting either standby on a tie as a restore, so an idle-system failover bumps every credential generation (STO-54, CNF-365)
description:
> *Filed 2026-10-23 from PR #23 review comment 4362842085 (reply 4363346364), on a read of master `b90783d`. Owner,
> 2026-10-23: "Follow-up ticket (Recommended)".*

`STO-54` (`05-persistence.md:1501-1513`) makes a promotion a restart when "the one further ahead is promoted", and
classes "Any other promotion — … or of the one not further ahead, …" as a restore. When both standbys report the same
end of WAL, as on an idle system, neither is further ahead, so the text can be read to class promoting either one as a
restore. The same sentence's reasoning, "both hold a prefix of one WAL sequence, so that one holds them all", covers a
tie.

Read as a restore, an ordinary failover runs the restore procedure, where "every tenant's credential generation is
bumped" (`05-persistence.md:1550`), so every spending token dies.

The promotion paragraph is pv-s4m's chosen form, which PR #23 landed, so the tie was left to this bead rather than
reworded there. Its fix wording gets a reading round in the PR that lands it.

Owners: `STO-54`, `CNF-365`.

title: No conformance item asserts tenant_suspended on the create that API-58 step 4 fails (API-58, WIR-9a)
description:
> *This was generated by AI while preparing the `pv-uuv` Run (branch `pv-uuv`), 2026-10-21.*

`WIR-9a`'s `conflict` union lists `"tenant_suspended"` (`API-58`), and no conformance item asserts
that reason where `API-58` records it, so a build that stamps a different reason (or none) on a
suspension-failed create passes conformance.

- `API-58` step 4 "transitions the tenant's own work — `requested_by: caller`, never a system
  cancellation — that is already `queued` but never claimed straight to `failed`, carrying the
  reason in the operation's `error`", with `conflict` and `details.reason: "tenant_suspended"`.
- That reason is recorded on an operation, never sent as a `409`, so `pv-uuv` takes it out of
  `CNF-248`'s driven set and points at its owner instead.
- The items that cite `API-58` (`CNF-113`, `CNF-194`, `CNF-202`, `CNF-218`, `CNF-244`, `CNF-253`,
  `CNF-299`, `CNF-312`, `CNF-272`, `CNF-362`) were grepped on master `3f14280`: `CNF-312` and

title: OPS-22's zero-row exit ends the worker in OPS-22 and STO-3 but the whole engine in ADR-0022 and CNF-290 (OPS-22, STO-3, CNF-290)
description:
Found by panel r65 on a read of master `b90783d`, while weighing pv-buc's forms.

When a worker's guarded settled-state write affects no row, the spec disagrees on what exits.

The engine reading:
- `ADR-0022` (lines 40-41): "B's settle then affects zero rows and the engine exits under `OPS-22`".
- `CNF-290` (10-conformance-checklist.md:1505): "the old process's late settled-state write affects **no row**
  and exits it". "It" is the old process.

The worker reading:
- `OPS-22` (03-operation-lifecycle.md:1825-1828): "the worker MUST log it loudly, saying what it observed rather
  than asserting a restart, leave the record alone, and exit".
- `STO-3` (05-persistence.md:33-35): "A write that affects no row means something other than this execution
  moved the operation — the startup pass after a restart, or a later claim after a defer — and the worker
  exits (`OPS-22`)".
- The worker algorithm (03-operation-lifecycle.md:1730-1732): "so the worker stops there".

Under the engine reading, one zero-row write stops every other worker in the process and strands their
`running` rows until the next startup pass. Under the worker reading only that worker exits. Decide which is
meant, and make `OPS-22`, `STO-3`, `ADR-0022` and `CNF-290` say the same.
close_reason: **Close as superseded by the generation-fence amendment.** `CNF-290` now says the old write “commits nothing and exits it (`OPS-50`)”, followed by the engine-exit quote. `OPS-22` separately states: “A write that `OPS-50`'s generation check refuses is not a zero-row write: the engine exits at once”. Its genuine zero-row path still names the worker. The remaining engine-exit sentence in `ADR-0022` is in the historical bad-guard scenario; changing that narrative alone does not justify another bead.

title: API-13's disk-identifier row sets no length cap, though SEC-29 caps individual fields per API-13 (SEC-29, API-13)
description:
Found during the `pv-6p8` drain review (branch `pv-6p8`), 2026-10-22.

**The problem.** `SEC-29` says "Request bodies MUST be size-capped globally, and individual fields MUST be capped per `API-13`." `pv-6p8` added an `API-13` row for disk identifiers, `target.identifier` and `layout.drives[].identifier`: "a JSON string, non-empty after normalization (`RSC-46`)". It sets no length cap. The panel's reviewed form set none either.

Every other caller string in `API-13`'s table has one: hostname "1–253 characters", offer identifier "1–256 characters", catalog image "1–256 characters". So a single disk identifier can fill the global body cap ("2 MiB is a reasonable default"). It is then stored in the operation's request and compared in the worker.

**Example.** A caller sends a 1.9 MiB `target.identifier`. Engine A refuses it, reading `SEC-29` as requiring a per-field cap. Engine B admits it, because `API-13` states none, and repeats the comparison in the worker (`OPS-23`). Both conform to `API-13` as written.

**Question.** What is the disk identifier's length cap in `API-13`, if any? Should `SEC-29` say that a row without a cap is capped only by the body cap?

title: DOM-9's offer has no field for an offer-reported cancellation bound (PRV-44, PRV-31)
description:
`PRV-44` says the descriptor's `cancellation_bound` "MAY be reported on the offer instead", and the
`request_summary` row resolves the snapshot bound "taking the later of the descriptor's `cancellation_bound`
and the offer-reported bound where both exist". But `DOM-9`'s offer table has no field that carries an
offer-reported cancellation bound. Its fields include `traffic_bound`, but no cancellation bound. So a driver
that reports the bound on the offer, as `PRV-44` permits, has nowhere to put it. Admission's "later of" read,
and `pv-hsm`'s claim-time re-test, have no offer-side input to read. The launch Robot driver declares its bound
in the descriptor and is unaffected.

Decide whether `DOM-9`'s offer gains the field (and, if so, its wire disclosure under `WIR-30`), or whether
`PRV-44`'s "on the offer instead" option is withdrawn for the cancellation bound.

Found by panel r54 (opus), docs/research/panels-2026-10/r54/. Requirement text and conformance only.

title: Migration admission refusal has no defined outcome
description:
When deployment admission is exhausted before a migrator or waiting migration runner can connect, the migration's refusal behavior is unspecified. The deployment cannot tell from the requirements whether that entry point exits, waits, or retries, what bounds apply, or how it reports that the release cannot advance. This affects release progress and failure handling.

Verified on master bf82bfe93715ca120a08e73fb0cca20e4f47fce8. STO-55 says "Every physical connection attempt by component pools, reconnects, rollout incarnations, startup-lock holders, migrators and waiting runners MUST receive a distinct durable reservation before dialing from one serialized authority outside the protected store." Its refusal cases say "Startup acquisition refusal exits for supervisor retry; `api` returns `overloaded` before any transaction; worker/periodic acquisition refusal is an `OPS-49` store error". They do not name migration acquisition refusal separately.

STO-13 says "Migrations MUST be forward-only and MUST be applied by the deployable's own `migrate` entry point, run by the deployment **before any component of a release starts and while the previous release's engine and `api` keep running** — never by `api`, and never by the engine at boot, whose restart window `ADR-0016` priced at seconds and `OVR-18` alarms." That places migration before release startup, rather than making it the component startup case. OPS-49 limits its retry rule to "Where a store call by a worker, or by a periodic component running in the engine process (`OVR-17`), errors or times out"; its admission clause says "An attempt denied by `STO-55` admission is a store error for this loop and sends no SQL".

Source: PR #32 summary, https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond/pull/32#issuecomment-6474225495. Review evidence: pr32-*.json under /var/tmp/rloop-units/provisiond-spec-pv-3jw6-1028T162500/. Owners to consult: STO-55, STO-13, OPS-49. This record leaves the refusal policy undecided.

title: CNF-55's and CNF-364's claim-time refusals do not assert the resource-offer exclusion freed (CNF-55, CNF-364, OPS-43, STO-58)
description:
> *Filed 2026-10-22 while judging panel B (pv-7j3, pv-p3k, pv-009, pv-gpw, pv-ss4), from a full read of the set at `1bdf453`.*

Two claim-time refusals don't assert that the create's resource-offer exclusion is freed, unlike the sibling cases that settle the same way. `CNF-55` covers the `OPS-43` step-3 refusal with `allow_orders` turned off; `CNF-364` covers the step-4 `list_offers` gate.

- `OPS-43` (`03:801`): "Where the create holds a resource-offer exclusion, settlement frees it (`STO-58`: "Its lifetime follows the winning create's outcome settlement" …)". `OPS-11`'s create row repeats this for any create failure recorded before step 9.

title: STO-54 says nothing about a crash inside the restore procedure; a plain restart after one is the naive boot
description: Found while modelling pv-vwe.11 (Provisiond.Restore). STO-54 orders steps (1)-(3) and OPS-15 quarantines the irreversible queued kinds 'on a restore', but nothing in the set says how the engine knows a store is restored. If the process dies after the restore lands and before step (2)'s pass commits, the successor comes up under STO-5's restart rule on the restored store: OPS-15 inspects running rows only, the executed create is claimed again, and every destructive witness ADR-0023 lists fires. The model refuses to carry a crash as a recovery event for this reason (see the module docstring's omissions). Candidate fix: the restore procedure writes a durable 'restore in progress' row before the startup lock, and OPS-15's pass branches on that row rather than on the operator's knowledge; the row is cleared when step (3) completes. Decide the owner (STO-54 vs OPS-15) and land the sentence, then extend Provisiond.Restore with a crash event and prove the theorems survive it.
close_reason: Rule landed on STO-54 with STO-56's record; Provisiond.Restore carries the crash; gates green

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Specification-ambiguity analysis from a Manager-seat test of gpt-6-astra (2026-09-20, not a real rloop Run — rloop cannot drive a codex Manager today). It picked this ticket off the ready frontier in id order, ran the gates, and blocked rather than choosing a reading, which is what RUN-19 asks for.

The two readings it names:
1. The latest process event determines the boot mode. After the restore lands, the recovery process dies before quarantine commits; its successor is an ordinary restart on the same committed store, so a create restored to queued can be claimed again even if the provider already executed it, and a suspension parent resumes with no operator.
2. The unfinished recovery incident determines the boot mode. A crash does not end the restore incident; successors keep its restrictions until the recovery work is finished. This needs a durable 'restore in progress' distinction the text does not provide.

Passages it cites: STO-5 (05-persistence.md:70) 'A restore from backup is not a restart and is not covered by this sentence'; STO-54's step (2) and its freeze-lift clause (05-persistence.md:1144); OPS-15's restore branch and its 'on a restart; after a restore it waits' suspension exception (03-operation-lifecycle.md:315); and Restore.lean's own omission note, which already points here.

Its recommendation: adopt reading 2 explicitly, with STO-54 owning the incident's lifetime and crash-survival obligations and OPS-15 citing that owner; require the unfinished incident to be durably recognizable before any restored component starts; and say how a repeated step avoids moving the restore instant or repeating credential generation and derivation-index changes. ADR-0023 explains the naive-boot danger but does not settle the interrupted-procedure boundary.

This is the owner's call, not an implementer's: it changes what the system is allowed to do.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Landed 2026-09-20. Owner: STO-54, per reading 2 of the comment above. STO-56 is the new artifact — `restore_incidents` (`restore_instant`, `steps_completed`, `closed_at`), one open row at a time, written into the restored store before either component starts and closed by the operator. OPS-15 cites STO-54's sentence for its branch instead of carrying a copy; the worker algorithm's startup block reads the record and passes it to the pass.

Departure from this ticket's candidate fix, which said the row 'is cleared when step (3) completes': it is not. Two obligations outlive step (3) — OPS-32's second pass and the operator confirming every waiting parent — and clearing at (3) hands both to a successor that no longer knows it is in an incident. The record instead carries a per-step mark, and the operator closes it when the last obligation is discharged. The marks also answer astra's third point: a marked step does not run again, so the grace is written once, the generation bumped once and the derivation index skipped once; only a step interrupted before its mark repeats, and that repeat is safe on each of its writes (the instant comes from the record, the quarantine is guarded on (id, status = queued), step (3)'s two writes only rise).

The marks were not in the first draft. A two-axis review found what the instant-only record costs: repeating a completed step (1) backdates an `exhausted_since` that a later re-derivation had set, burning the interval LDG-16 exists to give, and pauses the listener a second time for a customer already served. ADR-0023 carries that as the reason the record is not a single bit.

Formal: Provisiond.Restore gains Store.record, Event.crash, afterCrash/faultAfterCrash and the recordDecidesBoot parameter; all five restore theorems now quantify over runs containing crashes, and restart_never_reorders gained the hypothesis that the record is closed — that hypothesis is the finding. Witnesses: crash_inside_procedure_continues_it (the successor keeps the restore mode and serves nothing), crash_inside_procedure_is_the_naive_boot (with the parameter off, the executed create is ordered twice), marked_step_does_not_repeat. ci.yml gains the control row, 37 -> 38; all five Restore controls verified locally, one targeted red each. check-all.sh green unpiped.

title: The citation gate never compares a straight-quoted value nested in a straight-quoted citation (tools/check_citations.py, DEF-16)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during the `pv-oes` drain (branch `pv-oes`), 2026-10-21. The class was first seen while landing PR #16 (`pv-uuv`), whose `CNF-248` quotes moved to curly outer marks to get compared.*

`tools/check_citations.py` pairs straight double marks left to right. In a straight-quoted citation that itself contains a straight-quoted value, the outer quotation closes at the first inner mark, so the nested value is never compared with the owner, and a misspelt reason name there stays green. How much else goes unchecked depends on the form:
- **Possessive form** (`` `X`'s "…" ``): nothing in the quotation is compared.
- **`says` form**: the fragments between the inner marks are still compared, but the nested values aren't.
- A probe on `pv-oes` confirms both: in the `says` form, a planted `account_terminatd` exits 0 and a planted `three recoverable` exits 1.

- The gate's docstring names the class: "What it cannot see: balanced nested or mispaired straight/curly marks can still select the wrong span within a paragraph."
- Its quote-content fixtures (`check_quote_content`) wrap each quote in curly outer marks (`` `OPS-41` says “…” ``), so straight inside curly is tested. No self-test fixture nests straight marks inside straight ones.
- The one site at master `ad40707` was `03-operation-lifecycle.md`'s `OPS-43` step 1, quoting `API-63` with `details.reason: "account_terminated"` and `"state"` inside. There, planting `account_terminatd` exited 0.
- Method: a non-historical, attributed chunk whose paired straight span holds an odd number of backticks, so it ended inside a code span.
- PR #17 (`pv-oes`) switched that site's outer marks to curly “…”, as `CNF-248` (PR #16) and `05-persistence.md` already do. The count is now zero. The `account_terminatd` plant there exits 1, and so do a `"stat"` plant and a `three recoverable` plant.
- The same scan's looser shape, two straight spans joined by a short token, finds two hits, and neither is a citation: `04-api-contract.md` (`API-63`'s own text) and `13-wire-contract.md` (a JSON fixture).

So the curly workaround holds only while every author knows to use it; nothing fails when one doesn't.

Fix asked for: teach the gate to compare those values, so authors stop needing the curly workaround. For example, pair straight marks around inline code spans, so a straight-quoted value inside one is compared as content. Every nested value at the one site sat in a code span.

Question for triage: is pairing around code spans the right rule? The cheaper alternative is to fail an attributed straight span that ends inside a code span, naming the curly-mark fix in the message. That would enforce the workaround rather than remove it.

Acceptance:
- a self-test fixture where a typo in a nested straight-quoted value goes red;
- a `ci.yml` negative-control step for it (`DEF-16`);
- the docstring's "What it cannot see" paragraph updated;
- the gates exit 0 unpiped.

title: No gate parses inline JSON examples, so WIR-10b's rescue_inventory example and its identifier rule are unchecked (WIR-37, WIR-10b, RSC-46)
description:
Found during the `pv-6p8` drain review (branch `pv-6p8`), 2026-10-22. This is the reviewed form's out-of-scope bullet "No reader proposed a gate that cross-checks the inline example".

**The problem.** `WIR-37` says "every JSON example in this document parses under `WIR-1a` with real-shaped values — full UUIDs, `Z`-suffixed timestamps, 64-hex digests — so the examples are test inputs, not illustrations". `tools/check_fixtures.py` reads fenced ```json blocks only. JSON written inline in backtick spans, such as `WIR-10b`'s `result` examples, is never parsed by any gate.

`WIR-10b`'s `rescue_inventory` example now encodes `RSC-46`'s identifier rule: `identifier` is `wwn`, else `serial`, else `null`, plus a device with all three `null`. In panel r61 the readers planted three bad examples, and every gate passed each one:
- `/dev/sda` in place of `null`;
- an `identifier` not equal to its `serial`;
- a `null` `identifier` beside a present serial.

The drain checked the example only with a throwaway script outside the repository.

**Example.** A later edit swaps the example's `identifier` back to the serial while keeping a WWN. All gates stay green, and a client that copies the example gets the preference rule wrong.

**Question.** Should the fixtures gate also parse inline JSON examples (at least `WIR-10b`'s), and should one check assert `RSC-46`'s identifier rule on `WIR-10b`'s inventory example, with a negative control in `ci.yml`?

Verification evidence under /var/tmp/rloop-units/provisiond-spec-pv-6350-1028T015300/: manager-round6-before-check-all.log (unpiped, exit 0), manager-round6-focused.log (exit 0), manager-round6-flake-build.log (exit 0), manager-round6-publication.log (failure/success paths verified), and manager-round6-ci-control.log (child exits 0/1/0, intended rejection and restored bytes). No specification source changed.

title: Rescue inventory has no wire form for a device with no unique identifier (WIR-10b, WIR-40, RSC-26)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during the bot review of PR #15 (`pv-pj0`), 2026-10-21: codex P2 on round 2 (tip 78b49de), review comment 4335098584, https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond/pull/15#discussion_r4335098584. Replied and resolved on the PR; not fixed there because the gap predates PR #15 and needs a wire-contract decision.*

`WIR-40` says rescue inventory returns "the device inventory with **stable identifiers**", and `WIR-10b`'s
`rescue_inventory` result shows every device with a string `identifier`. But `RSC-26` (unchanged since before
PR #15, base 80c8b42) says "duplicate or empty serials are real on consumer and virtualised disks", and
`01-domain-model.md` gates rescue inventory on the account capability alone:
"| rescue inventory | `rescue_ssh` (`RSC-38` boots rescue to read the inventory) |". So a machine whose
device exposes neither a serial nor a WWN can reach `rescue-inventory`, and no conforming response exists:
omitting the field, returning null, or inventing an unstable value each break the current wire contract.
PR #15 (pv-pj0) made the case explicit: an offer with no per-device unique identifier stays sellable without
`raw_disk` and `rootfs_via_rescue`, and `RSC-26` now says such a machine "meets the abort this paragraph
opens with".

Question for triage: which representation?
1. `identifier: null` for that device (the install side already aborts `integrity` on zero matches);
2. omit the device from `devices` (the fingerprint still covers the whole set?);
3. refuse `rescue-inventory` on such a machine (needs a static signal, since inventory is the only reader).

Acceptance: `WIR-10b`/`WIR-40` define the chosen form, `RSC-33`/`RSC-38` agree, and one CNF item asserts it.

title: Cover survived-stop failure before the cancellation fence
description:
Found while applying pv-9j6. Recheck the required pre-fence cancellation route and its coverage.

`OPS-21` says "A cancellation of `execute` that the engine survives MUST be recorded before the engine exits, for every operation kind" and "A stop that arrives while a store transaction inside `execute` is in flight or repeating under `OPS-49`, such as `OPS-43`'s step-8 transaction or an `OPS-45` marker write, is the cancellation being recorded." A stop can arrive before the cancellation's first fence transaction is sent, or during one the store refuses, while `execute` is cancellable. With the store working before the Stop-record bound ends, the record can land with neither fence nor write-started marker set.

`OPS-11`'s last row now says "any failure the worker records while `OPS-45`'s write-started marker is unset" and "MUST settle `failed`, whatever its kind". The cancellation is unaccepted and has no rescue session; its cut-off failure therefore settles `failed` without an operator. `OPS-48`'s row for "`failed` — deterministic; the provider did not act" gives `stalled` with the fence "**Unchanged**". This supplies a stalled/null-fence prefix without a crash or operator resolution.

`CNF-312` still says "it orders no such failure before this fence write" and "Therefore drive route 1 alone." `ADR-0032` says "no current clause orders a worker-recorded failure before the fence write". `OPS-41`'s verification note calls pre-fence failure "an over-approximation, not a specified injection point"; the fence verification passages still say "no current ordering clause establishes that injection point". Reconcile these passages with the survived-stop requirement and add a real survived-stop/null-fence prefix to the conformance coverage if confirmed. Keep the existing crash prefix as its own case. Those passages were outside pv-9j6's allowed edits.

description:

Authority: ADR-0025 ("a negative theorem for every guard a dated amendment added"; a formalized clause keeps its requirement identifier; a theorem is never a conformance item; no CNF identifiers in Lean) and the admission test in pv-vwe's 2026-09-21 comment (composition with an existing state transition or an authoritative rendered table). Panel: docs/research/panels-2026-10/r47/synthesis.md (owner decision Q30, 2026-10-13: write it). Every new guard is a named field of the model's parameter record with a witness pair (refused with the guard, admitted without it) and one negative-control row in .github/workflows/ci.yml that flips it and reds exactly that witness. Do not weaken any existing theorem statement (AGENTS.md); keep rendered regions in step (tools/check_regions.py). No requirement text changes except where a docstring quote must follow its source.

`Fence.ofReply` carries OPS-48's first column and maps a successful reply to gone/succeeded; nothing in `Fence.lean` produces `Settled.scheduled`, so no Fence trace reaches the rendered scheduled row of `Tables.episodeStep`. v1 sells only Robot, whose every delete is a dated cancellation followed by one read-back (PRV-13): the provider's mapped not-found records the machine gone at that read; "Read failure does not turn the accepted dated cancellation into `needs_reconciliation` or establish absence" — a failed or still-present read settles `succeeded` as `cancellation_scheduled`, fence kept, the sweep's gone-write closing it later (ADR-0037 Q21's repair: the scheduled row closes at the gone-write, not a tombstone).

Model the dated acceptance and the read-back's three answers (not-found, present, failed) and compose them with the existing episode transition. Witness pairs: dated acceptance + failed read-back → `scheduled`, fence unchanged, with the guard; without it (ADR-0037's rejected "`now` is immediate" constant) → gone-write, fence cleared, machine present. Dated acceptance + mapped not-found → closed `resource_gone` at the read; with the read-back skipped → scheduled. This is outcome coverage, not a metering proof; say what stays outside (the meter's stop instant is `LDG-38`'s, proved in Funding).

title: WIR-48's refusal of a confirmed-terminated account names no conflict reason (WIR-48, WIR-9a, API-63)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during the two-axis review of `pv-uuv` (branch `pv-uuv`), 2026-10-21. First raised by the `pv-uuv` Run as a follow-up comment on `pv-uuv`.*

`WIR-48`'s refusal of an assignment to a confirmed-terminated account is a mandated `409` with no
named reason, so two conforming engines can send different reasons for the same refusal.

- `WIR-48` says "naming one not flagged assignable is `conflict` with `details.reason: "state"`" and,
  in the next sentence, "Assigning a tenant to an account that `SEC-46` has recorded as
  confirmed-terminated is also `conflict`", with no reason.
- `WIR-9a`'s `conflict` row requires a `reason` from its closed union, so the response must carry one.
  Two readings: `state` (continuing the preceding clause), or `account_terminated` (`API-63`'s reason
  for a terminated account).
- `CNF-248` stays meetable either way, but under the second reading `account_terminated` becomes a
  `409` reason as well as a recorded one, and `CNF-248` (which `pv-uuv` made exclude it) would then
  not drive that `409`.

Question for triage: which reason does `WIR-48`'s confirmed-terminated refusal carry? If
`account_terminated`, `CNF-248`'s exclusion of it needs revisiting. (`WIR-48`, `WIR-9a`, `API-63`,
`SEC-46`, `CNF-248`)

title: With passEveryStartup off the startup-pass witness never claims, so it cannot show a row left running while other work proceeds (OPS-15)
description:
Check strength. `Provisiond.Witnesses.successor_strands_power_without_pass` (`Witnesses.lean:1427`) refutes
`Provisiond.Restore.successor_sweeps_running` with `passEveryStartup` off. It shows the power operation claimed
after step (2) still `running` after the crash, lock and startup pass, with `passDone = false`.

It cannot show the harm `OPS-15` guards against: a row left `running` while other work proceeds. With the guard
off, `step`'s `.startupPass` (`Restore.lean:442`) skips the pass once step (2)'s mark is set, so `passDone` stays
false. `permits.claim` requires `passDone`, so the engine never claims again. In the model, skipping the pass also
stops every claim; a spec change that skipped the pass but still let claims through would not be refuted.

Question for triage: should the witness, or a second one, separate the pass from the claim permit, so that a
skipped pass is refuted by a trace where other work is claimed while the stranded row stays `running`?

Found in the review of panel C's change (`pv-n98`, `OPS-15`). The witness is new on this branch; the spec text is
not affected.

comments.text:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug. **Readiness:** ready to apply the adopted M-I package as written.

**Owner answer, verbatim (2026-10-28):**

> Add M-I (Recommended)

**Landing sites:** independent formal test model and named witnesses under `tools/formal/Provisiond/`, the independent negative-control step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and a bare witness pointer beside `OPS-15` in `03-operation-lifecycle.md`. Follow `ADR-0025`; keep conformance identifiers out of formal sources.

**Exact adopted package (verbatim from the reviewed brief):**

### Complete package M-I: retain the existing model and add an independent countermodel

Leave Restore.Params/current, permits, step, run, successor_sweeps_running and every existing witness unchanged. Add the printed permitsI, stepI, runI as a second formal test model alongside new named witnesses; give requirePass the explicit documentation:

> Global guard for OPS-15's before-any-claim requirement. True is the current policy; false permits claims after lock and the restore step-(2) mark without requiring the per-process pass. It contains no condition on a selected operation, desired stranded status, or desired result.

Use `I_required_step_eq` to establish equality with the original step for every state/event when requirePass=true. Keep its claim branch otherwise identical to Restore.step, including the lock, queued status, step-(2) and parent-exception checks. Add named witnesses for all four combinations of passEveryStartup and requirePass using the exact progressTrace printed above: true/true sweeps and progresses; false/true strands and blocks fresh claim; true/false sweeps and progresses on this trace; false/false strands old rows while a fresh claim applies. The false/false case is openly a two-guard negative engine, not evidence that the original one-field mutant already permits progress. Add an independent CI negative-control step that proves flipping requirePass back to true rejects the bad-model later-work assertion, and flipping passEveryStartup back to true rejects its stranded-row assertion. Keep the existing passEveryStartup control intact. Add a bare pointer beside OPS-15 to the independent witnesses, without changing normative prose. Expose the distinction in comments; no extra target-row predicate may gate claims or become a theorem premise.

This form adds a second model and a second global control. It offers independence at the cost of duplicated claim logic and only reaches the composite harm with both guards off. Decide whether that is an honest independent countermodel or unnecessary apparatus, rather than calling it a one-guard refutation.

**Shared code and trace (verbatim review input):** The M-I package selects only the I definitions and equivalence proof. S definitions/examples below are comparison context from the common review input; M-S is not adopted.

### Exact code and trace shared by the alternatives

`check/probe-models.lean`, printed completely below, supplies separate candidate transition functions and concrete pairs. It is scratch evidence, not a change to master. The final scratch compile must exit 0 before launch; its receipt is check/probe-models.{log,exit}. The all-event equality proof was repaired by simplifying after the Fault case split; its statement and both candidate transition functions are unchanged. It uses the existing fixtures and one trace: complete the procedure, admit/claim/apply create 4, claim power 3, crash, lock, attempt startup handling, admit/claim/apply fresh create 5. The bad outcome requires BOTH create 4 and power 3 still running while create 5 is running with applied true. This shows actual later model work, not merely a true permission bit. Good-model rows 4 and 3 must instead reconcile while row 5 still runs/applies. The baseline blocked-claim cell must remain reported, not relabelled as the harm we seek.

```lean
import Provisiond.Witnesses

namespace Provisiond.Explore
open Provisiond.Restore Provisiond.Witnesses

-- S: startup handling completes even when the mutant skips the sweep.
def stepS (p : Params) (w : World) : Event → World
  | .startupPass =>
    if w.locked && !w.passDone then
      if p.passEveryStartup || !w.stepTwoMarked then
        { w with passDone := true, stepTwoMarked := true,
                 store := { w.store with ops := fun j =>
                   let o := w.store.ops j
                   if o.status = .running || !w.stepTwoMarked then passOp p w o else o } }
      else { w with passDone := true }
    else w
  | e => Restore.step p w e

def runS (p : Params) (w : World) (es : List Event) : World := es.foldl (stepS p) w

-- I: independent claim-before-pass guard, tested in all four combinations.
def permitsI (requirePass : Bool) (p : Params) (w : World) : Permissions :=
  { Restore.permits p w with
    claim := w.locked && (!requirePass || w.passDone) &&
      (!w.fault.isRestore || w.stepTwoMarked) }

def stepI (requirePass : Bool) (p : Params) (w : World) : Event → World
  | .claim i =>
    let o := w.store.ops i
    let perm := permitsI requirePass p w
    if perm.claim && o.status = .queued
        && (o.kind ≠ .suspendTenant || perm.run .suspendTenantException) then
      { w with store := w.store.modify i fun o => { o with status := .running },
               secondOrder := w.secondOrder || (irreversible o.kind && o.applied),
               parentResumedUnconfirmed := w.parentResumedUnconfirmed
                 || (o.kind = .suspendTenant && w.fault.isRestore && !w.parentsConfirmed) }
    else w
  | e => Restore.step p w e

def runI (requirePass : Bool) (p : Params) (w : World) (es : List Event) : World :=
  es.foldl (stepI requirePass p) w

def progressTrace : List Event :=
  procedure ++ [.admit ⟨4⟩, .claim ⟨4⟩, .apply ⟨4⟩, .claim ⟨3⟩,
    .crash, .lock, .startupPass, .admit ⟨5⟩, .claim ⟨5⟩, .apply ⟨5⟩]

def initial : World := bootRestore freshWorkTrace
def skipped : Params := { restoredWorkParams with passEveryStartup := false }

example :
    let w := Restore.run skipped initial progressTrace
    (w.store.ops ⟨4⟩).status = .running ∧
    (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).status = .queued ∧
    (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).applied = false ∧ w.passDone = false := by decide

example :
    let w := runS skipped initial progressTrace
    (w.store.ops ⟨4⟩).status = .running ∧ (w.store.ops ⟨4⟩).applied = true ∧
    (w.store.ops ⟨3⟩).status = .running ∧
    (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).status = .running ∧ (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).applied = true ∧
    w.passDone = true := by decide

example :
    let w := runS restoredWorkParams initial progressTrace
    (w.store.ops ⟨4⟩).status = .needsReconciliation ∧
    (w.store.ops ⟨3⟩).status = .needsReconciliation ∧
    (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).status = .running ∧ (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).applied = true := by decide

example :
    let w := runI false skipped initial progressTrace
    (w.store.ops ⟨4⟩).status = .running ∧ (w.store.ops ⟨4⟩).applied = true ∧
    (w.store.ops ⟨3⟩).status = .running ∧
    (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).status = .running ∧ (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).applied = true ∧
    w.passDone = false := by decide

example :
    let w := runI true skipped initial progressTrace
    (w.store.ops ⟨4⟩).status = .running ∧
    (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).status = .queued ∧ (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).applied = false := by decide

example :
    let w := runI false restoredWorkParams initial progressTrace
    (w.store.ops ⟨4⟩).status = .needsReconciliation ∧
    (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).status = .running ∧ (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).applied = true := by decide

example :
    let w := runI true restoredWorkParams initial progressTrace
    (w.store.ops ⟨4⟩).status = .needsReconciliation ∧
    (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).status = .running ∧ (w.store.ops ⟨5⟩).applied = true := by decide

-- This is all-state equality for the valid guard, not just a single trace.
theorem S_current_step_eq (p : Params) (hp : p.passEveryStartup = true)
    (w : World) (e : Event) : stepS p w e = Restore.step p w e := by
  cases e <;> simp [stepS, Restore.step, hp]

theorem I_required_step_eq (p : Params) (w : World) (e : Event) :
    stepI true p w e = Restore.step p w e := by
  cases e <;> simp [stepI, permitsI, Restore.step, Restore.permits]
  all_goals cases w.fault <;> simp

end Provisiond.Explore
```

title: OPS-45's second marker: 'null where begin rescue was never dispatched' is false between the arming write and the dispatch
description: Found while modelling pv-vwe.7 (Provisiond.Rescue). OPS-45 defines rescue_exited_cleanly three-valued: 'null where begin rescue was never dispatched; false, written before begin rescue (PRV-15) is dispatched'. The two clauses cannot both be read as definitions: a process that dies after the arming write commits and before the dispatch leaves false with no session opened, so null is not equivalent to 'never dispatched'. The model proves the safe direction only, which is the sentence the same paragraph ends on -- 'Null is the only value that means no session was opened' (Provisiond.Rescue.Install.none_means_no_session) -- and records the gap in the module docstring's omissions. This is the same conservatism the first marker carries, and OPS-45 stated it there in the 2026-09-15 rewording: the marker 'establishes that preservation is no longer proven, not that a byte landed', and 'a process that dies between the write and the phase leaves a set marker over an untouched disk'. Candidate fix: reword the null clause the way the first marker's was, so the column's meaning is stated as what it forecloses rather than as a biconditional -- null means no session is known to have been opened, and the pre-dispatch false is the conservative case. No behaviour changes; the classifier already reads false as not-clean. Decide whether OPS-45 or 05-persistence.md's rescue_exited_cleanly row carries the wording (OPS-45 owns the rule) and land it.

title: allow_orders' scope is never defined: 'bill per order', 'bills on order', 'order-billed', 'per ordering account' (DOM-16, PRV-10, API-15)
description:
> *Filed 2026-10-22 while judging panel B (pv-7j3, pv-p3k, pv-009, pv-gpw, pv-ss4), from a full read of the set at `1bdf453`.*

Which accounts does `allow_orders` govern? Four texts name the scope four ways and none defines it. Since pv-p3k made `DOM-16` a MUST, the answer decides a listing and a create outcome.

- `DOM-16` (`01:570`): "Ordering capabilities (`provision_virtual`, `provision_bare_metal`) for providers that bill per order MUST be conditional on an explicit per-account `allow_orders` configuration flag: the descriptor (`PRV-44`) of an account whose flag is false does not declare them".
- `PRV-10` (`02:160`): "For a provider that bills on order, create MUST reject the request unless …".
- `API-15` (`04:986`): "A create request against an order-billed provider MUST carry an explicit purchase acknowledgement".
- `00-overview.md:396`: "`allow_orders`, per ordering account".
- `08-provider-notes.md`'s matrix marks Cloud VPS Create "yes" and only the dedicated columns "opt-in ordering", but that table "is not read by anything".

Two engines, each able to cite the text, given a Hetzner Cloud or DigitalOcean account (hourly-billed virtual machines) configured with `allow_orders: false`:
- **Engine A** reads it as order-billed. It withholds `provision_virtual`, `GET /v1/providers` omits it, and a create fails `501 unsupported` at `API-7` step 5d.
- **Engine B** reads it as not order-billed. It declares `provision_virtual`, and the create is admitted. Withholding it would breach `DOM-15`, whose new exception covers only "An ordering capability withheld under `DOM-16`".

Question for triage: is "bills per order" a property of the provider, of the account, or of the offer, and which v1 drivers does it cover? Owners: `DOM-16`, `PRV-10`, `API-15`.
