title: A queued paused-grace deferral can delay a later outage bound or suspension
description:
Found by Sol and confirmed by the Manager during Round 1 of pv-gip.29, landing ad6e2d9.

OPS-41 (03-operation-lifecycle.md:752-755) mandates `available_at` equal to "now + (one re-derivation interval − accumulated rate-present time)". OPS-6 says "The claim MUST select the oldest `queued` operation whose availability time has passed." OPS-39 says "a sweep MUST enqueue nothing against a machine whose episode under that key is open". LDG-64 says "cancel machines at that bound" if no rate has returned. OPS-41 says the current suspension and bound "retain the original wall-clock grace only".

Trace: the original wall-clock end has passed; a return and claim at 100 compute paused end 160 and queue the attempt until then. A new outage starts at 101, with bound 110. The existing attempt cannot claim at 110 and the bound cannot enqueue a second attempt for that episode. A suspension joining after the claim similarly cannot act before 160. Nothing currently advances availability on these events. The Lean Claim model explicitly omits the reader of available_at, so its theorem about a claim at the bound does not establish that the queue permits that claim.

Owner clarification required: retain the specified deferral instant and accept that later bound/suspension actions wait for it, or require those later actions to supersede a queued paused-grace deferral? The original work order mandates the deferral instant and the exception, while the brief excludes redesigning wake-ups; selecting an exception changes the specifications. Recommend preserving the bound/current-suspension exception, with an explicit rule making already-deferred attempts eligible when it applies. Do not pick a wake-up implementation before the behavior is decided.

Acceptance: decide this composition in the normative owners and ADR, and add a queue-eligibility-aware conformance trace for both a new outage/bound and current suspension after available_at was set. A test that manually claims a not-yet-available attempt does not cover the defect.

Full gates and every final workflow negative control passed. Evidence: /var/tmp/provisiond-implementation-report.md. pv-gip.37 remains open.

The pv-gip.29 work order's 'available_at = the paused end' contradicted that and was the caller's error. The paused deferral becomes OPS-8's short delay inside step 3, so every later claim re-decides from step 1 and a suspension or a bound is reached on time. Evidence is the requirement and a CNF trace; the formal claim does not model available_at. Work order: /var/tmp/provisiond-gates/gip29-residue.md.

title: Bound-based restore closure can discard grace for a still-queued funding cancellation
description:
Found by Sol and confirmed by the Manager during Round 1 of pv-gip.29, landing ad6e2d9.

STO-56 (05-persistence.md:1141-1148) permits closure when, for each currency, "either its accumulated rate-present time since step (3) has reached one re-derivation interval (`OPS-41`) or its outage has reached `LDG-64`'s bound" and asserts "no funding cancellation remains to protect past that bound". OPS-41 says "With no open restore record there is no restore-grace deferral." Its ordered worker decision applies the ordinary predicate when a rate exists. The owner's work order explicitly prescribed the bound-based close exception using that premise.

Trace: after the original wall-clock end, an active unfenced machine's queued attempt short-defers with no rate. The bound arrives before the next claim. All other incident obligations are done, so the operator closes the record. The rate returns before that queued attempt next claims. It now takes the funding re-check without any restore grace and can destroy the machine after less than one interval of rate-present time. Reaching a bound has not itself disposed of this attempt. The same issue can involve a provider refusal or an attempt awaiting availability; the simple queued trace suffices.

Owner clarification required: does merely reaching the bound irrevocably end restore protection for all affected machines, including an attempt that later sees a returned rate, or may incident closure use this exception only once the remaining protected work has a specified disposition? These are different promises. Recommend preserving protection for pending funding cancellations until a disposition or grace completion justifies closure, while retaining a finite escape for a currency that never regains a rate. The owner must settle that tradeoff; do not invent a new stored disposition or close criterion as an implementation detail.

Acceptance: make STO-56's premise and permitted closure match the chosen behavior; reconcile OPS-41 and ADR-0029; add the return-after-close-before-next-claim conformance trace. Do not claim current Lean proofs establish closure: the model explicitly omits it.

title: LDG-16 still identifies restore grace with its unpaused wall-clock end
description:

title: A rate_outage deficiency feeds provider payables forever: nothing resolves it
description:
Raised by two readers (fable, opus) of the 2026-10-03 panel on pv-gip.31; holds whichever way that question is decided.

LDG-66 (12-billing-and-ledger.md ~1285-1286): unresolved deficiencies 'MUST feed provider payables in the solvency check (LDG-17)'. STO-37 (05-persistence.md ~881-882): a rate_outage row's resolved_at 'stays null on this cause', and ~1302-1303 'nothing in this specification converts it'; only late_attach_cleanup deficiencies are ever resolved (05 ~872-875). So every outage's absorbed provider cost stays a payable in LDG-17's inequality after the outage ends and after the provider has been paid: the phantom liability 05 ~876-878 records for wind-down, again.

Trace: a 6-hour USD outage absorbs 40 USD of provider cost; the operator pays the provider's invoice; the 40 USD row still counts as owed in every later solvency check, forever, and accumulates across outages until the check fails on liabilities already paid.

Acceptance: one requirement says when a rate_outage deficiency stops feeding payables (e.g. when the provider cost it records is paid, or at an operator resolution), STO-37's 'stays null' agrees with it, and a CNF case asserts a settled outage no longer counts.

comments.text: Decided 2026-10-04 by the owner: E rejected. "Something like A+, we need a good accounting solution." Panel r10 drafted the design (brief and four answers in /var/tmp/provisiond-panel-r10/, synthesis.md there). Agreed by all four: one append-only payable balance per (provider_account, currency), outside ledger_entries; the invoice is the authority and replaces provisiond's accrual for its period; operator-recorded invoices and payments through an idempotent operator-only verb (DigitalOcean has a billing API, Hetzner Cloud and Robot have none); LDG-66's deficiency feed deleted; max(0, B) per account; an unrated currency omitted per LDG-40. Open sub-decisions put to the owner one at a time: the asset side (pay, record, then sell vs counted bank cash), derived vs stored accrual, what a stale tab does, and pv-gip.42.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Q4a decided 2026-10-04 by the owner ("accept"): no fiat on the asset side. The check counts held
satoshis only; the operator pays a provider from business money, records the payment, and only then
draws satoshis. Drawing first halts until the payment is recorded (opus r10). Accepted cost: about
one invoice cycle of working capital. Astra's counted business cash rejected: self-declared, it is
the unverifiable figure r9 rejected as D and behaves like LDG-59's forbidden last-known value.

Q4b decided 2026-10-04 by the owner ("Agree"): the accrual is derived at check time, never stored:
the native provider cost on entries (LDG-2) dated after the account's latest invoice period_end,
plus deficiencies carrying a charge no entry carries (opus r10: clamp_overflow, rate_outage,
unrecoverable_setup_fee; to verify against LDG-66's causes), joined subject -> provider account.
LDG-31's clamp splits the native cost as it splits the satoshis. Accepted: cost nobody is charged
for (LDG-25's free operations, a quarantined meter, a resource provisiond did not create) is missed
until the invoice replaces the accrual. Stored accrual rows (astra, sol) rejected: a second writer
at every posting and a second copy of what entries hold (LDG-17's 2026-09-02 deletion).

Q4c decided 2026-10-04 by the owner ("Agree"): no staleness rule, no alarm, no per-account block.
An unrecorded invoice leaves the accrual standing in; an unrecorded payment only stops the operator
drawing those satoshis. The operator gets a read of the tab (lines, accrual since the cutoff, latest
invoice, the headroom it may draw without failing the check), and recording an invoice returns its
true-up against the accrual. Recording is not a bill-increasing operation, so it is admitted under
a halt. Rejected: fable's stale/overdue/variance alarms (a calendar's job; "overdue" fires on paid
but unrecorded bills), astra/sol's per-account block (customers pay for operator bookkeeping).

comments.author: master
comments.text: Defaults chosen 2026-10-04 for the work order (panel r10, owner may veto): invoices are recorded net of the credits the provider applied (kinds invoice and payment only, no credit kind); D1 scope or delete LDG-64/LDG-66's 'nothing in this specification converts it', since the check values B at the current rate; D2 delete 'or the float' in CNF-138's valued-terms-short case so it exercises the payable leg; delete ledger_entries.settlement_ref and LDG-6's 'provider-side settlement reference once known' (no writer on an append-only row); LDG-20's 'before the liability falls due' made true without due dates (no due_at; opus: limit to the stress leg); STO-37 resolved_at kept only if the accrual needs it to avoid counting a late_attach_cleanup cost twice, else deleted.

title: ADR-0027's prose promise overstates its theorem: a poison between two honest prices becomes the median
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip` — the window median (`ADR-0027`). Raised by the Panel reviewing `pv-gip.1` (2026-09-23,
`gpt-6-astra` and `gpt-5.6-sol` independently, verified by arithmetic).

## What is false

`ADR-0027`'s Decision section says a transient bad observation "cannot move the rate to a price
no honest pass in the window accepted". Counterexample: honest `[100, 103, 104]`, replace 103
with 101.5; the lower median is 101.5, a price no honest pass accepted. The theorem the ADR names
— *replacing any one observation in the window cannot move the median past a value another
observation in the window carries* — is a **range** bound and is true; the prose claim that the
rate is always an honest price is stronger than the theorem and false.

`pv-gip.1` landed the true form and flagged it: `LDG-16` says a transient bad observation "moves
the rate (`LDG-58`) no further than to a neighbouring price some honest pass in the window
accepted"; `PRV-13e` says "No single rate observation moves the rate outside what the window's
other observations carry". The ADRs were out of that ticket's scope.

The ADR is also split on "half": its Decision says "at least half the window", its *What this
does not promise* says "more than half". The requirements say half / at least half, which is
correct for a lower median (two of four suffice).

## What to land

- Amend `ADR-0027`'s prose to the range bound the theorem supports, with a dated note recording
  the interior-poison counterexample.
- Make its "half" consistent with the requirements.
- Consider an interior-poison case in `CNF-99` (`[100, 103, 104] → [100, 101.5, 104]`, assert
  the rate is 101.5 and lies inside the honest range): the current far-below case never shows the
  poison itself becoming the median.
- `pv-gip.2` must state its theorem as the range bound, not the ADR's prose.
close_reason: ADR-0027 restated to the range bound the requirements carry

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Fixed in the ADR, 2026-09-23. The three sentences that said "a price no honest pass accepted"
now say the range bound the requirements landed: no further than the honest values on either side,
never outside the range the honest passes carry -- and the ADR carries the counterexample itself
(honest 100, 103, 104; 103 replaced by 101.5 reads 101.5) as the reason the bound is a range and
not a membership. "More than half" is now "half" everywhere, matching the lower median on an even
window. PRV-13e's second half in the ADR is restated as "a rate outside what the honest passes
carry needs at least half the window to carry it", which is the true form; pv-gip.1 landed the
requirement's wording as "No single rate observation moves the rate outside what the window's
other observations carry", and LDG-16's "no further than to a neighbouring price some honest pass
in the window accepted" -- the two-axis review of e7ab053 is checking whether that LDG-16 phrase is
itself true of 101.5 (it is a neighbouring price, but no honest pass accepted it), and if not that
lands with pv-gip.1's record fixes.

The interior-poison CNF-99 case this ticket suggested is moved to pv-gip.3, which already owns
the next CNF-99 edit. Closing; pv-gip.2 now waits on pv-gip.3 instead, since Q2 there (does one
failed pass still halt) decides the rate module's no-rate cases.

## Historical no-rate time without a subject outage row

Found while reviewing pv-vwe.34 exit closure, but pre-existing for ordinary ticks. This is

`STO-37` at both revisions defines the replayed start as "the earliest instant of the maximal
interval, ending at the writer's posting, throughout which the window yielded no rate" and opens

at rate boundaries does not itself supply the missing historical row or change that endpoint.
The set leaves unstated how this elapsed no-rate segment acquires the row/window the apportioning

Decide and specify the missing historical-row/replay behavior, then add conformance traces for
both writers and the matched stop-boundary variant. Any formal coverage must state its replay

title: A rate outage lifts a solvency halt already in force
description: From the Spec review of pv-gip.31 (b682c8a). The halt holds only while the check fails: 01-domain-model.md ~558 'Refused because a solvency or rate-availability gate is failing'; 04-api-contract.md ~251 'while LDG-20's solvency halt is in force'. Trace: a computed shortfall lies in the USD leg, so the halt is in force and invoices are cancelled; USD's window then yields no rate; LDG-40's amended row omits the USD leg, the valued terms pass, minting resumes and the deposit read stops reporting gate solvency. That is LDG-20's own case ('a customer could pay for a claim the operator had just computed it could not honour'), and starving one currency's window now lifts a declared halt. ADR-0029's 'A missing rate computes no such insolvency' is false when the insolvency was computed first; its accepted cost covers only shortfalls arising during the outage. Owner's decision: record it as a cost, or a pass with a leg omitted proves nothing, so the last computed verdict stands until every leg can be valued.

title: An interrupted cancellation can reach operator retry before its fence exists
description:
# Owner clarification: retry after interruption before the cancellation fence

Found by Opus in Round 1 of rloop Run 20261004T232205.225230922Z-2186469 and independently verified by the Manager against 922ff45e5de6bc106368e98d344248f0736b023a. This is a behavioral and conformance gap, not a cosmetic comment request. The assigned closed beads stay closed; this follow-up does not reopen Q11/Q12 or select their replacement.

## Passages and trace

- `03-operation-lifecycle.md:315`, OPS-15: “At startup, before any claim, the engine MUST move every `running` operation to `needs_reconciliation`”. Interrupt a cancellation after claim but before its fence transaction; no fence was written and no provider call occurred.
- OPS-48 at `03-operation-lifecycle.md:1025` maps `needs_reconciliation` to `uncertain` with “**Stays set**”; its resolved `not_applied` row at 1028 maps to `stalled` with the same fence cell. OPS-31 provides `not_applied`: “the mutation took effect, so the operation settles `succeeded`; or it did not, so it settles `failed`” (`03-operation-lifecycle.md:1122`). For the interrupted pre-dispatch delete, no mutation took effect.
- API-64 at `04-api-contract.md:1014` admits the stalled retry “by a conditional write guarded on `(id, state = stalled)`” and enqueues a fresh delete attempt. Its origin is stamped `requested_by: operator` with non-null `episode_id` at 1029.
- LDG-62 at `12-billing-and-ledger.md:1766` admits the guarded extension on “`machines.destroy_committed IS NULL`”. With a null fence, active tenant, healthy account, available rate, sufficient funds and no solvency halt, the customer can extend before the retry worker's fence transaction. API-7 supplies no separate open-episode refusal on this extension path.
- OPS-41 step 2 at `03-operation-lifecycle.md:812` says retry bypasses the funding decision “regardless of the current rate or suspension”. If the episode remains open and the machine present, its step 1 does not abort. The retried worker can fence and delete without reconsidering the newly funded machine.
- This conflicts with OPS-42's ordering sentence: “Extension first: the worker's read sees the new commitment, `OPS-41` applies, and it makes no provider call at all.”

## Readings requiring the owner

1. OPS-48's “Stays set” asserts a fence is already present at uncertain/stalled. Then the interrupted-claim path needs a specified writer/ordering that establishes it, which the current startup and resolution rules do not provide.
2. The table preserves the actual value, including null on the interrupted-claim path. Then an API-64 retry can be unfenced and the unconditional retry funding bypass conflicts with extension-first safety.

These lead to different admissible extensions, retry outcomes and provider calls. No reading is selected by this issue. Do not repair this by silently narrowing OPS-15, weakening OPS-42, or assuming every stalled episode is already fenced.

Recommendation: the owner should explicitly define when deletion becomes committed on a never-fenced interrupted attempt and what happens when an extension wins before that commitment, preserving OPS-42's extension-first guarantee. Specify the relevant startup/resolution/retry ordering and refusal behavior. Then align the model and conformance with that decision; do not treat a model omission as evidence of impossibility.

## Model and check gap

title: ADR-0028 in the requirements: the restore grace is one instant in the restore record; destroy_not_before withdrawn
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip`. This ticket lands `ADR-0028` (2026-09-25, amended the same day after a four-reader
self-consistency pass) in the requirements: the restore grace becomes one instant in the restore
record, and `machines.destroy_not_before` is withdrawn. `pv-gip.2` then models what the text says
(`ADR-0025`), so wording here is load-bearing. `ADR-0028`'s Consequences section is the edit list;
this ticket names the same edits and no others.

## What to land

Each bullet names the owner of a rule; everywhere else points at it (`AGENTS.md`). Every sentence
asserting what another requirement says carries that requirement's words. Every withdrawn rule
carries a dated 2026-09-25 note in the house form, after the record it amends, retaining the
withdrawn wording where a trap sits behind it — and the per-machine deadline is such a trap: it
looked right, was built for two days, and produced the five defects the ADR lists.

- **`STO-56`** gains `grace_ends_at`, nullable, written in the same transaction as step (3)'s
  mark ("A marked step does not run again") as that instant plus one re-derivation interval; and
  the rule that the record MUST NOT be closed before `grace_ends_at` has passed. Its existing
  sentence about both components reading the open row first is the startup read and does not
  cover the per-claim read, which `OPS-41` owns.
- **`STO-54`**: the freeze on the five frozen actors lifts at `grace_ends_at` rather than "when
  step (3) completes" (the `suspend_tenant` exception's own later condition stands on top); the
  step (1) clause writing `destroy_not_before` on "every machine whose stored `runway_until` has
  passed" is withdrawn; the "what the restore does not repair" paragraph says the grace is one
  interval from step (3), that a machine whose fence is set gets no extension from it — its route
  back is `OPS-42`'s — and that a retry's claim waits the interval like every claim. Quote
  `ADR-0028` for the reason, once.
- **`OPS-41`**: the claim rule — a claim of an exposure-reducing cancellation MUST defer while a
  restore record is open and its `grace_ends_at` is null or in the future: to `grace_ends_at` when
  it is set, by `OPS-8`'s short delay when it is not yet written; "the same write as `OPS-8`'s
  defer, though nothing refused it" (`F51`'s words — cite `F51`, since `OPS-8` covers an index
  refusal and a short delay, and this rule states its own scope and duration); the worker reads
  the restore record at each such claim; the rule applies whichever path enqueued the
  cancellation. Nothing in `OPS-41` reads `destroy_not_before` today; the provider-call sentence
  is `LDG-16`'s, below.
- **`LDG-16`**: the deadline paragraph withdrawn, including the sentence `pv-gip.1` gave it — "an
  exposure-reducing cancellation MUST NOT make its provider call while its machine's
  `destroy_not_before` is in the future" — retained in the dated note as the trap; the routing
  predicate is "stored `runway_until` has passed" alone; the bypass sentence says the bound's and
  the suspended tenant's cancellations claim like every other and wait for the grace; the worker
  sentences become one — the worker reads no fact the grace wrote.
- **`LDG-62`**, **`OPS-41`**: "clears the deadline" withdrawn where it survives from pv-gip.1.
- **`LDG-65`**: its deadline clause withdrawn; the outage-expiry and bound cases claim like every
  other. **`LDG-64`** carries no deadline sentence and is not touched.
- **`PRV-13e`**: "never writes `machines.destroy_not_before`" withdrawn.
- **`05-persistence.md`** machines table: the `destroy_not_before` row withdrawn with a dated note
  in the row's place per README's conventions; `STO-49`/`STO-54` cross-references that name it
  follow.
- **`CNF-99`**'s restore cases: measured from step (3); a queued delete re-run after a restore and
  claimed before step (3) defers by a short delay and writes no fence; one claimed after step (3)
  is re-queued to `grace_ends_at` and writes no fence; an extension inside the grace closes the
  episode `funded` at the re-claim; a fenced machine gets no extension.
- **`CNF-295`**'s restore rehearsal: its two assertions of `destroy_not_before` become assertions
  of `grace_ends_at` on the record.
- **`CONTEXT.md`** already carries **Restore grace**; if the rule and the glossary disagree, the
  rule is wrong.

## Must not touch

`LDG-38`, `LDG-58`, `LDG-59`, `STO-37` (the window and the opener are `ADR-0027`'s and are done or
in `pv-gip.16`'s hands). `tools/` and `docs/adr/` beyond a citation. `OPS-48`'s table gains no row:
a re-queued attempt has not settled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `grep -n "destroy_not_before" *.md` finds only dated withdrawal notes
- [ ] `grep -n "reads neither fact\|destruction deadline\|MUST NOT make its provider call" 12-billing-and-ledger.md` finds only dated notes
- [ ] `OPS-41` carries the claim rule with both branches (null, future) and the per-claim read;
      `STO-56` carries `grace_ends_at` and the closure rule
- [ ] `CNF-99` carries the five restore cases; `CNF-295` asserts the record, not the column
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes

title: LDG-64 closes the absorbed window at observed_at while STO-49 lets a pass read early and commit late
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip` — the window median (`ADR-0027`). Raised by `gpt-5.6-sol` reviewing `pv-gip.1`
(2026-09-23). Pre-existing: the same instant was the closer before `ADR-0027`.

## The gap

`LDG-64` closes the absorbed window "with that observation's instant" — its `observed_at`.
`STO-49` says a row is "written before that rate is used for anything" and that "a pass that reads
early and commits late, writes a row whose instant precedes one already stored". A row observed at
`t0` and accepted at `t1` ends the outage at `t0`, though no rate was usable until `t1`; the
hours `t0..t1` are then priced at a rate that did not exist while they elapsed — what `LDG-64`'s
"never billed retroactively" forbids.

## Recommendation

Close the absorbed window at the accepting write's instant (or the later of the two), stated in
`LDG-64`, and say in `STO-49` which column carries it if `observed_at` cannot.

title: pv-gip.1's record: the dated notes it owes, and the promise stated once
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip` — the window median (`ADR-0027`). `pv-gip.1` landed the rules; this ticket lands the
record it owes and states the promise once. `AGENTS.md`: "The rule and the record are two edits
with two different failure rates. Land the rule; write the record after." Found by the two-axis
review of `e7ab053`, which the Run's own four-reviewer Panel passed over. Independent of
`pv-gip.3`, which is the owner's.

## The promise, stated once

`PRV-13e` (`02-provider-contract.md:356-359`) states the true bound: "No single rate observation
moves the rate outside what the window's other observations carry". Three other copies say "no
further than to a neighbouring price some honest pass in the window accepted" — `LDG-16`
(`12-billing-and-ledger.md:1555-1556`), `CNF-99`'s headline (`10-conformance-checklist.md:413`,
which also asserts "never the print"), and `executive-summary.md:302`. Read as a destination, that
is false: honest `100, 103, 104` with the `103` replaced by `101.5` reads `101.5`, a price no honest
pass accepted, inside the honest range. `ADR-0027` now carries that counterexample.

- `LDG-16` owns the promise and states the range bound in `PRV-13e`'s form, or `PRV-13e` owns it
  and `LDG-16` quotes it — one home, the other three quote the owner's sentence verbatim.
- `CNF-99`'s one-poison case (`10:417-420`) feeds only a print "far below them all"; add an
  interior poison — the `101.5` above — and an upward one, asserting the range bound, not the
  destination. (`pv-gip.3` was holding this; it moves here.)

## The record

Each of these changed a rule or retired a trap without the dated note the house form carries
(`*Withdrawn 2026-09-23, ADR-0027 …*`, `**AMENDED 2026-09-23**`), or restated something outside
its home:

- `LDG-41` (`12:1057-1060`): re-keyed from the persistence rule to the window median under a bare
  `**AMENDED.**`; the withdrawn "not smoothing" framing is the trap `ADR-0027` names, so it is
  retained in a dated note. Its "a rolling median is a filter, and it is there for the observation
  it filters out" re-explains the ADR's argument; point at the ADR instead.
- `LDG-65` (`12:~1192`): the reference clause and the whole 2026-09-21 paragraph replaced with no
  note; the 2026-09-21 record vanished. Keep the dated record of what was withdrawn and why.
- `STO-49` (`05:585-587`): the one-window floor is undated; the reference clause was deleted
  silently. Date the floor; the clause records a fact that changed and may go, but say when.
- `STO-49`'s 2026-09-21 heading (`05:596`) was reworded in place — a record is what was decided
  then. Restore its words; the 2026-09-23 note goes after it.
- `PRV-13e` (`02:337-341`): "**The interval is not the rate window.**" is a new rule, undated, and
  the paragraph restates "twenty-four hours by default" — the number's home is `LDG-58`; cite it
  and let it hold the number. The old conflation of interval and window is a trap the ADR names:
  retain it in the dated note.
- `STO-54` (`05:~1204`): the 2026-09-21 rejection record ("re-keying that slot to an observation …
  was refused") guarded the surviving deadline and was deleted. Restore it with the reference
  part marked withdrawn.
- `LDG-39` and the meter (`12:267`, `12:790`): "`LDG-16`'s persistence delay" was dropped as a
  reachability path without substituting the window's lag, which `ADR-0027` says produces the
  same shortfall. Substitute it.

## Must not touch

`LDG-38`'s split rule and `LDG-59`'s quorum halt — both are `pv-gip.3`, the owner's. `tools/`.
Nothing in `docs/adr/` beyond a citation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `grep -n "neighbouring price" *.md` finds only the owner's sentence and verbatim quotes of it
- [ ] `CNF-99` carries the interior and upward one-poison cases asserting the range bound
- [ ] Every site above carries its dated note, in the house form, after the record it amends
- [ ] `grep -n "twenty-four hours" *.md` finds only `LDG-58` and `OVR-19`'s register row
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: Landed by rloop Run 20260923T062212. LDG-16 owns the promise, stated as the range bound; PRV-13e, CNF-99 and executive-summary quote it (citations gate QUOTED). CNF-99 carries far-below, far-above and interior (100,103,104 -> 101.5) one-poison cases asserting the range. Dated notes in the house form at LDG-41, LDG-65, STO-49 (floor dated, 2026-09-21 heading restored), PRV-13e's interval paragraph (number moved to LDG-58, conflation retained), STO-54 (2026-09-21 record restored, reference part withdrawn); LDG-39's clamp sentence and the meter name the window's lag. Panel of four (fable, opus, astra, sol): no blocking findings; cosmetic follow-up filed as a sibling bead. Gate green unpiped, three independent runs.

title: A claim-time rejection of a present value has no kind outside PRV-47's caller-supplied values (OPS-23, OPS-43, PRV-47, CNF-342)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during the two-axis review of `pv-p1y` (branch `pv-p1y`), 2026-10-21.*

`pv-p1y` gave `PRV-47`'s rejection of a **caller-supplied** value a kind. Two claim-time
rejections of a value that is **present** still have none:

- **A stored value that fails boundary validation at `OPS-43`'s step 3.** `OPS-23` names kinds
  only for a missing field ("For create, install, power and delete, a missing required field MUST
  fail as follows"). `CNF-342`'s step-3 case asserts only that it "fails at `OPS-43`'s step 3
  instead, with no provider request at all".
- **A value the engine itself writes that `PRV-47`'s driver validation rejects**: the operation-id
  name or tag on a temporary key, or Robot's generated correlator key. `PRV-47` covers "every value
  it forwards to the provider". Since `pv-p1y` the `invalid_request` rule names only a
  caller-supplied value, and `DOM-17` calls `invalid_request` a caller error, so an engine-written
  value has no kind.

Two engines that conform: one fails the step-3 case `invalid_request` with `retryable: false`, the
other `conflict` with `retryable: true`. Both settle `failed` under `OPS-11`'s create row, so the
caller is told to fix the request by one engine and to retry it unchanged by the other.

Siblings: `pv-xer` (claim-time failures with no stated `retryable`) and `pv-p3k` (no kind for
`allow_orders`). The review suggested one rule in `OPS-23`/`OPS-43` covering every claim-time
rejection, instead of one kind sentence per check. That is a design call for triage.

Found by the local review of `pv-p1y` (findings 1 and 7) and the `pv-p1y` Run's follow-up comment.

  transaction, or during a first transaction that has not erred, is not "during that loop".
- pv-zbp widened that span. The record of a stop after `execute` returns holds "before that
  write's first transaction, during it and while `OPS-49` repeats it", and `OPS-21` says "the
  later-stop exit" applies to it "as they do to a recorded cancellation".
- The formal model takes one reading: `Provisiond.StopRecord.later_stop_exits` holds for any
  prefix, the empty one included, so a `laterStop` before the record's first transaction is an
  exit. `CNF-362` drives a later stop only "during the record's whole-transaction loop" and
  "between repeats of the settle write".

Example: a deploy stops the engine just after a create's `execute` returns success, while its
settle write waits for a store connection. A second stop arrives before the first transaction
is sent.
- Engine A exits at once, as the model does. The row is still `running`; at restart `OPS-15`
  moves it to `needs_reconciliation`, and the correlator searches for an order the worker had in
  hand.
- Engine B sends the transaction, since no loop has started. The create settles `succeeded` and
  its money posts once.

The same split applies to a cut-off record of a cancellation of `execute` (pv-tst).

Question: does a later stop end the record at any point after the stop being recorded, as the
model says, or only once the record is repeating under `OPS-49`? If it ends it at any point, does
`OPS-21`'s "A transaction already sent MAY finish" cover a record transaction in flight? Raised as
follow-up 2 on `pv-zbp`; it predates pv-zbp. (`OPS-21`, `OPS-49`, `OPS-15`, `CNF-362`)

title: OPS-23's repeated sale check before dispatch: does it read the create's snapshot or the live offer (PRV-31, PRV-13b)
description:
`OPS-23` says "Validation that was performed at the API boundary MUST be repeated in the worker before the driver is called." `API-7`'s create tail refuses "when the named offer is not sellable under `PRV-13b` or `PRV-31`", so the worker repeats that sale check. No sentence says what the repeated check reads: the create's `request_summary` offer snapshot, or the driver's current offer listing and descriptor.

Example: a customer creates at 10:00 from an offer whose bound is provider-local today; the API admits it. At 10:05, before claim, the provider re-lists the offer with a one-month minimum term (or a traffic term `PRV-13b` would refuse). A worker that re-checks the snapshot dispatches the order; a worker that re-checks the live listing fails the create with `offer_not_sellable`. Both are conformant today, and the customer sees different outcomes. No money is lost either way: nothing has been ordered. (`invalid_request` is not on `OPS-11`'s admission-only list, so a worker may emit it.)

For a snapshot an older `api` wrote without the bound, reading the snapshot makes the missing field "a deterministic failure in the worker" (`OPS-23`); `pv-d21` closed that rollout half as unreachable.

Found by panel r53 (opus), docs/research/panels-2026-10/r53/. Requirement text and conformance only.
close_reason: Done in 96cddcb: OPS-43 re-tests the create's offer for sale at claim (PRV-13b, PRV-31) against the running descriptor and one current List offers result, in the owner's five-step order, failing invalid_request/offer_not_sellable (retryable false, failed, commitment released under LDG-39). OPS-23 points at OPS-43; CNF-241 carries the bound, traffic, ordering, control and restart cases and 'no provider mutation'. Gates green. Pre-existing gaps are follow-ups 1-6 above.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** The worker re-tests the create's offer for sellability (`PRV-13b`, `PRV-31`) against the provider's current offer and the running descriptor at claim, before any provider mutation. The rule lives in `OPS-43`.

**Current behavior:**
`API-7`'s create tail refuses "`invalid_request`/`offer_not_sellable` when the named offer is not sellable under `PRV-13b` or `PRV-31`", but only at admission. No sentence says whether the worker repeats that check before ordering, or what it reads. `OPS-23` says "Validation that was performed at the API boundary MUST be repeated in the worker before the driver is called", but it does not say whether that covers purchase-tail checks (`OPS-11` makes some of them admission-only). `PRV-42`'s dispatch check only confirms the offer "is still listed". As a result, an offer re-listed between acceptance and claim with a traffic allowance, or a descriptor redeployed with a later cancellation bound while creates are queued, is ordered by one conformant engine and refused by another. When it is ordered, the cost falls on the operator (overage is "operator exposure too", `PRV-13b`) or on the customer's spare balance and then the operator (`LDG-63`). The create's `request_summary` snapshot cannot serve the check, because it carries no traffic bound.

**Desired behavior (owner decision 2026-10-16, panel r54, 4–0):**
- **Home: `OPS-43`.** At claim, before any provider mutation, the worker MUST re-test the named offer under `PRV-13b` and `PRV-31`. It uses the descriptor it runs with and the current driver List offers result, the same result `OPS-43`'s price re-read and `PRV-42`'s presence check use. Date bounds resolve against provider-local today at the time of the check.
- **Claim-time order, stated in the text:** (1) `PRV-40`'s stored channel-closure read; (2) the current List offers result; (3) the sellability re-test; (4) `OPS-43`'s price comparison; (5) any per-order key upload or other provider mutation. An unsellable offer gets no price comparison. Without this order, an offer both re-priced and unsellable gets `price_moved` from one engine and `offer_not_sellable` from another.
- **Failure:** `invalid_request` with `details.reason: "offer_not_sellable"` and `retryable: false`, as `WIR-9`'s inner object embedded under `WIR-10b`. It carries no `refusals` or `not_checked`, which belong to the purchase tail. `OPS-11`'s create row classifies it `failed`. The commitment is released in full under `LDG-39`'s "Deterministic rejection before acceptance" case, with no setup fee or first unit debited (`LDG-32`).

- **`CNF-241`:** add these cases:
  - With the price unchanged, change between acceptance and claim (a) the declared cancellation bound to later than provider-local today, and (b) the offer's `traffic_bound` to an allowance. Each must fail as above with no provider mutation, the commitment released and nothing debited.
  - A still-sellable control proceeds.
  - The same cases hold across a restart between acceptance and claim.

- Record the decision as a dated amendment, citing `pv-hsm` and panel r54. Use an ADR amendment only if the requirement edits need one.

**Key interfaces:**
- `OPS-43`: claim-time offer re-read, now also the sale re-test and the claim-time order.
- `OPS-23`: pointer only.
- `CNF-241`: new cases and the wording fix.
- `WIR-9` / `WIR-9a` / `WIR-10b`: existing `offer_not_sellable` error shape, reused unchanged.
- `PRV-40`: existing claim-time closure read, ordered first.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `OPS-43` states the sale re-test, its inputs (running descriptor plus current List offers), the five-step claim order, and the error with its classification and commitment release. Each claim about another requirement carries a quote (`AGENTS.md`).
- [ ] `OPS-23` carries a pointer to `OPS-43` and no second copy of the rule.

- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`, run unpiped, exits 0. If a formalized clause is touched, its Lean declaration moves with it.

**Out of scope:**
- Adding a field to `DOM-9`'s offer for an offer-reported cancellation bound. That is a separate bead.
- Pre-column rows and bound-less snapshots (`pv-d21`, closed as unreachable).
- `ADR-0039`'s live-evidence gate for allowance offers.
- Any change to admission-time tail refusal ordering, or to post-order term handling (`PRV-13c` exception path, Q25).

title: OPS-23's install timing binds 'these checks'; a present-value check run after the rescue marker would settle with a rescue_exit the marker contradicts (OPS-23, OPS-45, WIR-9a)
description:
> *Filed 2026-10-22 while judging panel B (pv-7j3, pv-p3k, pv-009, pv-gpw, pv-ss4), from a full read of the set at `1bdf453`.*

On an install, does `OPS-23`'s new present-value check have to run before the `OPS-45` markers, as the missing-field checks do?

- pv-gpw added `03:1896`: "A field that is present but fails this repeated validation fails as its writer's bullet above says, on both the error and the operation view, and settles as these missing-field failures do."
- The timing rule a few lines on reads: "On an install, these checks MUST run before either `OPS-45` marker is written: its rescue marker is "**false, written before begin rescue (`PRV-15`) is dispatched**". The install settles `failed` with `disk_effect: "none"` and `rescue_exit: "none"`". It follows "These missing-field failures settle `failed`".
- `OPS-23`'s own bound for repeated validation is only "before the driver is called".

Two readings:
- **Reading A:** "these checks" is all of the repeated validation. A present-value failure comes before the markers and settles with `rescue_exit: "none"`.
- **Reading B:** "these checks" is the missing-field checks. A present-value check may run after the rescue marker is written `false` and before begin rescue is dispatched.

Under reading B, "settles as these missing-field failures do" promises `rescue_exit: "none"`. But `WIR-9a` renders `rescue_exit` from that marker ("`none` only where no rescue session was opened"; `unknown` "where it failed or the operation died before reaching it"). So two engines can send different `rescue_exit` values for the same rejected install.

Owners: `OPS-23`, `OPS-45`, `WIR-9a`.

description:
Formal layer: the sweep's effective-window maximum and its failed re-read (Reconcile).

Authority: ADR-0025 ("a negative theorem for every guard a dated amendment added"; a formalized clause keeps its requirement identifier; a theorem is never a conformance item; no CNF identifiers in Lean) and the admission test in pv-vwe's 2026-09-21 comment (composition with an existing state transition or an authoritative rendered table). Panel: docs/research/panels-2026-10/r47/synthesis.md (owner decision Q30, 2026-10-13: write it). Every new guard is a named field of the model's parameter record with a witness pair (refused with the guard, admitted without it) and one negative-control row in .github/workflows/ci.yml that flips it and reds exactly that witness. Do not weaken any existing theorem statement (AGENTS.md); keep rendered regions in step (tools/check_regions.py). No requirement text changes except where a docstring quote must follow its source.

1. **Effective window is a maximum (PRV-36, STO-53, OPS-32; ADR-0018, 2026-09-08).** `Reconcile.Windows.visibility` is a plain number whose docstring claims "max(declared, max(observed))"; nothing computes it. Make the visibility window read by `pastWindow`/`sweepStep` the maximum of the declared value and the observed samples under a guard. Witness pair beside `late_acceptance_*`: declared 8, one observed sample 20, a complete pass with the machine unlisted and the re-read `notFound` at wait-end + 10. With the guard: nothing recorded, the meter runs. Declared-only: `authoritativeAbsence`, `meterStoppedAt = some 10`, commitment closed, `live = true` (OPS-32's "this sentence read 'declared' until 2026-09-08"). The theorem is about OPS-32's sentence as written; STO-53's sample write path stays outside the model (samples are given), and say so in the docstring.
2. **A failed re-read is not absence (OPS-32, ADR-0034 Q20).** `Reconcile.Answer` has only `found | notFound`. Add the failed answer so "a failed direct absence confirmation cannot record absence" has its pair: the bad amendment is `a = .notFound` becoming `a ≠ .found` in `sweepStep`.

title: A stop during PRV-13's direct read after an accepted dated cancellation settles needs_reconciliation (OPS-21) or succeeded (PRV-13) by engine choice (PRV-13, OPS-21, OPS-11, CNF-362, CNF-147)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during the pv-zbp review.*

A stop during the direct machine read after an accepted dated cancellation gets two answers: a
cut-off `needs_reconciliation`, or the accepted cancellation's `succeeded`.

- `PRV-13`'s amendment of 2026-10-11 says "After an accepted cancellation returns an effective
  date, the driver MUST read that machine once on its known provider account and external
  identity", and "If the machine remains present, or this read fails for any reason including
  throttle, authentication, network error or deadline expiry, the accepted attempt settles
  `succeeded` as `cancellation_scheduled` with its effective date." It adds "Read failure does not
  turn the accepted dated cancellation into `needs_reconciliation` or establish absence."
- That read happens inside the delete's `execute`. Since pv-zbp, `OPS-21` says "`execute` returns
  only once the outcome its settle write records is final, so every provider call that outcome
  depends on is made inside `execute`."
- A stop the engine survives during that read is a cancellation of `execute`. `OPS-21` says "The
  recorded error is a cut-off `conflict` with `details.reason: "cut_off"` (`WIR-9a`)", and the
  kind's row classifies it. `CNF-362` asserts that "power, reverse DNS, delete and release
  attachment stopped during their provider call after dispatch enter `needs_reconciliation`".

Example: Robot accepts a dated cancellation and returns its effective date. A deploy stops the
engine during the one direct machine read that follows.
- Engine A reads the stop as `OPS-21`'s cancellation. The delete enters `needs_reconciliation`
  with a cut-off `conflict`, and an operator resolves a cancellation the provider already
  accepted.
- Engine B reads the cut-short read as one that "fails for any reason". The delete settles
  `succeeded` as `cancellation_scheduled` with its date.

Both read the text as written. This predates pv-zbp: pv-tst's record rule reached this read.
pv-zbp's review found the same split at `PRV-13c`'s post-order read, where the branch's new
sentence and `CNF-362`'s Placement control chose the cut-off. One principle likely decides both.

Question: when a stop the engine survives cuts short a provider read whose failure the
requirement absorbs, is the stop recorded as that read's failure with the outcome already known,
or as a cut-off `conflict`? (`PRV-13`, `OPS-21`, `OPS-11`, `CNF-362`, `CNF-147`)
close_reason: Decided with pv-zbp: owner decision 2026-10-19 on panel r59 (option 1). OPS-21 now says a survived stop after a delete's cancellation is accepted with an effective date MUST NOT cancel execute, and the stop ends PRV-13's direct read as a failed read. See docs/research/panels-2026-10/r59/synthesis.md and pv-zbp's Agent Brief amendment 2.

title: No conformance item drives API-63's step-8 conditional write with a recoverable status, so a build sending retryable: false there passes (API-63, OPS-43, CNF-360, CNF-278)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during the PR #20 review (`pv-xer`, codex P2 on `6928ccc`), 2026-10-21.*

**The problem.** No conformance item drives `API-63`'s step-8 conditional write with a
recoverable status. Since `pv-xer`, that failure carries “`"state"` for the two recoverable
statuses” and “`retryable: true` for `"state"` on both the error and the operation view”
(`API-63`). Every step-8 refusal the checklist drives uses termination:

- `CNF-278`'s **Fourth** case and its second **Account-read** case commit the termination
  before step 8 commits.
- `CNF-361`'s lost-reply control records `terminated` before the whole-transaction repeat.
- `CNF-360`'s "Refuse the separate `STO-47` check" asserts the values "for the recorded status"
  and doesn't name one, so `terminated` satisfies it.

The recoverable statuses are driven only before claim, where `OPS-43`'s step 1 read fails them.

**Example.** An engine fails step 1 correctly (`state`, `retryable: true`) but copies
termination's `retryable: false` onto every step-8 refusal. Record `credentials_rejected` after
step 1 and before step 8: the engine answers `retryable: false`, and every specified case still
passes.

**Question.** Should `CNF-360` (or `CNF-278`) refuse the step-8 check with `credentials_rejected`
and with `account_unreachable`, recorded after step 1 and before step 8, and assert `state` and
`retryable: true` on the error and the view?

Found by the codex review of PR #20 (thread on `CNF-360`). Not amended there, since it was the
review's second P2.

Review evidence includes independent false-error/true-view and true-error/false-view counterexamples for each recoverable status. Every added line and full-sentence sweep hit was reviewed. Evidence: /var/tmp/rloop-units/provisiond-spec-pv-ip7-1027T215614/implementer-retryability-review.md, implementer-before.log, implementer-after.log, manager-round1-before.log and manager-preaccept-review.md. Specification SHA-256 334fea48a850aed1daed6273d9d9016fa05ffb0692915f97b9d42ea02b1e6edf. Specification-only correction; no system-conformance claim.

title: A create interrupted before OPS-43's step 8 goes Unresolved though it made no provider mutation (OPS-15, OPS-27, OPS-29)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during review of pv-14b (2026-10-17).*

A create interrupted before its correlator entry made no provider mutation, yet it goes to an
operator. `pv-14b` widened that window.

Under `OPS-43`'s claim order, the correlator entry is written at step 8, "in the correlator
transaction", and every provider mutation is step 9. A create with no entry has made no provider
mutation. Its only provider contact was step 4's List offers read. But on interruption:
- `OPS-15`: "the engine MUST move every `running` operation to `needs_reconciliation`".
- `OPS-29`: "Where no correlator exists, the correct outcome is *unresolved*".
- `OPS-27`'s last row: "no verified correlator exists for the operation's ordering channel" is
  **Unresolved**, "Escalate to an operator", with the commitment "Released per `OPS-33`".

The 2026-10-17 review made the zero-correlator reading explicit in `OPS-38`, so engines now agree.
The cost is the outcome: a restart during claim pages an operator, and it holds the customer's
commitment until `OPS-33` releases it, for a create that provably ordered nothing. Before
`pv-14b`, `05-persistence.md` said the correlator was "Written **before** the provider call, like
`provider_account`". `pv-14b` item 6 aligned that row with `PRV-26` ("before the order is sent")
and `API-63` ("the last write before the ordering call"), so the window now spans the List offers
read, the sale re-test, the price comparison and driver validation.

This is a design question, not a contradiction: may a `running` create with no correlator entry
settle `failed` (deterministic, commitment released under `LDG-39`) instead of going unresolved?
The answer turns on whether "no entry" proves "no mutation" across crashes. It does if step 9
cannot start before step 8 commits. Near `pv-qga` (a failed claim-time read), which does not cover
interruption.

Found as follow-up 1 of the `pv-14b` Run (2026-10-17), confirmed in the post-Run review.
close_reason:
Landed in ff6f9ba (spec: settle a create interrupted before step 8 failed on a restart; ADR-0042), after two rloop Rounds. Each Round was reviewed by fable, opus, astra and sol; Round 2 had no findings.
- operations.about_to_order_at: written in OPS-43 step 8 on every channel, under the worker guard, acknowledged before step 9.
- OPS-15: a restart-only exception settles a running create with a null column failed (internal, retryable true) and releases its commitment under LDG-39. It is off while a restore record is open and on a store that may have lost committed writes.
- API-63's test moved to the column, the STO-13 backfill added, pointers placed, and ADR-0042 written.
- Lean: a restart-only guard with its ci.yml row, a restore-trace theorem and a migration theorem.
- Conformance: CNF-358, CNF-359 and CNF-360 added.
The Manager confirmed locally that flipping createExceptionOnRestart in Restore.current gives exactly one red, on the targeted witness (Witnesses.lean:1249), and that deleting the restart-only test literally turns the build red (Restore.lean:575). Gates exit 0. Follow-ups are in the preceding comment.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during PR #6 review (2026-10-17).*

PR #6 review: the codex bot raised this case (P2, https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond/pull/6#discussion_r4300992671): "even an interruption during the step-4 List offers read now holds the customer's commitment until `OPS-33` and pages an operator for an order that could not have been sent. Either record a pre-dispatch marker earlier or make recovery settle this pre-step-8 case deterministically and release the commitment." The thread was answered as owned here and resolved. PR #6 merged as `1292174`, with this bead queued for triage (owner, 2026-10-17).

Two inputs for triage:

1. **An empty correlator entry is not proof of "nothing sent" on every channel.** `PRV-33`: "The driver declares the absence as that channel's `correlator: none`", and "an ambiguous create on that channel MUST resolve to an operator, never to a guess". No text says what such a create stores at step 8. `05-persistence.md` describes the columns as "what the create wrote into the provider (`PRV-26`)", and such a channel writes no correlator into the provider. On that reading the columns stay null after a real order, so a rule that settles a `running` create with a null entry `failed` would settle a dispatched order as a deterministic failure. This description's test, "It does if step 9 cannot start before step 8 commits", holds only where the entry is written on every channel.
2. **The likely fix is a create-side pre-dispatch marker.** Step 8's transaction would record a fact on every channel, correlator or not: "dispatch may have begun". A `running` create found without it at startup made no provider mutation, so it could settle `failed`, with its commitment released under `LDG-39`. `OPS-45` rules this out today: "It does **not** reach `create`: there is no machine yet, the question is whether a *resource was produced*, and the answer comes from `OPS-27`'s correlator search". Its warning names what such a marker must not do: read unscoped, "the marker is unset, so settle `failed`" would settle every ambiguous create as a deterministic failure. A create marker would have to be set in step 8's transaction, before any step-9 mutation, and never cleared. Only its unset case would settle.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

This is the contract. It rests on:

- panels r56 and r56b (`docs/research/panels-2026-10/r56/`, the synthesis and `r56b/`);
- the owner's decisions of 2026-10-17, recorded at the end of that synthesis.

The bead's description and its first comment are context.

**Category:** bug

**Summary:** A create interrupted before `OPS-43`'s step 8 ordered nothing, yet it goes to an operator.
The fix:

- step 8's transaction writes a new write-once column, `operations.about_to_order_at`, on every
  ordering channel;
- a new `OPS-15` restart exception settles a `running` create whose column is null as `failed` and
  releases its commitment;
- `API-63`'s dispatch test moves to the column.

**Lean changes are in scope.** The formal model, the theorems and the `ci.yml` guard witnesses below are
part of this bead, not a follow-up.

**Current behavior:**

- `OPS-15` says "the engine MUST move every `running` operation to `needs_reconciliation`". Its only
  exceptions are `refresh` and `suspend_tenant`.
- What happens to a create interrupted in steps 1-7:
  - It made no provider mutation, because step 9 holds every one, the per-order key upload included.
  - Even so, `OPS-38` gives "A create that recorded none has no count" and "**Unresolved**", and
    `OPS-27`'s last row escalates it to an operator, "Released per `OPS-33`".
  - On Robot that wait is "bounded by **operator response time**" (`PRV-33`). The customer's commitment
    is held for it.
- `API-63` already asserts the invariant the fix needs: "a claimed create with no entry has not passed
  the conditional-write check and does not dispatch". On a `correlator: none` channel (`PRV-33`;
  Robot's standard channel today) no text says what step 8 writes into
  `correlator_kind`/`correlator_value`. So the sentence is not guaranteed there: it is a false statement
  inside a requirement.
- Step 8's operation-row write already carries the claim term (`OPS-6`: "every write that worker makes
  to the operation MUST carry `claim_number = mine`"). Three things are missing:
  - its status term;
  - "zero rows affected means no step 9";
  - a rule that step 9 waits for step 8's acknowledgement. Only `OPS-45` states one for its markers:
    "each acknowledged by the store before the provider call it precedes is made".

**Desired behavior:**

1. **The column.** `operations.about_to_order_at` is a nullable timestamp, null on every kind other than
   create.
   - It is written once, in step 8's transaction (`API-63`'s correlator transaction), on every ordering
     channel, `correlator: none` included.
   - It is never cleared, and it survives the payload purge on entry to a settled state or to
     `needs_reconciliation`.
   - It is not a correlator. The pair's meaning, `PRV-26`, `OPS-38` and the machine row are unchanged,
     and nothing copies the column to a machine row.
2. **`OPS-43` step 8:**
   - the column write is guarded by `STO-3`'s worker guard, status `running` plus `OPS-6`'s claim term;
   - zero rows affected means no step 9, and the worker exits;
   - step 9 begins only after step 8's transaction is acknowledged;
   - a lost acknowledgement leads to `OPS-49`'s whole-transaction repeat, never to a speculative
     dispatch;
   - the step order itself is unchanged.
3. **A new `OPS-15` exception**, beside `refresh`. On a restart only, a `running` create whose
   `about_to_order_at` is null MUST be settled `failed`:
   - **Error:** `internal`, naming the restart (as `refresh` does), with `retryable: true` on the error
     and on the operation view. `OPS-16` keeps an error already recorded.
   - **The guard:** the null test sits inside the startup pass's own conditional write, guarded
     `(id, status = running, kind = create, about_to_order_at IS NULL)`, not in a read before it.
     Whichever of the pass and a live step-8 write commits first, the other affects no row.
   - **Money:** the commitment is released in that same write under `LDG-35`. It follows `LDG-39`'s
     "Deterministic rejection before acceptance" row (never debited) and `LDG-32`. `STO-58`'s
     resource-offer exclusion is freed.
   - **Not a classification:** it is not an `OPS-11` classification. Say so, citing `OPS-45`'s "an
     operation interrupted rather than classified is `OPS-15`'s".
   - **Where it is off:** during an open `STO-54` restore incident, and on a store that may have lost
     committed writes, such as a promoted asynchronous standby. State that condition here; how a
     deployment recognises a promotion is pv-s4m's.
   - **A set column** keeps today's path, `needs_reconciliation`.
4. **`API-63`:** the entry test becomes the column.
   - Null means the create has not passed the conditional-write check and does not dispatch. Set means
     it may have dispatched.
   - Qualify "Interruption can instead leave the create unresolved" with the new exception.
5. **Migration (`STO-13`):** a create claimed before the column existed MUST stay conservative and never
   read as "null, so never dispatched".
6. **`STO-3`:**
   - the startup-pass bullet gains the create settlement, with the null test in its guard;
   - the worker-write list gains step 8's write.
7. **Pointers:**
   - `OPS-45`: a dated pointer in its scope sentence. Its "rather than from anything the engine can record
     about itself" is no longer true for this case.
   - `OPS-11`: a pointer saying the exception is not a classification.
   - `LDG-39`: the deterministic row names this case.
   - `CONTEXT.md`: the Marker entry, or a new term, covers the column.
   - `OPS-15`'s "`suspend_tenant` is the other exception" no longer counts right.
8. **ADRs:**
   - A new **`ADR-0042`** (next free) that amends `ADR-0016`'s startup pass, citing r56 and r56b.
   - A dated pointer in `ADR-0035`'s rejected bullet "A durable dispatch marker on create, like

9. **Lean** (`OPS-15`'s `@[req]` declarations in the restore model):
   - `passOp` gets a create arm under a restart-only guard;
   - `Op` gets the recorded field;
   - `restart_never_reorders` is re-proved;
   - check whether `Fence`'s `interrupt`, also tagged `OPS-15`, models a create. If it does, it needs the
     same arm.
10. **Three checks that do not exist today.** In r56b each reader planted a plausible bad edit on top of
    a correct one. None of the four tripped a check that exists at `96ce45c`, and the two reds came from
    checks the readers had just added. This bead adds all three:
    - **a.** A Lean restart-only branch with a **restore-trace theorem**: a create never settles

11. **A kill-timing conformance item** in `CNF-302`'s shape, next to `CNF-290`:

    - kill after step 8 commits: expect `needs_reconciliation`;
    - run both with an auction-channel and a standard-channel (`correlator: none`) descriptor;

**Prior work to start from** (machine-local, may vanish, at `96ce45c`). Two readers' clones hold
gate-green drafts. Rename their columns to `about_to_order_at`.

- `/var/tmp/provisiond-panel-r56b/opus/`:

  - The working tree also holds opus's planted bad edit: the `OPS-43` step-8/9 hunk and the 05 row move

title: A create first claimed after its tenant's suspension may be bought and charged its setup fee and first unit before a cancellation is enqueued; no text says whether that is intended (API-58, OPS-43, OPS-27)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during the `pv-1wn` drain review (branch `pv-1wn`, panel r60), 2026-10-21.*

**The problem.** A create first claimed after its tenant's suspension can succeed. The customer is charged the
setup fee and the first billing unit, and only then is a cancellation enqueued for the machine. No text says
whether this is intended.

- `API-7` step 5b refuses a create once the suspension commits, so a suspended tenant's queued create was admitted
  before the flag. Ordinarily it is older than the `suspend_tenant` parent. (fable, r60: a create whose step-5b
  read came before the flag can still commit with a later `created_at`.)
- `OPS-6` says “The claim MUST select the oldest `queued` operation whose availability time has passed”. A create
  names no machine, so `OPS-8`'s index never refuses its claim, and a worker claims it before the parent's step (4)
  can fail it.
- `OPS-43` step 1 reads “the provider account's stored status”, not the tenant's. Step 3 repeats boundary
  validation under `OPS-23`: “Validation that was performed at the API boundary MUST be repeated in the worker
  before the driver is called”. Nothing says whether `API-7` step 5b's suspension check is such validation. If it
  is, the create fails at step 3, and no text names the error: `API-58` says the kind `suspended` is one “which
  `OPS-11` classifies as admission-only and forbids a worker to emit”. If it is not, the create orders.
- `LDG-39` debits the setup fee “only when the order is known to have landed and the create settles”, with the
  prepaid first unit beside it (`ADR-0033`).
- `OPS-27` then acts: “Where the machine's tenant is suspended at the moment of the attach, that same transaction
  also enqueues a system cancellation”. That cancellation can itself fail and leave the machine running.

What the text does say: `API-58` step (2) covers only “a create claimed before the suspension landed”, and step (4)
only work “`queued` but never claimed”. `API-58` names the backstop: “A create that has produced no machine yet
passes the re-sweep's test, so settlement here is not the last guard: where such a create later attaches a machine
to a still-suspended tenant, `OPS-27`'s one-transaction rule enqueues the cancellation in the attach transaction
itself”. It also promises “nothing further can be bought”. All four r60 readers called this a real gap. opus frames
it as a question: is buying, charging and then cancelling the intended outcome?

**Lead fix (fable, r60):** a tenant-status read at claim, in `OPS-43` step 1 beside the account-status read, failing
the create before any provider request with a stated error.

**Also (astra, sol, r60):** a store-level test that keeps create coverage for step (4). astra: seed the create's
`available_at` in the future, then run the parent. sol: exercise step (4)'s write directly at the store, as
`CNF-290` tests a claim “directly at the store”. Both cover the transition, not reachability through the scheduler.
This overlaps pv-gvc's kinds and commitment-release terms.

`CNF-202`'s step-(4) case uses a power operation held behind a running one for this reason (owner, 2026-10-21,
option (a)). Record: `docs/research/panels-2026-10/r60/synthesis.md`.

(`API-58`, `API-7`, `OPS-6`, `OPS-8`, `OPS-43`, `OPS-23`, `OPS-27`, `LDG-39`, `CNF-202`, pv-gvc)

title: The engine accepts a Startup-lock wait bound that PostgreSQL rounds to zero, which disables the generation advance's timeouts
description:
## Behaviour

`OVR-19` types the Startup-lock wait bound as a "finite, positive duration", and `OPS-15` says the
advance's "replacing statement MUST run with `statement_timeout` and `lock_timeout` both set to
`OVR-19`'s Startup-lock wait bound". PostgreSQL stores both settings as whole milliseconds and
rounds a fractional value to the nearest integer; zero disables the timeout. Checked on
PostgreSQL 18.6 with `postgres -C`: `400us` reads back `0` (disabled), `600us` reads `1`,
`1500us` reads `2`. So a positive bound under 0.5 ms passes `OVR-19` and leaves the advance with
no timeout at all, the case `OPS-15`'s timeout exit exists to bound.

A value PostgreSQL rejects outright is already covered: it is a store error, and `OPS-15` says
"On that timeout or any store error, including a lost reply on its commit, the engine MUST log
loudly and exit non-zero having claimed nothing".

## Wanted

An engine startup check that refuses a Startup-lock wait bound below a stated minimum (exits
non-zero before the advance). The shape (the minimum, where it lives: `OVR-19`'s type column, an
`OPS-15` clause or both, and its conformance item) is for the panel.

## Sources

- `OVR-19` (00-overview.md, register row "Startup-lock wait bound"), `OPS-15` (03-operation-lifecycle.md)
- PR #25 review thread on 00-overview.md:407: https://github.com/douglaz/provisiond/pull/25#discussion_r4369366309
- Precedent for filing in the next PR: PR #22, WIR-48

title: The Lean pass of the citation gate has no document pool
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## The gap

`pv-vwe.18` gave the QUOTED rule a second source, the Lean docstrings under `tools/formal/`, and
passes them to `find()` as their own dict. `find()`'s document pool at the `docpool` line resolves a
`` `NN-name.md` `` citation against **the dict it was handed**. For the Lean pass that dict holds
only `.lean` keys, so `docpool` is always empty: a docstring that quotes a document's own words and
names the document cannot verify against it.

Nine such document citations already sit inside Lean docstrings — `Admission.lean`, `Claim.lean`,
`Fence.lean` (`05-persistence.md`), `Rescue.lean` (`01-domain-model.md`, `05-persistence.md`,
`CONTEXT.md`). None fires today, because none of them also carries an attribution verb and a quote.
The first docstring that does will be a false positive no baseline anticipated, and the reader will
be told a correct quote is unverifiable.

## Shape

Give `find()` the Markdown `docs` as its document pool independently of the dict being scanned — a
third parameter, or a separate lookup dict — so the Lean pass resolves `` `NN-name.md` `` the way
the Markdown pass does. Add a docstring that quotes a document's own words as the regression check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Lean docstring quoting a document's own words alongside its filename verifies
- [ ] The three baselined residue spans are unchanged; no new baseline entry
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green

title: QUOTED loses trailing possessive apostrophes during nested-quote normalization
description:
Found during Round 2 acceptance of the citation repair, after a2b58e458f856c9b6e8735df07455f3b0029e2c0. LDG-57 in 12-billing-and-ledger.md says "A deployment MUST watch only unexpired deposits' addresses". A current attribution `LDG-57` says "A deployment MUST watch only unexpired deposits addresses". is compared but incorrectly accepted. The only alteration removes the trailing possessive apostrophe.

Read-only reproduction from the repository root:

```python
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
import check_citations as c
docs, adrs, reqs = c.load()
text = '`LDG-57` says "A deployment MUST watch only unexpired deposits addresses".'
print(c.find({'probe.md': text}, adrs, reqs))
```

At a2b58e4 the result is ([], [], 1). Loading tools/check_citations.py from git show d9d68b6:tools/check_citations.py into a module and running the same find() over the current corpus gives one LDG-57 finding: a deployment must watch only unexpired deposits addresses. Synthetic rows' / rows probes also match incorrectly in both directions.

Cause: QUOTED comparison_text preserves single marks only between word characters; a trailing possessive mark is removed like a closing quotation delimiter. Its current docstring accurately states that narrow rule. EXISTS intentionally retains its older removal of all single and double marks and is not the subject of this report.

Follow-up should distinguish trailing possessive content from nested quotation delimiters sufficiently to reject this misquote while preserving the accepted nested-quotation match, word-internal apostrophe protection, and baseline identities. Assess the appropriate bounded comparison behavior before implementation; no algorithm is selected here. Demonstrate exact -> named QUOTED failure -> restored exact on the real gate and a control that fails when the protection is removed. Do not broaden baseline exemptions or rewrite historical records to hide the case. This issue was filed only, not selected or worked in the repair Run.

then interrupted. Two conforming engines diverge on them.

- `OPS-15`: "at startup, before any claim, the engine MUST move every `running` operation to
  `needs_reconciliation`", and "nothing but a restart can leave a `running` row with no worker
  behind it".
- `STO-54`: "a process that starts while a restore record is open is continuing that incident, not
  restarting". It "resumes at the first step the record does not mark", and "**A marked step does
  not run again**".
- `STO-54`'s step (2) names only `queued` rows and `suspend_tenant` parents ("every `queued` create,
  install and rescue inventory is moved to `needs_reconciliation`"). No text says whether
  `OPS-15`'s pass over `running` rows is part of step (2) or runs at every startup.
- `Restore.lean` keeps `passDone` across `Event.crash` (`afterCrash` resets only `fault`, `now` and
  `locked`). So in the model a successor's `startupPass` changes nothing, and `claim` takes only
  `queued` rows.
- CNF-358's restore-control case "after the freeze lifts while the record remains open" is about the
  restored backup row only.

A concrete case:

1. A restore lands. The engine marks steps (1) to (3), and the freeze lifts at `grace_ends_at`; the
   record stays open, waiting on `STO-56`'s close rule.
2. A customer creates a machine. The worker claims it and commits step 8.
3. The engine crashes while the order is in flight.
4. The successor starts with the record open, so it is continuing the incident.
   - **Engine A** runs `OPS-15`'s pass. The create goes to `needs_reconciliation`; pv-k4l's null
     exception is off while the record is open.
   - **Engine B** reads step (2) as marked and skips the pass. The create stays `running` with no
     worker behind it, and its commitment stays held.

Question: on a startup while a restore record is open, does `OPS-15`'s pass over `running` rows run
whatever the record marks? If it does, the restore exceptions still apply: the frozen
`suspend_tenant` exception, and pv-k4l's create exception staying off. Does `Restore.lean`'s crash
then need to reset `passDone`?
close_reason: Landed in 20d9c26, 204e4e3 and 0169178: OPS-15's pass over running rows runs at every startup, step (2)'s mark keeps only its own work from running again, and Restore.lean separates the process pass from the record's mark (passEveryStartup, successor_sweeps_running). Follow-ups: pv-ymjo, pv-ap89 (0d03081).

title: The citation gate does not check a quote attributed by a bare possessive
description:
Raised by the opus Reviewer of the pv-vwe.30 / pv-vwe.27 Run, 2026-10-02, by running the gate's own `find()`.

## What was found

`tools/check_citations.py`'s `ATTRIB` matches a speech verb ("`X` says …") or the possessive-noun
form ("`X`'s rule that …"). A possessive followed directly by a quote — `` `LDG-72`'s "the greatest
`increment end` among that subject's rows" `` — matches neither, so the quote is not checked.
Reproduced on `CNF-216`'s 2026-10-02 clause: with "greatest" changed to "smallest" the gate stays
green; the same misquote behind "`LDG-72` says" is refused. The shape is what the Run's briefs
recommend for long sentences, and it already occurs across `11-open-findings.md`, `02-`, `05-`,
`13-` and the ADRs, so those quotes rest on hand checks only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A quote of four or more words directly after `` `X`'s `` is checked against X's body, or the
      gate's docstring names the shape under "what this does not catch" with the reason
- [ ] If checked: a negative control (a misquote in that shape is red), and the standing residue
      ratcheted rather than failed outright

import types,os
rev='85ae85856fe6494cc0d5fb80f5e48613727fe83a'
c=types.ModuleType('citations_at_first_closure')
c.__file__=os.path.abspath('tools/check_citations.py')
exec(subprocess.check_output(['git','show',rev+':tools/check_citations.py'],text=True), c.__dict__)
bare=re.compile(r'`((?:%s)-\d+[a-z]?)`\'s\s+(?=["“])' % c.NS)

def measure(texts,docs,adrs,reqs):
 rows=[]; skipped=[]

  for sent in c.chunks(t):

    rid=m.group(1); quote=c.norm(quotes[m.end()])

    row=dict(file=f,attribution=rid,quote=quote,

title: PRV-13b's "no declared traffic bound" is undecided for a null descriptor traffic_bound with an offer-reported value (PRV-44, CNF-241)
description:
`PRV-13b` says "An offer with no declared traffic bound MUST NOT be sold". `PRV-44` lets the
descriptor give `traffic_bound` per offer "or explicit `null` where no bound is declared", and says
"Like `cancellation_bound`, it MAY be reported on the offer instead". `DOM-9`'s offer field is "The
offer's declared traffic limit". For the cancellation bound, `PRV-31` names both sources: "if either
its descriptor-declared bound or its offer-reported bound is". For traffic, no sentence says whether
an offer-reported value counts as "declared" under `PRV-13b` when the descriptor's entry is `null`.

Example: a descriptor declares `traffic_bound: null` for an offer, and the driver's List offers
result reports `traffic_bound: unlimited` on it. One engine reads the offer's report as the declared
bound and sells the offer. Another reads the descriptor's `null` as "no declared traffic bound" and
refuses `offer_not_sellable` at admission. The same split recurs at `OPS-43`'s claim-time sale
re-test.

`CNF-241` case (b) (`pv-hsm`, 526acea) encodes the first reading: "With the descriptor's
`traffic_bound` for the named offer explicit `null` … the offer reports `traffic_bound: unlimited`
at API acceptance." An engine on the second reading refuses that create at the API, so the case
never reaches the queue and the engine fails it.

Question: does an offer-reported `traffic_bound` satisfy `PRV-13b`'s "declared" when the
descriptor's entry is `null`? Triage with `pv-2s6`, which owns the case where both sources give a
value.

Found as follow-up (c) on `pv-hsm` (review-fix Run, 526acea), confirmed in the post-Run review
2026-10-16. Pre-existing at admission. 96cddcb's case (b) left the descriptor unstated; the review
fix narrowed its dependency to this one reading. Requirement text and conformance only.
close_reason: Defined declared traffic bounds and the refused null-descriptor case; gates and citation plant verified.

title: CNF-362 drives no later stop during an in-flight record transaction, so OPS-21's no-repeat clause for a sent record transaction is unchecked (OPS-21, OPS-49, CNF-362)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during the two-axis review of the pv-ay3 + pv-gq8 + pv-vkb batch (branch `pv-ay3-gq8-vkb`), 2026-10-20.*

`CNF-362` checks the later-stop exit before a record's first transaction and while `OPS-49` repeats it, but never with a record transaction in flight, so an engine that re-sends that transaction after the later stop passes conformance.

- `OPS-21` says "A later stop, one arriving after the stop being recorded and before that record lands, ends the record as an exit without worker classification at any point: before the record's first transaction, during it, or while `OPS-49` repeats it; the worker MUST NOT repeat a record transaction already sent when that later stop arrives."
- `OPS-21` says "The sent transaction's fate is the server's: `OPS-49` says "the server decides every statement's fate before the client does"."
- `CNF-362`'s later-stop cases deliver the stop "before the record's first transaction is sent" and "while `OPS-49` repeats the cut-off record's transaction, with the store refusing every transaction until after that later stop". Neither has a transaction in flight when the stop arrives.

Example: a deploy stops the engine while a create's cut-off record transaction is in flight at the store. A second stop arrives before the reply.
- Engine A exits at once; the server commits or refuses the sent statement, and restart recovery under `OPS-15` reads whatever landed.
- Engine B re-sends the transaction after the later stop, against the MUST NOT above. Both pass `CNF-362` today.

Fix shape: a `CNF-362` case that delivers a later stop with one record transaction in flight, for each record, and asserts the engine sends no further transaction and exits; the row is then either settled by that one transaction or still `running`, with restart recovery under `OPS-15` in the second case. The pv-gq8 Run declined to write it because the assertion is an either/or on the server's result (pv-gq8 comment 733). Check strength only; no requirement change. (`OPS-21`, `OPS-49`, `OPS-15`, `CNF-362`)
close_reason: CNF-362 now delivers a later stop with each record's transaction in flight: no transaction after it, engine exit, either outcome accepted (OPS-21, OPS-15). Implemented by hand on branch pv-oes; quote plant red.
