title: PRV-47's driver rejection has no error kind, so OPS-43's step-7 failure has no classification (OPS-11, CNF-342)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during review of pv-14b (2026-10-17).*

`PRV-47`'s driver rejection names no error kind. Since `pv-14b` it runs at `OPS-43`'s step 7,
and `OPS-43` says "The first failing check stops subsequent checks; its owning classification
governs disposition". `PRV-47` gives that check nothing to classify: "the driver MUST validate
every value it forwards to the provider, including provider options, and MUST reject invalid
values without any provider mutation for that create". `CNF-342` asserts the step-7 rejection
and no mutation, but no kind, reason or `retryable`.

Two engines that each conform:
- Engine A fails it `invalid_request` with `retryable: false`, settles `failed` under `OPS-11`'s
  create row ("otherwise `failed`") and releases the commitment under `LDG-39`.
- Engine B reports it as a driver `provider` error with no upstream status. `OPS-11` calls that
  ambiguous ("the error kind is `provider` *and* the upstream status was 5xx, or no upstream
  status was recorded at all"), so the create goes to `needs_reconciliation`. With no correlator
  entry yet, `OPS-27`'s last row makes it **Unresolved** and pages an operator.

The caller sees a permanent refusal from one engine and an operator case from the other, for a
create that made no provider mutation on either.

Pre-existing: `PRV-47` never named a kind. `pv-14b` placed the check and made precedence explicit.
Sibling of `pv-p3k` (no kind for `allow_orders`), which does not reach `PRV-47`.

title: PRV-10's allow_orders refusal has no error kind, at admission or when ordering is switched off before claim (API-15, DOM-16, OPS-23, CNF-55)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

`PRV-10`: "create MUST reject the request unless the request's provider options carry an explicit
purchase acknowledgement, *and* the account is configured to allow ordering." `API-15` and
`CNF-55` repeat the rule. None of the three names an error kind, `details` or `retryable` for the
configuration half. `allow_orders` is per-account configuration (`00-overview.md`'s configuration
table, `DOM-16`), so a restart with changed configuration can turn it off while a create sits
queued between API acceptance and claim. `OPS-23` makes the worker repeat the check: "Validation
that was performed at the API boundary MUST be repeated in the worker before the driver is
called". `pv-14b` places that repeat before `OPS-43`'s List offers read, but the claim-time failure
has no kind either.

`DOM-16` says ordering capabilities "SHOULD be conditional on an explicit per-account
`allow_orders` configuration flag". An engine that follows it fails at the capability gate, and
`DOM-10` says a capability check failure "MUST return an" `unsupported` error "naming the provider
account and the capability". An engine that doesn't follow it fails under `PRV-10` with whatever
kind it picks.

Example: a create is admitted on an account with `allow_orders: true`, and the operator turns the
flag off before a worker claims it. Engine A fails it `unsupported`, naming the account and the
capability. Engine B fails it `invalid_request`, and engine C `conflict`/`state`. Each picks its
own `retryable`, and both values have a reading, since the operator can turn the flag back on. A
caller that obeys `retryable` re-sends on one engine and stops on another. Admission already
diverges the same way.

Question: what kind, `details` and `retryable` does an `allow_orders` refusal carry at admission,
and does the claim-time repeat keep them?

The acknowledgement half is a field the caller supplies, so owner decision 2 on `pv-14b` already
covers it at claim. This bead is the configuration half only. `pv-14b` places the check and leaves
its kind here.

Found by panel r55 (opus, raised unasked), `docs/research/panels-2026-10/r55/synthesis.md`.
Pre-existing.

title: Apply ADR-0037 Q34: the committing settlement makes the one post-order read; LDG-33 home; operator attach writes null
description:
Apply ADR-0037's clarification of 2026-10-15 (owner decision Q34): "once" counts from the settlement that
commits. Panel: docs/research/panels-2026-10/r52/ (read synthesis.md, fable.md and opus.md, which name the
edits). Raised by the PR #3 codex review ("Make the one-shot read crash-recoverable").

Read the clarification first; it is the decision. Work order (requirement text and conformance only):

1. `PRV-13c` (02-provider-contract.md): the "MUST NOT be retried; a resolution pass, a refresh and the sweep MUST
   NOT read that machine's cancellation constraint again" sentence becomes: the pass whose landed-order
   transaction commits makes the one read, after its confirming read, and does not repeat it; an interrupted
   worker's read is discarded with the rest of its outcome (quote `OPS-49`'s "the outcome in hand is thrown
   away"); once the store holds the machine row, a resolution pass, a refresh and the sweep MUST NOT read its
   cancellation constraint. Keep the `PRV-13` pointer. Replace "retried" with "repeated" (`CONTEXT.md` defines
   **Retry** as an operator act).
2. `PRV-13c`: a settlement with no confirming read — the operator's synchronous `observed` attach (`WIR-35`) —
   makes no post-order read and stores the date as null. Quote `WIR-35` for the verb.
3. `OPS-27` (03-operation-lifecycle.md), the 2026-10-15 landed-order placement sentence: the column write is "the
   date of a successful read the committing pass holds, otherwise null", by quoting `PRV-13c`.
4. `LDG-33` (12-billing-and-ledger.md): its formula's cost-through-earliest-date term gains "or, where
   `machines.earliest_cancellation_date` is null, through the offer's declared bound (`PRV-31`)"; `PRV-13c`'s "On
   failure, the declared bound MUST remain the priced term" then quotes `LDG-33` as its home. Keep v1's result
   (zero: the v1 bound is the provider's today). If a rendered region or Lean model carries `LDG-33`'s formula,
   keep it in step (ADR-0025).
5. `CNF-356` (10-conformance-checklist.md): add crash cases — kill the engine after a successful post-order
   read and before the landed-order commit, and again after a failed read; assert the committing resolution pass
   makes one read after its confirming read and writes that date (or null on its own failure) with the machine
   row, and that no read follows settlement. Assert the operator `observed` attach makes no constraint read and
   writes null. Replace "exactly one `GET /server/{n}/cancellation` for each create" with the per-committing-pass
   count.

Out of scope: anything else; other beads.

Rules: quote, don't restate (AGENTS.md "Cite the owner"), in the form the citation gate checks
(`` `ID` says "…" ``, four or more words); RFC 2119 keywords; dated amendment markers on each changed
requirement. Gates: `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` unpiped, exit 0.

title: RSC-26's 'declare an offer unsellable' is neither API-7's sale verdict nor DOM-9's strategy gate (CNF-206)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during review of pv-14b (2026-10-17).*

`RSC-26` uses "unsellable" in a sense that `API-7`'s verdict does not cover. It says "The driver
MUST prefer WWN where the provider exposes it and MUST declare an offer unsellable for `raw_disk`
and `rootfs_via_rescue` where no per-device unique identifier is available at all". `CNF-206`
asserts "an offer whose devices expose no unique identifier is unsellable for rescue installs".

The sale refusal is `API-7`'s create-tail verdict. A create fails `offer_not_sellable` "when the
named offer is not sellable under `PRV-13b` or `PRV-31`, or absent from the offers the check
reads". Neither condition is `RSC-26`'s. Strategy eligibility sits elsewhere. `DOM-9`'s
`install_strategies` is "The offer's subset of `DOM-13`'s strategies, which **gates** them
(`WIR-30`)", and "empty means no install is available for it". The offer itself stays sellable.

Two engines that each conform:
- Engine A omits `raw_disk` and `rootfs_via_rescue` from the offer's `install_strategies` and
  sells the machine. A later rescue install is refused by the strategy gate.
- Engine B reads "declare an offer unsellable" literally. It withholds the offer from sale, or
  refuses the create `offer_not_sellable`, so the customer cannot buy a machine they could have
  used with `provider_native`.

Decide which mechanism `RSC-26` means, then align `CNF-206`. Pre-existing. Found as follow-up 8 of
the `pv-14b` Run (2026-10-17).

title: check_citations.py does not check a colon-form quote (AGENTS.md 'Quote the sentence')
description:
> *This was generated by AI during review of pv-14b (2026-10-17).*

`tools/check_citations.py` cannot catch a misquote written in the colon form,
`` `X`: "..." ``. Its docstring scopes the check: "REACH: a quote is checked only when its SPLIT
chunk carries an ATTRIB match (a speech verb, or `X`'s <noun> that) before it, or is directly
after a bare possessive (`X`'s "four or more words")". The colon form is neither, and the
docstring does not name it as a deliberate limit.

The set uses the colon form heavily. A naive regex finds about 41 in the root documents, and
`pv-14b`'s diff (06cd56d) added more, e.g. `PRV-40`: "the worker MUST read the stored closure…" in
`OPS-43`. In the `pv-14b` Run's Round 1, a misquote attributed to `OPS-15` in this form passed a
green gate run. Only a manual fixed-string check caught it. Every quote in 06cd56d then had to be
checked by hand.

This is check strength, not engine divergence. `AGENTS.md`'s "Quote the sentence" rule is enforced
only for the forms REACH names. Either check the colon form or name it in REACH as unchecked, the
same choice `pv-n9p` offered for the possessive form. Related: `pv-sgj` (closed) recorded
colon-form quotes as a follow-up only. `pv-erp` is a different QUOTED defect.

Found as follow-up 14 of the `pv-14b` Run (2026-10-17).

title: A promoted asynchronous standby can lose committed writes, and no text says whether bringing the engine up on it is a restart or a restore (STO-5, STO-54)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage of pv-k4l (panels r56 and r56b, 2026-10-17).*

An engine brought up on a promoted asynchronous standby may be running on a store that lost writes the
primary had committed. No text says whether that is a restart or a restore.

- `STO-54`'s durability posture: "The deployment runs asynchronous streaming replication and continuous
  WAL archiving". Synchronous commit covers only "the deposit mint and `STO-30`'s payment-credit
  transaction", with "`local` everywhere else".
- `STO-5` covers "process restart" and excludes only "A restore from backup". `STO-54` governs "A store
  restored from backup".
- The requirement documents never mention a promotion or a failover; `standby` appears only for the
  synchronous standby's name.

Read as a restart, a promotion that lost writes runs `STO-54`'s own failure cases, for example:

1. At 10:00:00 a create is claimed.
2. At 10:00:01 it commits its correlator entry (`OPS-43` step 8) with `local` durability.
3. At 10:00:02 it sends the order.
4. At 10:00:03 the primary dies before the standby has received the step-8 write, and the standby is
   promoted.
5. On the new primary the create is `queued` or `running` with no entry:
   - If it is `queued`, `OPS-15` leaves it alone, so it is claimed again and orders a second time. This is
     `STO-54`'s "a `queued` create that already ordered in Δ orders again (on a restart `OPS-15` inspects
     `running` rows only)".
   - If it is `running`, pv-k4l's new `OPS-15` exception would settle it `failed` and release its
     commitment, though the order went out.

Question: is an engine brought up on a promoted standby that may have lost committed writes in a
`STO-54` restore incident? If so, how does the deployment open that incident before the engine starts?

pv-k4l's exception is stated as off on such a store whatever this bead decides, so pv-k4l does not wait on
it. This bead owns the general classification, which also reaches `queued` creates and `STO-54`'s other
examples (a lost extension, a revoked token, a `suspend_tenant` fan-out).

Found by opus in panel r56 (`docs/research/panels-2026-10/r56/synthesis.md`, "Gaps found beyond the
brief"). In r56b opus's draft edit made every promotion a full `STO-54` incident; that edit stayed in the
reader's clone and is not landed. Pre-existing.
close_reason: Landed in cb8345e and a51ce6c: every commit waits for one of two synchronous standbys, each new connection is checked, and a promotion is a restart only for the standby STO-54's report puts further ahead (ADR-0045). Restore-instant follow-up: pv-3jw6 (d291613).

pv-k4l's `OPS-15` create exception now has an off-switch that depends on this bead. `OPS-15` says
"It does not fire while a restore record is open (`STO-54`, `STO-56`), nor on a store that may have
lost committed writes, such as a promoted asynchronous standby".

Two points for triage:

1. **There is no conformance item for the lost-writes off-switch.** No text says how a deployment
   recognises such a store, so nothing can drive the case. pv-k4l's round 2 removed the assertions
   in CNF-29 and CNF-358 that could not be driven. Whatever this bead decides should add the case.
2. **The lost-writes condition has no end, and the restore one does.** `OPS-15` bounds the restore
   exclusion: "This restriction lasts for the whole open incident, independently of the freeze's
   end." The lost-writes exclusion states no end. Two engines could diverge on every later restart
   of a promoted store, not only the first. Suppose one engine fires the exception while the store
   may still lack the step-8 write. It fails a create whose order the provider holds, releases its
   commitment, and leaves the order orphaned.

title: OPS-23's missing-field kinds stop at create, install, power and delete (OPS-11: rescue inventory, reverse-DNS, release attachment, refresh)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during review of pv-14b (2026-10-17).*

`OPS-23`'s missing-field kinds cover four operation kinds. The rest are not addressed. `pv-14b`
(decision 2, panel r55b) added "For create, install, power and delete, a missing required field
MUST fail as follows", with two cases:
- `conflict`/`"incomplete_record"`, `retryable: true`, for a field the `api` writes at admission;
- `invalid_request` naming the field, `retryable: false`, for a field the caller supplies.

`OPS-23`'s own rule, "A field a previous-release `api` may not have written is a deterministic
failure in the worker, never a passed check", applies to every operation kind. The remaining
worker-run kinds in `OPS-11`'s table are:
- rescue inventory ("Same rows as `install`");
- reverse-DNS and release attachment (the create row);
- refresh ("Always `failed`").

None of these has a kind for a missing field.

Two engines that each conform: for a reverse-DNS record missing an `api`-written field, engine A
fails `invalid_request` with `retryable: false`, and engine B applies the create rule by analogy
and fails `conflict`/`incomplete_record` with `retryable: true`. A caller's retry decision differs.

Rescue inventory also gets no marker-timing rule or `rescue_exit` value. `OPS-23` gives an install
both: "these checks MUST run before either `OPS-45` marker is written" and `rescue_exit: "none"`.

Decide whether the two cases extend to every worker-run operation kind, and what rescue
inventory's outcome is. Found as follow-up 10 of the `pv-14b` Run (2026-10-17).

title: Establish held exclusion for the queued auction-offer removal check (CNF-342)
description:
The queued auction-offer removal arm of `CNF-342` needs triage for a potentially vacuous exclusion-release check. This is separate from the missing-acknowledgement case strengthened by pv-5hnq.

`CNF-342` starts: "Run on `CNF-241`'s `correlator: per_order_key` ordering channel." Its older offer-removal paragraph says: "For a valid request, remove the named auction offer after admission and before claim" and "Repeat for an ordinary catalogue offer removed in that same window." Its release assertion remains "the resource-offer exclusion freed where the create holds one."

`PRV-44` lists each ordering channel's `correlator: operation_id | per_order_key | none` and `offer_is_resource: true | false`. `CNF-241` specifies “on a `correlator: per_order_key` ordering channel”; it does not pin that resource flag. The offer-removal paragraph does not explicitly establish an `offer_is_resource` channel or a held exclusion for the auction fixture. The catalogue control intentionally has none: `CNF-342` says "A catalogue create takes no resource-offer exclusion."

Check-strength risk: a per-order-key fixture with no held resource-offer exclusion can satisfy the conditional release assertion without exercising exclusion release at the queued auction-offer refusal. A build leaking only that exclusion may therefore pass this arm. `CNF-342` now requires “assert this create's exclusion for its provider account, ordering channel and offer id is held at admission”; this does not establish held state for the separate offer-removal fixture.

Triage whether the auction-removal arm must explicitly establish the resource-offer channel and held exclusion while keeping the catalogue control on an appropriate separate fixture. No wording or repair is adopted here; no requirement, checklist, descriptor policy or gate is changed. Owners for triage: `CNF-342`, `CNF-241`, `PRV-44`, `PRV-42`, `STO-58`.

title: check_citations.py's sentence splitter does not break on a sentence that ends inside markup
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## The defect

`tools/check_citations.py`'s `SPLIT` is

    re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n\s*[-*]\s+|\n\s*\n|\n(?=\|)")

The lookbehind wants the character immediately before the whitespace to be a sentence ender. It is
not, whenever the sentence closes inside markup: `happen.**"` ends with `"`, `it does.*` ends with
`*`, `` runs.` `` ends with a backtick. Those sentences do not break, so one chunk carries an
attribution verb for one requirement and then a later citation's quote, and `find()` blames the
verb's requirement for words it does not contain.

## Measured

One entry in `tools/citation-baseline.json`'s `quoted_attributions` is this defect.
`tools/formal/Provisiond/Admission.lean:603-605`:

> `LDG-62` grows the commitment "from available balance at the **current** rate", and `LDG-59` says
> "**Falling back to the last known rate MUST NOT happen.**" A purchase priced at an unknown rate is
> what create's row halts for, and the extension is "authorized like a purchase".

The sentence closes at `happen.**"`; the lookbehind sees `"` and does not fire; `LDG-62`'s
"authorized like a purchase" lands in `LDG-59`'s chunk and is reported against `LDG-59`.

**The other two entries are NOT this defect** and this ticket does not retire them. The two spans
blamed on `LDG-40` at `Admission.lean:773-776` are one English sentence whose only `.` is its last
character; there is no sentence ending inside it for any lookbehind to miss. Their cause is
`find()`'s `owner = rid` — one attribution verb owns every quote in its chunk — over a single
sentence citing two requirements. Widening the ownership rule was considered for `pv-vwe.18` and
rejected: it reintroduces the inverted-attribution class `find()`'s own comment records
("`STO-43` says `STO-14` 'reaches settled operations'" is STO-43's sentence *about* STO-14).
Those two have no exit today, by decision.

## Shape

Widen the lookbehind to allow closing markup between the sentence ender and the whitespace —
`(?<=[.!?])[*`"”)\]]*\s+` or equivalent — and re-run. The Markdown surface is clean under the
current splitter, so any change there is a regression; check it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SPLIT` breaks a sentence that ends inside closing markup
- [ ] Every `*.md` still clean; the `--selftest` WIR-1 known-positive still fires
- [ ] The `LDG-59` entry is gone from `citation-baseline.json`'s `quoted_attributions`; the note
      no longer names this ticket as the two `LDG-40` entries' exit
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green

"Naming the field" has no wire form. `WIR-9a` says `details` "keys are defined per kind, not left

Three engines that conform:
- Engine A puts the name in `details.field`.
- Engine B puts it in another `details` key.
- Engine C writes it only in `message`, which is what `WIR-9a` exists to prevent ("routing a value
  through `message` ... forces an agent to parse English").

Two cases have no stated form either:
- a value nested inside `provider_options`: is the name `provider_options` or a path under it?
- several rejected values in one create: `WIR-2` picks "the first unknown field", but `PRV-47`
  and `OPS-23` give no order.

So `CNF-342`'s provider-options fixture and `CNF-34`'s caller-field case have no defined expected
value.

Found by the local review of `pv-p1y` (findings 2 and 5) and the `pv-p1y` Run's follow-up comment.

- if `tools/formal/` moves or is renamed, `load_lean_docstrings()` returns `{}` silently and every
  baselined signature goes unmatched — the whole Lean surface stops being checked with no red.

Both print a visible mismatch (`Lean quoted attributions: 2, none new against baseline 3`) and
neither fails. `check_citations.py`'s own docstring already holds the standard this falls short of,
for the index: "a missing index is a red gate, not a skipped rule."

The `unquoted_attributions` baseline has the same gap, so this is a widening rather than a
correction, which is why it was not folded into `pv-vwe.18`.

## Shape

Fail when a baselined signature is not among the current findings, for both baselines, naming the
entry to delete. That makes "may shrink, never grow" a thing the gate enforces instead of a thing
the note asserts, and gives the silent-skip case the treatment a missing index already gets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A baselined signature that no longer fires makes the gate exit 1 and names the stale entry
- [ ] Emptying `tools/formal/` of `.lean` files is red, not green
- [ ] HEAD is green with no stale entries in either baseline
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green

The bootstrap at the end of `main()` still rewrites `citation-baseline.json` from scratch when

The damage is loud rather than silent (the next run goes red with three findings) and the trigger
needs a hand-mangled file, which is why it is filed here rather than fixed in `pv-vwe.18`.

title: RSC-46's "ASCII whitespace" is undefined, and common definitions disagree on U+000B (RSC-46, CNF-363)
description:
Found during the `pv-6p8` drain review (branch `pv-6p8`), 2026-10-22. This is the reviewed form's out-of-scope bullet about pinning "ASCII whitespace" to U+0009–U+000D plus U+0020. Two readers proposed it in r61c.

**The problem.** `RSC-46` normalizes an identifier with "trim ASCII whitespace, ASCII-lowercase, then strip exactly one leading `0x`", and the wire values are "trimmed of ASCII whitespace". The set doesn't define "ASCII whitespace", and common definitions disagree on U+000B (vertical tab):
- WHATWG Infra's "ASCII whitespace" is U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D and U+0020. It excludes U+000B.
- C `isspace` and Python `bytes.strip()` include U+000B.

The trimmed value is what the wire shows, what matching compares, and what the `inventory_fingerprint` hashes.

**Example.** A disk's serial is read as `"ABC123\v"`. Engine A trims it to `ABC123`. Engine B keeps `ABC123\v`. They show different `serial` and `identifier` values and compute different fingerprints over the same disks. `CNF-363` case (2) asserts the fingerprint "equals an independently computed hash". Its outcome then depends on which definition the conformance suite uses.

**Question.** Pin "ASCII whitespace" in `RSC-46`, for example to U+0009–U+000D plus U+0020, or cite a definition?

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** exact trimming policy, technically unanimous

**Owner decision:** “Approve E (Recommended)” (`owner-decisions-1030.md`, item 12). Adopted exact form: `docs/research/panels-2026-10/r84/r84b/check/tally/q3-E.md:4`.

**Current behavior:**

`06-rescue-install.md:312` at `3109b5b44eae17e288cf52aaa976993bd8c5626c`:

```text
**RSC-46** **Identifier normalization and the fingerprint's canonical form.** Before comparison,
an identifier — a caller's `target.identifier`, a `layout.drives[].identifier`, or a value read
from the inventory — is normalized in this order: trim ASCII whitespace, ASCII-lowercase, then
strip exactly one leading `0x`. A value that is empty after normalization is absent and matches
nothing. Matching uses the normalized values and tries the WWN first, then the serial; a WWN
match and a serial match naming different devices aborts `integrity` before any write (`RSC-26`).
Each device on the wire carries `identifier`, `wwn` and `serial`. The `wwn` and `serial` values
are the strings as read, trimmed of ASCII whitespace, or `null` where normalization leaves
nothing. The `identifier` is byte-equal to `wwn` if that is non-null, else `serial`, else `null`.
The `inventory_fingerprint` is SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the device list, each
element exactly `{wwn, serial, size_bytes}` using normalized values and `null` where a value is
absent. The list is sorted by each element's RFC 8785 serialization, compared as UTF-8 byte
strings. Identical elements are kept, one per device. Device paths are excluded, because they
are the unstable part. On the wire the fingerprint is 64 lowercase hex characters.
(`WIR-20`, `WIR-10b`)
```

**Desired behavior / key interfaces:**

Insert in RSC-46 immediately after its bold heading and before “Before comparison,”:

```text
Here ASCII whitespace means exactly U+0009, U+000A, U+000B, U+000C, U+000D and U+0020;
trimming removes only a maximal prefix and suffix of those code points, never interior
characters or any other code point. This definition applies to normalization and to
trimming the as-read wire values in this requirement.
```


**Acceptance criteria:**

Insert in CNF-363 after its numbered cases and the selected size paragraph, before its final owner-reference line:

```text
      **Whitespace boundaries.** Apply `RSC-46`'s exact trimming set to the caller
      fields and to both inventory WWN and serial. For each of U+0009, U+000A,
      U+000B, U+000C, U+000D and U+0020, independently surround `0XAb` with that
      character: the as-read wire value is `0XAb`, the normalized hash value is
      `ab`, and both its wire echo and `ab` resolve the unique disk under both
      install strategies. A caller value consisting only of that character is
      refused `invalid_request` before enqueue; an inventory value consisting
      only of it is absent and shown `null`. U+0008, U+000E, U+001F, U+007F and
      U+00A0 at the edges are retained on the wire and in normalized values;
      their presence prevents stripping a later `0x` that is not leading.
      Interior occurrences of every tested character are preserved. Separately
      test serial-only and WWN-only one-disk reports, `size_bytes: 1024`:
      independently construct the normalized one-element device list, whose
      element is exactly `{wwn, serial, size_bytes}`, and the RFC 8785 canonical
      bytes of that list, including its enclosing array brackets. Compute
      SHA-256 over those list bytes and assert that `inventory_fingerprint`
      equals the digest encoded as 64 lowercase hex characters. The reference
      must not call the engine's trim, normalization, serialization or
      fingerprint helpers. (`RSC-46`, `API-13`)
```

Everything else remains pinned.


**Out of scope:**

`docs/research/panels-2026-10/r84/r84b/owner-questions.md:20`:

> **Scope of approval:** exact `check/tally/q3-E.md`, without adding a required identity value to the separate one-disk hash fixtures or mandating their cross-product with every boundary value. The printed explicit boundary assertions all remain. No claim of compatibility with every provider identity or outside library convention is made.

title: Persist the declared cancellation bound for LDG-33's null-date fallback (PR #3 codex P2)
description:
Persist the declared cancellation bound the create was sized from, for LDG-33's null-date fallback.

Raised by the PR #3 codex review (P2, round on 94dba30, thread on 12-billing-and-ledger.md LDG-33): "When the
post-order constraint read fails and this column is null, later re-derivations cannot obtain the create-time
declared bound required here. The durable machine schema in `05-persistence.md` stores only `offer_id`, while
its closed `request_summary` offer snapshot omits `cancellation_bound`; the live offer may subsequently change
or disappear, and the operation is eventually deleted."

Why deferred from PR #3 (owner's "merge when ready", 2026-10-15): no v1 effect. Every v1 Robot offer's declared
bound is the provider's today (08-provider-notes.md "Launch-set cancellation declaration"; ADR-0037 Q25 makes a
later bound unsellable), and LDG-33 prices the fallback "only if later than provider-local today", so the term is
zero for every v1 machine whichever offer terms are read. It matters once an offer with a later bound is sold, or
an offer's declared bound changes under machines already sold.

Work order: give the fallback a durable source — e.g. a `machines` column written in OPS-27's landed-order
transaction from the bound PRV-31 sized the commitment with (all three entry points; null for the operator
observed attach), or the bound in the operation's request summary carried onto the machine — and make LDG-33 /
PRV-13c quote it; CNF-356 asserts the fallback uses the stored bound after the offer changes. Needs an ADR-0037
note if it changes what is stored. Requirement text and conformance only.

Gates green.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Give `LDG-33`'s null-date fallback a durable source: store the declared cancellation bound on the machine row when the machine is attached.

This brief is the contract. Where it differs from the description's work order, the brief wins. In particular, the description's "null for the operator observed attach" is wrong; see Desired behavior.

**Current behavior:**
`LDG-33`'s `protected_sats` prices the earliest-date term "or, where `machines.earliest_cancellation_date` is null, through the offer's declared bound (`PRV-31`)". `PRV-13c` quotes that line. Nothing durable holds that bound:
- The `machines` row keeps only `offer_id` from the offer, "retained as the **provenance** record". The install gate's rule is "MUST NOT re-resolve the offer". Elsewhere an offer is "a live provider listing ... it can be re-priced, withdrawn, or have its terms changed".
- `STO-50`'s closed enumeration of the create's offer snapshot in `request_summary` (`offer_id`, `install_strategies`, recurring price, currency and period, setup fee, prepaid first unit with `billing_unit.seconds`) does not include the bound.
- The operation, and its summary with it, is removed by `STO-14`: "remove **settled** operations older than a configured age".
- On Robot's auction channel the listing leaves the feed when it is bought. `08-provider-notes.md` records "each listing left the feed on purchase". `PRV-44` lets a driver put the bound on the offer instead of the descriptor ("which MAY be reported on the offer instead"). So a re-derivation may find no offer to read.

The column is null after a failed post-order read and always after the operator's synchronous `observed` attach (`WIR-35`). On those machines, every later re-derivation needs the bound and has no source for it. In v1 the priced term is zero: Robot's launch bound is the provider's today (`ADR-0037` Q25), and `LDG-33` prices only "if later than provider-local today". The defect is that an implementation must invent the source. It starts mispricing once an offer with a later bound is sold, or once an offer's terms change under machines already sold.

**Desired behavior:**
- **Snapshot at accept.** The create's offer snapshot in `request_summary` carries the declared cancellation bound that the admitting transaction sized the commitment with. It is the bound resolved to a provider-local date at acceptance, in `PRV-13`'s day-only representation ("a day-only value MUST be stored as the UTC instant at the start of that day in the provider's date zone"). Where the descriptor's `cancellation_bound` and the offer-reported bound both exist, the snapshot holds the later of the two. `PRV-31` refuses the sale if "either" is later than today, so the later one is the worst case the sale admitted.
- **Copy at attach.** A new nullable `machines` column, `declared_cancellation_bound`, is copied from that snapshot in the same transaction as `offer_id` and never re-resolved. This mirrors `machines.billing_unit_seconds` (`ADR-0033`). The copy is written on every path that writes the machine row from the create:
  - the create's own settlement and the other `OPS-27` landed-order entry points: automatic resolving-observed after a lost order reply, and `OPS-36`'s late attach after `OPS-33` released the commitment;
  - **and the operator's synchronous `observed` attach (`WIR-35`)**. That is the one path where `earliest_cancellation_date` is always null, and `CNF-356` already asserts there that "the earliest-date term is priced from the declared bound under `LDG-33`". The operation is still in `needs_reconciliation`, so its summary still exists.
- **The fallback reads the copy.** `LDG-33`'s fallback prices through `machines.declared_cancellation_bound`. It never reads the live offer, and never the descriptor, at re-derivation. A null `declared_cancellation_bound` contributes no term and MUST NOT fall back to the live offer or the descriptor. No v1 machine can be null, since `PRV-31` makes an offer with no bound unsellable.
- `earliest_cancellation_date` keeps its meaning exactly. Writing the bound into that column is rejected: `PRV-13c` says "After the committing pass's failed post-order read, the column MUST remain null until such a response supplies the date", and the 2026-10-15 r51 clarification makes that null what marks the term unverified in `WIR-11`'s machine view.

**Key interfaces:**
- `STO-50` (the "For a create" bullet) and the `request_summary` row: the offer snapshot gains the declared cancellation bound. This amends a closed enumeration.
- The `machines` table gains `declared_cancellation_bound` (timestamp, nullable). Its row text states the writer (the snapshot copy, at create or at attach, including `WIR-35`), "never re-resolved", and the null-read rule.
- `LDG-33`'s formula line: "through the offer's declared bound (`PRV-31`)" becomes the stored column.
- `PRV-13c`'s sentence that quotes `LDG-33` ("For pricing a null column, `LDG-33` says ...") changes in step, quoting the new words exactly.
- `CNF-356`: new cases as below. Also check `CNF-166` and `CNF-147` for any assertion that prices the term from the live offer.
- `ADR-0037`: a dated amendment note recording this decision (owner, pv-tsb triage, 2026-10-16) and its rejected alternatives: reading the live offer or descriptor at re-derivation, and writing the bound into `earliest_cancellation_date`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `STO-50` and the `request_summary` row name the declared cancellation bound in the create's offer snapshot, including the later-of-both rule.
- [ ] The `machines` table defines `declared_cancellation_bound` with its writer on every attach path (the `OPS-27` entry points, `OPS-36`'s late attach and `WIR-35`'s observed attach), "never re-resolved", and a null read as no term with no live-offer or descriptor fallback.
- [ ] `LDG-33`'s formula names `machines.declared_cancellation_bound` as the fallback source, and `PRV-13c`'s quote of that line matches the new text word for word.
- [ ] `CNF-356` gains a case: sell from an offer, fail the post-order read, then withdraw the offer from the listing (and, in a separate case, change its reported bound to a later date). On the next re-derivation, assert that the earliest-date term is priced from the stored bound and that no offer or descriptor read supplies it.
- [ ] `CNF-356`'s operator `observed` attach case asserts that `declared_cancellation_bound` is written from the snapshot while `earliest_cancellation_date` is written null.

title: No text says whether a cancelled execute must record its outcome, so a create cancelled after step 8 settles failed or parks by engine choice (OPS-21, OPS-11, OPS-15, CNF-361)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during the pv-qga review.*

No text says whether a cancelled `execute` must record its outcome before the process ends, and
since pv-qga the answer moves a customer's money.

- `OPS-21`: "`execute` MUST be cancellable, and cancellation MUST be treated as an ambiguous
  outcome, except for the create case below." It says nothing about who writes what when a
  cancellation lands.
- `OPS-11`'s create row applies to "Any create failure the worker records before any step-9
  request (before any per-order key upload or order request)". A cancellation the worker records
  is a cut-off `conflict` and settles `failed`.
- The note under `OPS-11`'s table: "A restart in that same window takes the ordinary path (`OPS-15`:
  "the engine MUST move every `running` operation to `needs_reconciliation`"), since the column is
  set."
- `OPS-49`'s retry loop already exits without writing: "A worker cancelled during the retry loop
  stops retrying and exits".

Example: a create is claimed, step 8 commits and is acknowledged (`about_to_order_at` set), and
the engine is shut down before the worker invokes step 9. Nothing was ordered.

- Engine A records the cancellation as a cut-off `conflict`. The create settles `failed` and the
  commitment is released at once.
- Engine B lets the cancellation end the process without a write, as `OPS-49` does inside its
  loop. On restart the column is set, so `OPS-15` moves the create to `needs_reconciliation` and
  the commitment stays held until `OPS-33`'s window.

Both read as conforming. Before step 8 commits the two differ only in the error (a cut-off
`conflict` against `OPS-15`'s restart `internal`); both settle `failed`. Before pv-qga both parked
after step 8 as well.

`CNF-361` already tests as if recording were required: "Also record an `OPS-21` cancellation of
`execute` at each of steps 1-8 on each channel" and then asserts `failed`. Engine B fails that item
on no stated requirement.

Question: must a cancelled `execute` record its outcome (and so settle `failed` before step 9),
or may it exit and leave the row to `OPS-15`? If exiting is allowed, `CNF-361` should test only the
recorded case and say so.

Found in the post-Run review of pv-qga (2026-10-18, spec reviewer). Exposed by pv-qga's create row;
the pre-step-8 kind difference is pv-k4l's.

title: ADR-0033: prepay the first billing unit — requirements, conformance and formal edits
description:
Owner decision Q2 (2026-10-06): `ADR-0033` — a machine's first billing unit is prepaid machine time
at the customer rate, on `LDG-39`'s setup-fee lifecycle, and the meter starts where it ends. Read the
ADR first; it carries the reasons and the rejected alternatives (do not re-litigate them).

Edits owed (the ADR's Consequences list is the source; keep them in step):
- `PRV-44`: per-offer `billing_unit` `{seconds, native_floor}` — a per-contract fact (`PRV-13c`).
- `PRV-13b`: a reserve term for the prepaid unit beside `setup_fee`.
- `LDG-7`: a new entry kind for the prepaid unit (its own kind, not `usage_debit`).
- `LDG-39`: the prepaid unit follows the setup fee's lifecycle table (commit before order, debit on
  confirmed acceptance, release where the provider never charged).
- `LDG-38`: the machine's first seed places its mark at the seed instant plus one unit; re-entries
  inside the unit are discarded by the existing discard rule; an exit inside it clamps to zero.
- `LDG-33`: `runway_until` counts from the later of now and the prepaid unit's end.
- `LDG-75`: the residual (final partial unit after the first; grid straddles) as an accepted
  accounting gap.
- Offer disclosure beside `setup_fee_sats` (`DOM-9` and its wire shape).
- Conformance items for each new MUST (the coverage ratchet will demand them).
- Formal layer: `Provisiond.Runway` (LDG-33), `Provisiond.Period`/`Meter` (first seed), and
  `Provisiond.Funding` (lifecycle with the prepaid entry); a witness pair for the guard "first seed
  is offset by one unit" (refused with, admitted without), and a successful-execution witness.

Acceptance: `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped; every sentence that
asserts what another requirement says carries its quote; the ADR and the requirements agree.

description:
# pv-ucs.10 — branch review residue (two-axis review of 903053d..82bc3d8, 2026-10-11)

Text and consistency repairs found by the review; no new behaviour. Read the then-current text by
identifier. Owner decisions Q23a–c (if any) are in the ticket's latest comment.

## Standards (README *Requirement conventions*, AGENTS.md)
1. Delete markers for wording that never reached master (master = 903053d): `PRV-45`'s "The 2026-10-08
   `ADR-0037` wording restricted the date case to the future…"; `PRV-49`'s "Clarified 2026-10-11"; the
   amendment markers on conformance items created on this branch (CNF-316, CNF-319, CNF-328 ×3 and its
   reversed headline, CNF-329, CNF-343, CNF-345); `OVR-19`'s 2026-10-10 satoshi-form and Q20 clauses and the
   2026-10-09 Q13 note on rows added on this branch (00-overview); `DOM-8`'s "amended 2026-10-10 … Q20"
   (01-domain-model). Keep a marker only where it amends master text; then state the current rule plainly.
2. Delete the tombstone "*Comparison with the former network-restriction refusal removed 2026-10-10
   (`ADR-0038`).*" (04-api-contract); judge 13-wire-contract's "the earlier Cloud fixture was removed…" the
   same way (keep only if a trap sits behind it).
3. `ADR-0034`'s Context quotes `OPS-48` as "Neither returns the attempt to `queued`"; the current text is
   "Neither case returns the attempt to `queued`". Fix the quote.
4. `PRV-13a`'s "this settles batch B step 9 only for that order": name where step 9 is defined
   (`docs/research/provider-verify-2026-10.md` §5).
5. 02's "Amended 2026-10-09 (research V7)": name the ADR or the research file per the convention.
6. Lean: scope `set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000` (Admission.lean) with `set_option … in`.
7. README's identifier-reservation note cites "ADR-0034, Q19" for a rule Q19 does not state; cite the
   ticket/verification record instead.

## Spec consistency
8. `OPS-32` still says "`DOM-8` refreshes that record only on an explicit caller operation, and nothing in
   this set refreshes on a schedule", contradicting its own Q20 present-write; `PRV-43` quotes it. Reword
   both to the Q20 rule.
9. `ProviderTraffic.fresh` requires `observedAt ≤ now`; `DOM-8` treats any observation younger than the
   window as fresh. Make them agree (state the future-timestamp case in DOM-8 or drop the Lean guard).
10. `WIR-35`'s `delete_machine` example `"effective_cancellation_date": "2026-09-12T00:00:00Z"` is a
    start-of-day instant; convert per `PRV-13`'s rule (Europe/Berlin CEST: `2026-09-12T21:59:59Z`) or frame
    it as an explicit provider timestamp.
11. ADR-0039: the descriptor is "Pure and synchronous; it MUST NOT perform network I/O", yet `PRV-13c` says
    "The driver MUST read allowance and overage price from current provider terms, declaring the per-offer
    `traffic_bound` through `PRV-44`", and CNF-340 says "the descriptor follows the current terms". Route an
    allowance offer's bound through List offers (`PRV-44` already allows "reported on the offer instead");
    CNF-340 tests the offer. No field holds an overage price: either add none and say the price is read when
    an allowance offer is re-admitted, or drop "and overage price" — no new field without an owner decision.
12. `PRV-9`: a successful create keeps the caller's key until the next `OPS-32` sweep, wider than ADR-0040's
    "A caller's key held by an unresolved operation blocks that caller's next create". If the ADR does not
    settle deletion at settlement, BLOCK with the passage.
13. `WIR-47`'s withdrawal body `{"status": "unknown"}`: state whether `operator_ref` is refused (WIR-2's
    unknown-field rule) or ignored.
14. `CNF-354` tests "Reject enablement until …", a gate no requirement specifies (`PRV-49`: "does not require
    a runtime refusal API"). Reword CNF-354 to what is testable (the precondition stated and cited), or
    BLOCK if that leaves a MUST without a CNF.
15. `PRV-40`'s declared limit "supplies an alarm threshold" and CNF-344 checks it "is read for … the alarm
    threshold", but the only alarm fires on the provider's 403 (ADR-0036 rejected a local count). Align the
    text with the 403-raised alarm.
16. Resolved, record only: the 10 Gbit uplink cannot be bought through `provider_options` — Robot's
    `GET /order/server/product` and `GET /order/server_market/product` list only `primary_ipv4` as an
    orderable add-on (read-only, 2026-10-11). Note it beside ADR-0039's exclusion in 08-provider-notes.

## Owner decisions Q23a–c (ADR-0037's amendment of 2026-10-11, "a failed read-back's tail, the attachment cap, and the earliest date's instant"; panel r41)
17. Q23a: after a failed or present read-back, state (after `PRV-13`'s read-back branch) that the meter runs to
    `LDG-38`'s stop boundary, time past wind-down is `LDG-74`'s sweep-interval residual ended no later than
    the stored date, and beyond the commitment it meets `LDG-31`'s clamp; add this path to `LDG-31`'s
    reachability list; qualify `LDG-74`'s "maximum time a customer can be billed" for a sweep that yields
    to `rate_limited`; `CNF-64`: exhaust the commitment and fail the read-back — a clamp record, nothing
    taken from available, the stop at the date. No new reserve term; no meter stop at a failed read.
18. Q23b: `LDG-32`'s sale sentence becomes a pointer ("whether an offer may be sold with a billable
    attachment that can outlive its machine is `PRV-49`'s"); `PRV-49` states the accepted residual is
    uncapped (EUR 1.90 a month per stray address until noticed; accident only); `PRV-13b`'s duty to bound
    its own exposure reads with the same exception; align `CNF-354` (see item 14).
19. Q23c: `PRV-13`: a day-only `earliest_cancellation_date` is stored as the start of that day in the zone
    the provider dates in (Robot `Europe/Berlin`, `[verify]`); a date equal to provider-today has passed
    (ordinary branch); cost through a future earliest date runs to that day's end. `PRV-13c` and the
    `05-persistence` column cite it. `CNF-63`: Berlin fixtures (`2026-10-31` → `2026-10-30T23:00:00Z` stored;
    a future date priced through its day's end). `CNF-147`: replace "Size the commitment from the machine's
    read `earliest_cancellation_date`" (contradicts `PRV-31`'s "MUST NOT resize the commitment") with
    pricing the earliest-date term, commitment unchanged.

title: ADR-0034: refresh from cache, reverse-DNS ceiling, provider request budget with a system reserve
description:
Owner decision Q3 (2026-10-06): `ADR-0034` — tenant traffic cannot spend the provider request budget
the system needs. Read the ADR first; it carries the threat (D2r: a `refresh` loop on one machine
drains Hetzner Cloud's 3600 requests/hour per project, and throttled exhaustion deletes stall under
`OPS-48`), the reasons and the rejected alternatives (do not re-litigate them).

Edits owed (the ADR's Consequences list is the source; keep them in step):
- Refresh answered from the cache: a refresh of a machine whose `state_observed_at` is within the
  stated freshness window settles without a provider call (`DOM-8`, `OPS-11`'s refresh row, the
  refresh endpoint's contract in `04-api-contract.md`).
- `SEC-39`: reverse-DNS gains a per-principal ceiling; a write of the value already held settles
  without a provider call.
- `PRV-44`: a declared request limit per credential scope beside `order_budget`; `PRV-40` generalised
  (or a sibling requirement) so the deployment spends it before any provider call, may lower it and
  never raise it.
- The reserve: a stated share for `OPS-39` episodes, `OPS-27` resolution and `OPS-32`'s sweep; a
  tenant-initiated operation is refused deterministically before its first provider call once only
  the reserve remains; admission is decided once per operation, and a later request of an admitted
  operation is never refused locally.
- `OVR-19` rows: freshness window, request budget, reserve share.
- Conformance items for each new MUST; an alarm on tenant-share exhaustion.
- Formal layer: `Provisiond.Admission`'s ceiling map gives `.refresh` and `.reverseDns` none today
  (Admission.lean:233); give reverse-DNS its ceiling, and model the reserve as an admission rule
  with a witness pair (tenant call refused at reserve-only, system call admitted; refused-without
  the guard).

Acceptance: `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped; quotes carried; the ADR
and requirements agree.

comments.text: Manager blocked, 2026-10-08: ADR-0034 Decision 1 says "At most one provider read per machine per window then reaches the provider, however fast a caller loops", but its cache predicate uses state_observed_at. The machines table defines that timestamp as "when state was last established by an authoritative read of the provider" (state is Markdown-code-formatted in the source); DOM-8 says "A reader MUST take the staleness bound from state_observed_at rather than from the fact of a caller having asked" (state_observed_at is code-formatted in the source). A stale machine, a failed provider refresh read, and a fresh caller operation one second later leave the predicate stale; OPS-11 refresh classifies the first failure as "Always failed" (failed is code-formatted). With tenant budget still available, observation-only caching permits another provider read in the same window. Reading the at-most-one sentence as unconditional instead requires suppression after failed reads and a specified outcome for the fresh caller operation. Owner clarification needed: is the bound limited to successful observations, or does it include failed refresh reads? If unconditional, must a subsequent request fail locally, wait, or return stale state? Recommendation: count dispatched refresh reads toward a separate per-machine cooldown, never advance state_observed_at without evidence, and deterministically fail a new refresh locally while that cooldown remains; the owner must approve this behavior, including its error/pacing contract. No specification changes made and no new bead filed. Full report: .rloop/runs/20261008T053437.986583063Z-1159992/finished.md.

title: ADR-0035: a failure after an accepted mutation is ambiguous — driver field, OPS-11 bullet, settle-time search, release resolution
description:
Owner decision Q4 (2026-10-06): `ADR-0035` — a failure after the provider accepted a mutation is
ambiguous, whatever its kind. Read the ADR first, then `docs/research/panels-2026-10/r20/synthesis.md`
(four readers, verified citations). Do not re-litigate the rejected alternatives (dispatch, a
rate_limited-only rule, a durable create marker).

Edits owed (the ADR's Consequences list is the source; keep them in step):
- `PRV-5`: every driver error carries `details.accepted` — true once the provider answered with
  success the request that performs the mutation and carries the correlator (`PRV-26`); a key upload
  is not that request; a driver that cannot tell reports `internal`. Map Robot's
  `403 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` to `rate_limited`.
- `OPS-11`: a fourth bullet under "A failure is **ambiguous** when" — the mutating request was
  accepted — reaching the whole last row (create, power, reverse-DNS, delete, release attachment).
- `PRV-11`: restate as an instance.
- `OPS-27`: after acceptance the settle-time search succeeds only on exactly one resource; anything
  else is `needs_reconciliation`; `OPS-33`'s negative window does not run against a matched order
  still in progress.
- Resolution (`OPS-31`/`OPS-48`): a release resolved applied writes `released_at`.
- `LDG-39`: row precedence — an accepted, unresolved create takes the pending-fee row until
  `OPS-27`'s transaction.
- `CNF-31a` (today requires the defect), new CNF items per new MUST, `F48` note.
- Wire: the `retry_after_ms` / `retryable: false` pairing on a `needs_reconciliation` create of kind
  `rate_limited` (`04-api-contract.md` near API-26/WIR-9a).
- Formal: `Provisiond.Tables` — `Failure` gains `accepted`; `ambiguous` reads it; a theorem that an
  accepted last-row failure is never `failed`; update `classify_total`, `admission_only_failed`
  (pin `accepted = false` as its pre-provider premise), `install_marker_directions`, and the
  witnesses at Witnesses.lean:2271-2283; a witness pair for the new bullet.

Acceptance: `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped; quotes carried; ADR and
requirements agree.

title: A delete whose attachment listing fails leaves survivors unrecorded, and LDG-32 closes while a volume bills the operator
description:
Found by the r20 panel (opus), pre-existing, separate from ADR-0035.

A delete whose `DELETE` returns 2xx and whose follow-up `PRV-45` attachment listing
(02-provider-contract.md:427-429) is throttled settles `failed`. Only `PRV-45` writes
`machine_attachments` (05-persistence.md:322-337), so `STO-18` (05:338) holds nothing back and
`LDG-32` can close the commitment while a surviving volume (Hetzner: volumes, primary IPs, floating
IPs survive server deletion — docs/research/provider-verify-2026-10.md §3) bills the operator.
`OPS-32`'s sweep covers machines, images and keys, not attachments (03:1365-1378).

Proposed (opus): `PRV-45`'s listing runs on every gone path (OPS-48's gone-write row, LDG-74),

title: An unterminated Lean block comment leaves the citation gate through a traceback
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## The gap

`docstrings()` raises `ValueError('unterminated Lean block comment')` and `load_lean_docstrings()`
does not catch it, so a `.lean` file whose block comment never closes leaves the gate through a
traceback rather than through its own voice:

```
File ".../check_citations.py", line 194, in load_lean_docstrings
    docs[...] = '\n\n'.join(docstrings(source.read()))
ValueError: unterminated Lean block comment
exit=1
```

The message does not name the file, although `load_lean_docstrings()` has the path in hand. It is the
one extractor failure mode that does not behave like the others: every other case prints
`FAIL: <case>` and returns 1.

Low reach: Lean rejects an unterminated block comment, and `check_formal.sh` runs before this gate in
`check-all.sh`, so the build is already red by the time the citations gate runs. It bites someone
running `python3 tools/check_citations.py` on its own.

`pv-vwe.18` verified and shipped this path as-is; it predates that ticket's own extractor work.

## Two prose items to fold in while touching that docstring

One rule, one home, so these are recorded here rather than as tickets of their own.

- The exit line reads "an unverifiable quote, an unresolved name or a rise above the baseline or a
  failed extractor case". Two `or`s invite reading the last two as a pair; a comma after "name" fixes
  it.
- "A failed extractor case" has no referent above it: nothing in the module docstring mentions the
  fixture table, so a reader must find `check_docstrings()` to learn what a case is. Half a clause in
  the QUOTED paragraph, which already owns the Lean pass, would give it a home.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An unterminated block comment under `tools/formal/` produces a gate message naming the file, and
      the exit code the module docstring claims for it
- [ ] The exit line's two prose items above are folded in
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green

Cover OPS-32’s read-based deletes of images and temporary keys; the fast-shutdown window’s non-deposit consequences under FSW-N: replayed revocation, OPS-32, API-11’s 409, API-53’s revision, and LDG-14’s runway (disputed). title: StopRecord.lean reads an event list that ends early as an exit, so no theorem proves a survived stop is recorded (OPS-21, OPS-49, OVR-19)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during the PR #9 review (codex round 1, P2 on `StopRecord.lean`).*

`tools/formal/Provisiond/StopRecord.lean` cannot tell an exit from an event list that simply ends,
so no theorem there proves `OPS-21`'s main obligation for a general execution.

- `OPS-21` says "A cancellation of `execute` that the engine survives MUST be recorded before the
  engine exits, for every operation kind, subject to the bounded abandonment and later-stop exits
  below."
- `schedule p budget storeBudget []` returns `{}` (no tries), so `trace` reports
  `recorded = false` with both budgets positive, no later stop and no expiry. The same holds for
  any list that ends before an acknowledged try.
- `exit_store` takes `recorded = false` as its exit case, so it covers these unfinished prefixes
  too. `working_store_records` proves recording only for the one-event list
  `[.store (.committed true) redelivered]`.
- So the model admits a silent abandonment that `OPS-21` prohibits: nothing proves that an
  unrecorded result came from the Stop-record bound, the Store-retry bound's exhaustion, a later
  stop, or (with `shieldRecord` off) a redelivered stop.

Example: `trace current g s r 3 3 [.serialization]` gives `recorded = false`, `elapsed = 1`. In the
real system this worker is still inside its bound and must keep trying. The model reads it the same
as the expired case `trace current g s r 1 3 [.serialization, .store (.committed true) false]`.

Fix shape (for the implementer): give `schedule`'s result an exit reason (or an `unfinished`
flag set only by the `[]` case) and prove that `recorded = false` on a finished trace implies one
of the permitted exits. Optionally also prove progress: an unfinished prefix extended by an
acknowledged try within both budgets records. Then rewrite `trace`'s docstring, which now says
"`recorded = false` is an exit or an unfinished prefix ... nothing here yet separates the two".
Add a `ci.yml` negative control if the new theorem has a natural mutation (for example,
`schedule`'s `[]` case reporting a finished exit).

Markdown is unaffected: `OPS-21` already says this. Lean-only, no v1 effect.
(`OPS-21`, `OPS-49`, `OVR-19`)
close_reason: Separated unfinished schedules and proved the finished-unrecorded exit facts, with CI control.

title: The formal layer: every clause in the inventory gets a Lean home (ADR-0025, M2 through M8)
description:
## Problem Statement

The specification set has 497 requirements, six specification gates and a habit of cross-model review, and on 2026-09-12 three defects still landed that every gate and two readers passed: each citation resolved while the consequences contradicted. `LDG-38` described its billing-period reset as the customer's favour when the arithmetic says the opposite; `STO-12` and `STO-13` together demanded something PostgreSQL refuses; `STO-54` and `ADR-0023` called a one-interval grace a repair. The gates check that a rule is cited, owned and phrased; nothing checks what a rule implies, and the one gate that executed anything sampled floating-point inputs and never crossed a period boundary.

The owner's decision (`ADR-0025`) is that the set's precise semantics — calculations, predicates, closed tables and the lifecycle transitions with their real transaction and provider-call boundaries — are carried in Lean under `tools/formal/`, proved for every input, with the historical defects retained as executable witnesses so that "a plausible but incorrect amendment can no longer pass review merely because its prose sounds consistent". The first milestone (arithmetic and witnesses) has landed, been reviewed and been fixed. This spec is the remaining inventory.

## Solution

Extend the formal layer milestone by milestone until every clause in the agreed inventory has a Lean home: the claim model, the cancellation fence composed on it, the closed tables with the rendering gate that keeps the Markdown honest, reconciliation knowledge and restore, funding and the tenant lifecycle, rescue and install, wire canonicalization and redaction. Each milestone lands as theorems over every input, decided witnesses for the historical defects, and a negative theorem for every guard a dated amendment added — refused with the guard, admitted without it — all behind the one specification gate the set already runs, with a CI negative control per check.

Authority follows `ADR-0025`: a formalized clause's home is its tagged declaration; the requirement keeps its identifier, MUST, rationale and retained traps; the rendered formula or table is generated or diffed, never trusted. A theorem is never a conformance item.

## User Stories

1. As a spec author, I want a rule I amend to break a theorem when the amendment contradicts a property the set claims, so that the contradiction is found before review rather than by it.
2. As a spec author, I want the historical defects (`usable_sats > 0`, per-tick rounding, the unfenced funding read, the missing claim term, the period-reset direction) kept as executable witnesses, so that none can be re-laid without a red build.
3. As a spec author, I want every guard a dated amendment added to be a parameter of the model that carries it, so that removing the guard is a one-token change a witness theorem exercises.
4. As a spec author, I want a formalized formula or table rendered into the requirement from its declaration, so that I never maintain two copies by hand.
5. As a spec author, I want a rendered region that carries prose or citations diffed rather than rewritten, so that the rationale and citations around a table survive regeneration.
6. As a spec author, I want a backticked declaration name in a document to be checked against the emitted index, so that a renamed declaration cannot leave a dangling citation.
7. As a spec author, I want the model's identities (`OperationId`, `ClaimNumber`, `EpisodeId`, `MachineId`, `TenantId`) to be distinct types, so that a fence holding an attempt's id instead of an episode's is a type error rather than a review finding.
8. As a spec author, I want "the store committed" and "the worker learned it committed" to be separate facts in the model, so that `ADR-0022`'s lost reply is representable and not collapsed into rollback.
9. As a spec author, I want "dispatched", "applied" and "response received" to be separate facts for a provider call, so that a lost response is never read as evidence nothing happened.
10. As a spec author, I want `OPS-49`'s "never the last failed statement" to be a refuted alternative in the model, so that the prohibited partial-statement retry is expressible and shown harmful.
11. As a spec author, I want both commit orderings of `OPS-42`'s fence proved, so that "one of them provably loses" is a theorem and not a sentence.
12. As a spec author, I want the cancellation model to carry the rate-outage branch, the tenant's current suspension state and the episode, so that the theorem proved is about the requirement as written and not a simplification of it.
13. As a spec author, I want `OPS-33`'s release-without-resolution to be a reachable positive witness (`unknown` knowledge with a closed commitment), so that the model cannot mistake release for absence.
14. As a spec author, I want absence evidence to require a complete pass, an elapsed window and a direct reread as three separate conjuncts, so that dropping any one admits a witness.
15. As a spec author, I want restart and restore to be distinct events with distinct trace types, so that a restart theorem cannot be cited as covering a restore.
16. As a spec author, I want `STO-54`'s "an extension lost in Δ is not rebuilt" to be a proved existential, so that the weaker recovery guarantee is stated by a theorem and not assumed away.
17. As a spec author, I want every closed table (`OPS-11`, `OPS-3`, `OPS-48`, `DOM-31`, the halt matrix) to be a total function whose totality is decided, so that adding a kind without a row fails the build.
18. As a spec author, I want a migration plan's transaction mode to be a type, so that `F52`'s second defect — a `CONCURRENTLY` build inside a transaction — cannot be written.
19. As a spec author, I want the ledger's "consumption leaves `available` unchanged" and the clamp's "the credit is untouched" proved over every input, so that the 2026-09-02 double charge is unrepresentable.
20. As a spec author, I want provider windows, PostgreSQL semantics and `OPS-47`'s single engine to appear as named hypotheses on the theorems that depend on them, so that a signature shows what was assumed.
21. As a reviewer reading a landing without memory of the session, I want the emitted index to say which requirement each declaration formalizes, so that I can check a declaration against the sentence it claims to carry.
22. As a reviewer, I want every proof to rest on the three standard axioms only, with `sorry`, project axioms and `native_decide` refused by the gate, so that a green build means what it says.
23. As a reviewer, I want each new check to have a CI control that breaks the thing it guards and asserts the failure came from that check, so that a red for the wrong reason is never taken as evidence.
24. As CI, I want the formal layer to build and gate in the same job as the textual gates, under the same Nix shell a developer uses, so that there is one toolchain definition.
25. As CI, I want a module the build never imports to be refused, so that a proof file nobody reads is not a green check.
26. As a future implementer, I want the model's definitions to compute permitted outcomes for a sequence of commands and faults, so that an implementation can be compared against them in a test, without that comparison being mistaken for a refinement proof.
27. As a future implementer, I want the conformance checklist to count nothing from the formal layer, so that a proved model never reads as a passed test.
28. As the owner, I want the inventory built in the order that lets each model be true when it lands — claim before fence, tables before the rendering gate, reconciliation and restore before funding — so that no milestone proves a false requirement to save time.
29. As the owner, I want Mathlib added only in a commit naming the theorem that cannot close without it, so that the dependency is never carried by default.
30. As the owner, I want the glossary term **reference model** added when the first lifecycle model exists, so that the glossary never describes an artifact that does not exist.

## Implementation Decisions

**Order and milestones.** Each milestone is one ticket; a milestone's acceptance is a proof or decided check that fails on a named historical defect.

- M2, the claim model (`ADR-0022`, `OPS-5`, `OPS-6`, `OPS-8`, `OPS-22`, `OPS-49`, `STO-3`). A durable row with status and claim number; executions each holding their claim; a transaction as a list of statements with the guarded status write first; whole-transaction restart as the retry, with the last-statement retry definable so it can be refuted; the store outcome as committed-and-acked pairs; the provider outcome as dispatched, applied, reply. Theorems: a stale execution's write is inert after a later claim; a same-claim repetition changes nothing, `revision` included; provider calls across store retries are at most one; a lost reply on the claim itself is a transition to exit and never a re-claim. Witness pair: the stale-defer trace refused with the claim term, admitted without it. Both panel readers proved that pair in scratch; the decision-rich shape, from that prototype:

  ```
  guardOk withClaimTerm row write := row.status = running ∧ (¬withClaimTerm ∨ row.claim = write.mine)
  trace withClaimTerm := A claims (1); A defers; reply lost; B claims (2); A repeats its defer
  refused  : (trace true).status  = running
  admitted : (trace false).status = queued
  ```

- M3, the cancellation fence composed on M2 (`OPS-41`, `OPS-42`, `LDG-62`, `OPS-48`, `LDG-16`, `ADR-0021`). Model state carries the machine's commitment, stored date and `exhausted_since`, the fence as an optional episode id, the episode and its state, the rate as optional (outage is a branch, not a value), the tenant's current suspension state, and time. Events: sweep routing on the stored date and the column, claim, the fence transaction with its re-check inside it as a parameter, extension in its own serialization guarded on the fence, provider delete outside the serialization, reply, settlement, gone-write, retry from stalled only, rate movement. Invariants over reachable states with the single-engine assumption in the signature: destruction only after a fence transaction whose re-check read unfunded, no rate, or suspended; an extension after the fence opens nothing and moves nothing; an extension before the fence is seen by the re-check; a set fence names an open episode with the same id; closed is absorbing; gone clears the fence and closes the episode together. Witnesses, one parameter each: re-check outside the fence transaction, fence holding the attempt id, the withdrawn abort predicate inside the lifecycle, abort without the date write, suspension keyed on episode reasons.

- M4, the closed tables and the rendering gate (`OPS-11`, `OPS-3`, `OPS-48`, `DOM-31`, `DOM-17`). Each table is a total function with a `match` carrying no wildcard, its totality decided. The rendering gate: `lake exe gate` already emits the index; a Python specification gate reads it, diffs every marked region in the documents against what the declaration emits, generates the pure-computation regions, and resolves every backticked declaration name. The citations gate gains that resolver. `check-all.sh` orders the formal build before the gates that read its index. First marked regions: `OPS-48`'s transition table and `DOM-31`'s diagram emitted and diffed; `LDG-38`'s worked examples and `LDG-31`'s worked table generated. The migration-plan type (transactional versus standalone statement) lands here as the formal home of `F52`'s second defect.

- M5, reconciliation knowledge and restore (`OPS-32`, `OPS-33`, `OPS-36`, `OPS-27`, `PRV-36`, `STO-54`, `STO-5`, `OPS-15`). Knowledge as `unknown`, `observed present`, `authoritative absence`, `multiple candidates`, separate from the commitment's open or closed; absence evidence as three conjuncts; two window fields, never one. Fault events `crash`, `restart`, `restore Δ`, `complete procedure` with separate trace types; recovery phases as separate permissions, never one Boolean; quarantine of the irreversible kinds before the first claim; the lost extension not rebuilt as a proved existential.

- M6, funding and the tenant lifecycle (`LDG-8`, `LDG-9`, `LDG-31`, `LDG-70`, `STO-30`, `STO-31`, `WIR-42`, `API-34`, `API-35`). Ledger conservation; the clamp and the deficiency as separate quantities in separate units; rail-identity replay; deposit expiry; tenant deletion; operator attribution.

- M7, rescue and install (`RSC-3`–`RSC-5`, `RSC-26`, `RSC-39`–`RSC-44`, `OPS-45`). Trust state, inventory validation, write-started markers, rescue exit, recovery-key retention. Physical and cryptographic facts are hypotheses.

- M8, wire canonicalization, redaction and admission (`API-9`, `API-12`, `WIR-1a`, `WIR-32`, `API-21`, `STO-50`, `API-7`, `SEC-39`, `LDG-20`, `LDG-40`). Canonical serialization, fingerprint preimage, projection and redaction idempotence, the admission and halt matrices as decided policy spaces. Whether `WIR-37`'s fixtures are generated is decided at the end of M4 on the evidence of the rendering mechanism; if yes, `13-wire-contract.md`'s precedence sentence is amended to say a registered shape renders its declaration.

**Authority and rendering** (`ADR-0025`). One declaration per formalized clause, tagged with the requirement identifier; the requirement keeps identifier, MUST, rationale, amendment record and traps. Until a clause's region is gated, the Markdown is authoritative and the Lean is a checking interpretation. Ids stay append-only; withdrawn definitions live in a historical namespace that current policy cannot select. No hand-kept manifest.

**Trust.** Standard three axioms only, `sorryAx` refused transitively, no project axioms, `native_decide` refused everywhere under the project namespace except an `Explore` namespace nothing tags or cites. Rational witnesses close by `decide +kernel`. No Mathlib unless a named theorem cannot close without it.

**Assumptions.** Provider behaviour, PostgreSQL semantics and the single engine are named hypotheses on the theorems that use them; a model that omits a second engine says so in its docstring. Never an `axiom`.

**Vocabulary.** Specification gate, witness, model, assumption, property as defined in the glossary. **Reference model** is added to the glossary with M2, the first lifecycle model. *Oracle* stays banned. A settlement parameter is never named *target*.

**Modules.** One module per model, shared identity and outcome types in one place, witnesses in one module, the gate executable unchanged in role. Every module imported by the root, which the wrapper enforces.

## Testing Decisions

- The seam is `check-all.sh`: `lake build`, `lake exe gate`, the Python gates. Nothing else tests the formal layer.
- A good test is a property of external behaviour: a theorem about what the definitions imply for every input, or a decided witness over a concrete trace. Never a test of a proof's internals or a tactic's shape.
- Every guard has its pair: refused with the guard, admitted without. A model with only the positive theorem is incomplete.
- Every model has a successful execution witness (a create that succeeds, a cancellation that destroys) so that a model that refuses everything cannot satisfy its safety theorems vacuously.
- Every new check gets a CI negative control that mutates the thing the check guards, asserts the build or gate went red, and asserts the red came from that check and not from a syntax error or a missing toolchain. `ci.yml` holds the list. Prior art: the four Lean controls and the four textual controls already there.
- Bounded exploration publishes its bounds; it is evidence within them and not an unbounded theorem.
- A theorem never counts toward conformance coverage; the coverage gate reads nothing from the formal layer.

## Out of Scope

- An implementation oracle or a refinement proof; comparing a future implementation to the model is a test, and building that comparison waits for an implementation.
- Aeneas, Verso, or any documentation-platform migration.
- Formalizing provider behaviour, PostgreSQL, deployment, cryptographic hardness, or legal and commercial obligations beyond naming them as hypotheses.
- Rewriting the textual Python gates in Lean.
- Telling tenants a restore interval is running (decided against, `STO-54`).
- Wire fixture generation until M4's evidence is in.

## Further Notes

The panel that shaped this — Codex at xhigh and a fresh Fable reader on one brief — both warned that the fence model built without the claim model, the rate-outage branch, the suspended-tenant branch and the episode proves a false requirement; M3 depends on M2 for that reason and not for convenience. The same panel found by running Lean that `decide` sticks on rational equalities and that `decide +kernel` closes them under the standard axioms; that is why the trust policy can refuse `native_decide` outright.

This set's own record is that each fix round introduces defects at about the rate it removes them and that green gates are not the check. Every milestone therefore ends with a two-axis review of its diff before the next begins.
close_reason: M2-M8 inventory landed; remaining candidates disposed 2026-10-13 (r47): written as pv-hy1, pv-7i1, pv-zy2, pv-0uk; pv-4pn parked; four declined

comments.text:
2026-09-21 panel (opus + codex gpt-6-astra + codex gpt-5.6-sol) on where formalization still earns its place. Six beads created: .14 (LDG-16 defect), .15 (LDG-70), .16 (LDG-38/LDG-72), .17 (LDG-68), .18 (quote gate over Lean docstrings), .19 (SEC-46).

DECLINED, so they are not proposed again without new argument. A currency-indexed Money type: 3/3 called it ceremony — a module that does not retrofit Ledger/Funding/Meter cannot turn any amendment to the code that carries money red, and the premise that those modules carry satoshis as Nat was false (Ledger.Balances.sum is Int, Meter.postedDebit takes Rat). Tagging the untagged homes (Tables.ErrorKind, Tables.Kind, Admission.Verb): 3/3 called it housekeeping rather than a formalization bead — it repairs manifest and citation ownership and establishes no new red build; do it inside whichever bead renders that table from the enumeration, which is where the tag earns its place. OPS-38's correlator cardinality: already built — Reconcile.searchStep distinguishes [], [c] and cs via union, and duplicates_keyed_by_account_and_id decides it; an OPS-38-owned theorem and tag is cheap if wanted, and OPS-29's exactness is a separate question. WIR-37 fixtures (decided 2026-09-19), the DEF-*/CNF historical-trace row, PRV-13b's measurement procedure, API-9, WIR-32, RSC-27 and LDG-61: declined and the panel agreed.

CANDIDATES NOT WRITTEN, each with a reader behind it: DOM-10/PRV-4 capability gating, but only composed with dispatch, never as a freestanding declaration type; STO-53/PRV-36's effective-window maximum; OPS-40's two signed-URL expiry gates; WIR-45's abuse-case projection secrecy; STO-17's uniqueness key (F15, a review miss with money behind it); PRV-31's 'no declared bound MUST NOT be sold on prepaid terms' as a finite admission rule; LDG-9's aggregate reserved scalar, where subtracting one of two commitments is the bad amendment.

THE ADMISSION TEST, from sol, which is sharper than the one in the brief: a red-build pair per parameter is necessary, not sufficient, because an unused model can have excellent negative controls and protect nothing. Composition with an existing state transition or an authoritative rendered table is what admits a candidate. That test is what declined the Money module and what conditions the capability one.
