title: Claim model: shared identity and outcome types, ADR-0022's guard theorems
description:
## Parent

pv-vwe — the formal layer, M2 through M8 (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

The first lifecycle model. Distinct types for `OperationId`, `ClaimNumber`, `EpisodeId`, `MachineId`, `TenantId` (structures, never aliases); a store outcome as committed-and-acked, a provider outcome as dispatched, applied, reply. A durable row with status and claim number; executions each holding their claim; a transaction as a list of statements whose guarded status write comes first; whole-transaction restart as the retry, with the last-statement retry definable so `OPS-49`'s prohibition can be refuted rather than assumed. Every guard `STO-3` states is a parameter. Prototype shape, from the panel's probe: `guardOk withClaimTerm row write := row.status = running ∧ (¬withClaimTerm ∨ row.claim = write.mine)`; trace: A claims (1), A defers, reply lost, B claims (2), A repeats its defer. Adds **reference model** to `CONTEXT.md` now that one exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A stale execution's write is inert after a later claim (theorem over all rows and writes)
- [ ] A same-claim repetition of an accepted settlement changes nothing, `revision` included
- [ ] Provider calls across store retries are at most one, with the retry-last-statement alternative proved to double-post
- [ ] A lost reply on the claim itself is a transition to exit; no re-claim transition exists
- [ ] Witness pair by `decide`: the stale-defer trace refused with the claim term, admitted without it
- [ ] CI control: the claim term deleted from the guard turns the build red on the refused-witness theorem
- [ ] A successful execution witness: claim, settle, done
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, and every new check's CI negative control asserts the red came from that check.
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff (standards against `AGENTS.md`/`ADR-0025`/the glossary, spec against the cited requirement sentences) applied before the next ticket starts.

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately)

title: ADR-0026: the exhaustion mark becomes two facts, in the requirements
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`). The decision is `ADR-0026`.

## What to land

`ADR-0026`'s two facts, in the Markdown. The ADR holds the argument and the rejected alternatives;
this ticket writes the rules.

- **`LDG-16`** — replace the one setter and one clearer with the two facts. The rate confirmation
  reference is armed by **every rate-produced backward move**; where one write both arms it and
  lands in the future, **the arm wins**. It is discharged only by a strictly later accepted
  observation: still-exhausted confirms and permits routing, future-dated writes that date and
  clears. The wait is no longer "older than one re-derivation interval". Narrow the requirement's
  claim to **transient** error, per the ADR's "What this does not promise".
- **`PRV-13e`** — re-derivation arms the reference and records which observation it consumed.
- **`LDG-65`** — the outage rule keys on the new fact; `LDG-64`'s bound bypasses confirmation, since
  the deployment must "**cancel machines at that bound** if no rate has returned" and no observation
  will arrive to discharge anything.
- **`STO-54`** — the restore writes the **deadline**, not the rate reference, and preserves any
  reference already present. Its grace "buys the tenant one re-derivation interval in which to
  extend again" and no observation discharges it.
- **`STO-49`** — a transactionally increasing per-currency **acceptance order**. The table is
  "unique on `(currency, observed_at)`" and nothing makes `observed_at` monotone or non-reusable, so
  the comparison cannot be a timestamp. Retention must cover a referenced observation, which today
  is stated only in terms of subjects with an open increment.
- **`05-persistence.md`** — two columns where there was one, the reference written in the same
  transaction as the date it explains.
- **`OPS-41`** — the suspended-tenant path keeps its existing bypass; the ADR quotes it.
- **`CNF-99`** — drop the forty-five-to-forty case the wider arming rule deliberately changes; add
  the reading that crosses the horizon backward and lands in the future, which is the input that
  would have caught the dead branch; keep the natural-expiry and restore assertions unchanged.

## What must not change

`LDG-16`'s natural-expiry behaviour. Its own sentence is the reason the universal fence was
rejected: "The null case routes immediately, and that is the point: natural expiry of a runway the
customer was shown is not a glitch, and delaying it an interval would run every ordinary exhaustion
one interval into the wind-down reserve this requirement exists to keep whole."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each requirement above amended, `ADR-0026` cited where the argument lives, with the withdrawn
      wording retained only where a trap sits behind it (`README.md`'s retention convention)
- [ ] No sentence claims the mechanism catches a persistent plausible error
- [ ] `CNF-99` carries the horizon-crossing-into-the-future case
- [ ] Every quoted attribution carries the cited requirement's own words — run the check by hand
      over the diff, since `tools/check_citations.py` covers the Markdown and `pv-vwe.18` is the
      bead that extends it
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Re-scoped 2026-09-21 after a three-reader panel (opus, codex gpt-6-astra, codex gpt-5.6-sol). rloop's codex Manager blocked on this ticket as originally written and was right to: its acceptance criteria demanded a trace leaving the machine unrouted while its options included withdrawing that protection.

The panel changed the answer. Verified: the horizon disjunct of LDG-16's set rule can never fire, because a backward move crossing now+interval that does not land in the past lands in the future and therefore also triggers the clear. The harm it was meant to stop is real and reachable - a poison that IS the median has zero deviation and LDG-60 cannot exclude it by construction (sources 100,100,104, one corrupted to 103, 6100 usable sats, 61s -> 59s). A second counterexample offered in the panel was directionally inverted and does not stand; this one does. Deletion rejected, universal destruction fence rejected (LDG-16's own natural-expiry sentence plus a 40% reserve cost at PRV-13e's hourly default, and LDG-65 inverts during an outage), re-keying the single column rejected (it silently deletes STO-54's restore grace). Two facts, on two clocks. ADR-0026 has the argument.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Landed. LDG-16 owns the rule; PRV-13e, 05-persistence's machines rows, STO-49, STO-54, LDG-62,
LDG-65, OPS-41, CNF-99 and CNF-295 follow it. The two facts are machines.rate_confirmation_ref
(an STO-49 acceptance order, not an instant) and machines.destroy_not_before.

Two things ADR-0026 did not say, both found by the two-axis review, both now amendments on the ADR
as well as rules:

1. A backward move never confirms itself. The accepted discharge text - 'one that still derives
exhaustion confirms it and permits routing' - assumed an arming that was itself an exhaustion,
which the widened arming rule two sentences earlier had stopped guaranteeing. Read literally it
restores the defect the mechanism exists to stop: an ordinary wobble from two hours out to one
hour fifty arms the reference, the next reading is the poisoned one, and being strictly later it
confirms an exhaustion no observation before it derived. Discharge is now 'the first strictly later
accepted observation whose own write does not arm it again'. CNF-99 feeds that trace.

2. A move of a date that had already passed arms nothing. Without it a machine already known to be
exhausted goes back behind a fresh confirmation once per interval for as long as the rate drifts,
and LDG-13 becomes unreachable. The withdrawn rule had the same exclusion.

Also decided and added to the ADR: LDG-64's bound and the suspended tenant bypass the reference but
not the destruction deadline, which costs the bound at most one re-derivation interval and keeps
the restore grace a rule without exceptions.

Considered and kept, against review: 'acceptance order' (ADR-0026's own words; the 'order' on
CONTEXT.md's Deposit avoid-list is the provider-order sense) and destroy_not_before (states the
rule with no polarity ambiguity, unlike a second '_deadline' beside rate_outage_deadline; the
schema row now distinguishes it from destroy_committed).

attributions checked by hand over the diff - the citations gate caught one, where two quotes shared

re-verified.

title: LDG-70: the cached balance and the sum, as one theorem
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

`LDG-70`'s two representations of one balance, in `Provisiond.Ledger`.

`LDG-5` says "**Balance is the sum of entries** and nothing else"; `LDG-6` puts a running balance on
every entry; `STO-21` permits a cached one. `LDG-70` settles which the authorization reads: the sum
"is a definition, not a read strategy, and the read is `balance_after` on the tenant's latest
entry", written "inside the same serialized transaction that appends the entry".

`Ledger` today carries `Balances.sum : Int` and `available = sum − reserved`. It has no entry
history, no `balance_after`, and therefore no way to state the property `LDG-70` exists for: that
the cached read and the definition cannot diverge.

Model entries carrying a sequence, an amount and a `balance_after`; prove that an append preserves
the equality, that the authoritative read is `balance_after` at the greatest sequence, and that the
two disagree exactly when an append used a stale predecessor.

Every reader on the 2026-09-21 panel ranked this, and all three ranked it third.

## Why this one

This is `LDG-73`'s shape, and that shape has already cost this set once: the meter carried "what has
been charged" as a second representation until the rounding-credit redesign replaced it, and three
requirements were deleted rather than changed. The question `LDG-73` leaves standing is "whether the
second representation should exist" — the model is what answers it with a proof instead of an
argument.

## Red build

An append that computes `balance_after` from a row other than the current greatest sequence: two
credits of 10 and 7 against the same predecessor leave the latest `balance_after` at 7 while the
entries sum to 17, and a create is then authorized against a balance the sum does not fund.

## Must not touch

`Ledger.clamp` and the existing `available` definition; `LDG-35`'s serialization is already modelled
by `serializedAuthorization` and this composes with it rather than restating it. No SQL, no index
model.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entry history with `balance_after`, and the equality theorem over append
- [ ] The authoritative read is the greatest sequence, with a witness for a non-greatest read
- [ ] The stale-predecessor witness above, refused with the guard and admitted without it
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, `ci.yml` row per new parameter,
      rehearsed locally
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: done

comments.author: master
comments.text: Landed by rloop Run 20260926T183014.077293953Z-2295892, Round 1. The ticket's Red build was wrong as written: "two credits of 10 and 7 against the same predecessor leave the latest balance_after at 7 while the entries sum to 17, and a create is then authorized against a balance the sum does not fund" -- two stale credits make the cache UNDER-state the sum, so every create they authorize is funded. The witness uses stale debits instead (top-up 17, two debits of 10 and 7 both computed from the 17: latest balance_after 10, sum 0, a create of 10 authorized), chosen by consultation opus+sol (B) against astra (C). The ticket's 'the two disagree exactly when an append used a stale predecessor' is false as an iff; Ledger.drift_identity states the exact difference (each append's drift is the balance_after of the row it read less the greatest row's) and divergence_names_a_stale_append the true direction (opus+sol (i), astra (ii); astra's 10/7/3 counterexample corrected the wording and is decided in drift_identity_witness). New guard appendReadsLatest with its ci.yml row. Panel: astra and opus no findings, sol one finding rejected (`LDG-9`'s `available` names LDG-9's quantity in its own word, not a claim about what LDG-9 says), fable not run (quota). title: LDG-38's increment key and LDG-72's high-water mark
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

`LDG-38`'s real increment key, and `LDG-72`'s high-water mark, in `Provisiond.Funding`.

`LDG-38`: "A `usage_debit` MUST be idempotent per **`(subject, billing period, kind, increment
end)`**." `Funding.post` writes `key := .increment w.entries.length` — the entry count, unique by
construction — so the replay that key exists to refuse cannot be expressed in the model at all.
`Funding`'s own docstring already lists "`LDG-72`'s high-water mark" among what it omits.

Give the increment its stated key, carry the high-water mark, and prove the replay refused.

## Why this one

`Provisiond.Funding` already proves exactly this property for the other money-in path:
`replay_credits_once_by_key` shows a replayed settlement crediting once under `LDG-8`'s key, and
`replay_refused_by_record` shows `STO-46`'s unique payment row catching what the key does not. The
metered path is the one that runs every interval forever, and it has neither.

## Red build

**The replay.** A worker's reply is lost; the tick recomputes the increment ending at `T` and posts
again. Under the stated key it is refused; with the key as a sequence, two `usage_debit` entries
exist for the same seconds and the rounding credit `r` has advanced twice — and `Meter`'s
`single_corruption_bound` is about a corrupt `r` in range, not about an `r` advanced by a debit that
should never have posted.

**The stale read.** `LDG-38`'s 2026-09-04 clause: a tick that reads `running` before an `LDG-74`
stop "posts an increment computed from state that is no longer true". `Fence` and `Reconcile` model
the stop; neither posts money, so nothing today connects them.

## Must not touch

`Meter.lean`'s recurrence and `Ledger.clamp`. New `Params` fields go one per line: `ci.yml`'s loop
requires exactly one red per flip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The increment carries `(subject, billing period, kind, increment end)`, with the replay witness

title: LDG-68's period boundary, composed with the meter
description:
## Parent

## What to build

`LDG-68`'s period boundary, composed with `Provisiond.Meter`.

`LDG-68`: "**The billing period is the calendar month in UTC, and it is one boundary for the whole**"
deployment. `LDG-38` adds that "An increment also closes at every period boundary". `Meter` models
the rounding-credit recurrence and mentions the period reset in prose — "starting a period at `r =

Carrying `r` across `00:00Z` on the first of the month; assigning a straddling increment wholly to

must fail an executable boundary witness.

`Meter.postedDebit` and the corruption bound; no calendar library and no provider calendars. If a
calendar conversion cannot close on core Lean, that is the commit that names the theorem needing
Mathlib (`ADR-0025`), and it is a decision to take explicitly rather than by drift.

- [ ] A period key and the assignment rule, with the three witnesses above
- [ ] The existing recurrence theorems unchanged, or the one that changes named and argued
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, `ci.yml` row per parameter, rehearsed
      locally

title: The quoted-attribution gate reaches the Lean docstrings
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

Extend `tools/check_citations.py`'s QUOTED rule to the docstrings under `tools/formal/`.

The gate reads root `*.md` and `docs/adr/*.md` — `docs = {f: read(f) for f in
sorted(glob.glob("*.md"))}` — and states the hole in its own docstring: "Nor a quote inside a Lean
docstring under tools/formal/: this gate reads *.md only, and a docstring quoting withdrawn wording
stayed green for a day on 2026-09-15."

There are now over ten thousand lines of Lean prose making quoted claims about requirements, and it
is the largest ungated surface in the repository by the gate's own admission.

## Why this one

The defect rate here is measured, not estimated. A throwaway script run on 2026-09-20 over the
`pv-vwe.9` diff found **twelve** quoted spans that did not appear in the requirement they were
attributed to — bold markers swallowed into a quote, a truncated amendment, and one sentence
attributed to `API-7` that is `API-40`'s. Every one passed all seven gates. The same session's brief
to a review panel carried two more, and the panel read past one of them.

This is the cheapest item on the board: no Lean, no new mechanism, one new source for a rule that
already exists and already has a failure mode the file documents.

## Shape

Extract `/-- … -/` and `/-! … -/` blocks, normalize whitespace across line wraps — the quotes wrap,
the requirements wrap, and they wrap differently — and run the existing QUOTED rule. Ratchet the
first run against a baseline the way the UNQUOTED rule is ratcheted, if the clean-tree count is not
already zero; a gate that fails a clean tree is a gate someone deletes.

## Red build

Rewrite one quoted span in a module docstring to words its requirement does not contain: the gate
exits 1 and names the file and the span. The negative control asserts the red came from this rule
and not from a missing index.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The QUOTED rule runs over `tools/formal/**/*.lean` docstrings, whitespace-normalized
- [ ] HEAD passes, or the ratchet baseline is set with the residue listed
- [ ] A `ci.yml` negative control that breaks one docstring quote and asserts the named failure
- [ ] The gate's own docstring no longer claims the hole it no longer has
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: done

title: SEC-46's account-status table and the release rule
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

`SEC-46`'s account-status table as a total function, and the release rule as a theorem over it.

The requirement is headed "**AMENDED twice — and 'lost' turned out to mean three different things**",
and the states differ in what happens to the tenant's commitments. Release happens on one of them
and on no other.

Model the states, make the release predicate total over them with no wildcard, and prove release
holds exactly on the terminating one.

## Why this one

`SEC-39` calls confirming a termination "the largest single money movement any operator verb
performs", which is why it has its own operator ceiling. `API-63`'s own history is the warning: its
`terminated` path once released the commitments and left the meters running, and that was found by a
review pass rather than by a build. A four-state table with one releasing row is exactly the closed
space a `decide` settles and prose does not.

## Red build

An amendment that releases on `credentials_rejected`, contradicting "**Retained — losing the key is
not losing the servers**", or on `account_unreachable`, whose commitments are also retained.

## Must not touch

`API-63`'s full transaction — the meters, the affected-tenant lists and the closing debit are
`Provisiond.Fence`'s and `Provisiond.Funding`'s. This is the status table and the release predicate
over it, and nothing else.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The states as a closed enumeration with no wildcard, so a status added without a row is a red
      build
- [ ] Release holds exactly on the terminating state, decided over the whole enumeration
- [ ] Witnesses for the two retained states named above
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, `ci.yml` row if a parameter lands,
      rehearsed locally
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes

title: Model the setter: the re-derivation transition Fence has never exercised
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`). The decision is `ADR-0026`.

## What to build

The setter, in `Provisiond.Fence`. The module's own omissions say why this is owed: it excludes
"`PRV-13e`'s re-derivation, which is what sets `exhausted_since` under `LDG-16`'s horizon rule (the
column is set only in an initial world here)". **The layer models the clear and the routing and has
never exercised the rule that writes the mark**, which is why 495 tagged declarations and eleven
negative controls did not catch a branch that can never fire.

Model the re-derivation transition as a total function of the old date, the new date, the
observation consumed and the clock, carrying `ADR-0026`'s two facts as separate fields, so that a
write which both arms and clears is not representable. State the confirmation rule against the
acceptance order rather than elapsed time, and keep the two bypasses — `LDG-64`'s bound and the
suspended tenant — outside it.

## Red build

- **The dead branch, put back.** A parameter restoring the old clear-wins reading: a derivation
  moving the date from `now + 2i` to `now + i/2` leaves the machine routable before any second
  observation. Refused under `current`, admitted with the parameter off.
- **Elapsed time standing in for confirmation.** The same observation consumed twice, an interval
  apart, must not discharge the reference.
- **The restore grace discharged by an observation.** A deadline cleared by a rate that arrived
  seconds after the restore.

## Must not touch

`Provisiond.Fence`'s existing fence parameters and their witnesses — eleven `ci.yml` rows depend on
exactly one red per flip, so new fields go one per line. `Meter`'s recurrence and `Ledger`'s clamp
are out of scope.

## Blocked by

`pv-vwe.14` — the rules land first; this models what they say.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The re-derivation transition as one total function with no wildcard, both facts as separate
      fields
- [ ] The three red builds above, each with the pair the epic requires
- [ ] The existing fence theorems still hold, or the one that changes is named and argued
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, one `ci.yml` row per new parameter,
      rehearsed locally before the push
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: done

title: LDG-16's confirmation promise does not reach a cancellation already enqueued
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`). The rule is `LDG-16` as `ADR-0026` amended it; the
model that exhibits the gap is `Provisiond.Fence` as `pv-vwe.20` landed it (`bc08e19`).

## What the set promises, and where the promise stops

`LDG-16` opens with the promise:

> a rate-produced exhaustion MUST still be **confirmed by a strictly later accepted rate
> observation** before anything is destroyed, so a **transient** bad reading can move a date but
> cannot destroy a disk.

Its mechanism is a routing predicate, and only that:

> **The exhaustion sweep MUST route a machine where its stored `runway_until` has passed, its
> `rate_confirmation_ref` is null and its `destroy_not_before` is null or past — and MUST NOT
> route it otherwise.**

and, two sentences on:

> `OPS-41`'s re-derivation at claim is the last look before the mutation, so it reads neither
> fact except to clear them.

**Nothing gates a cancellation that is already enqueued.** `OPS-39` opens an episode "once, and
found open by every subsequent sweep until it closes", so a machine whose episode is already open
needs no second routing decision to be destroyed — and the reference is only ever read by the
routing decision.

## The trace, executed in the committed model

From `Provisiond.Witnesses.staleDateWorld` (commitment 100, stored date 0, `now` 0, one satoshi
per second, both facts null), under `Fence.current`:

```
sweep                      -- the stale stored date routes: natural expiry, reference null.
                           -- Episode 1 opens `attempting` with its attempt queued.
rederive 100 (some 5)      -- the interval's derivation writes the true date, 100.
                           -- Arms nothing: the old date had already passed. Reference null.
rateRestored 200           -- the price moves adversely, 1 -> 200 satoshis per second.
rederive 0 (some 7)        -- observation 7 moves 100 -> 0, a backward move of a date that
                           -- stood in the future: the reference arms with 7.
claim, fenceTxn, fenceWrite-- the queued attempt claims. OPS-41 re-derives at the same 200,
                           -- reads the machine unfunded, and writes the fence.
providerDelete true …      -- the disk is destroyed. `rate_confirmation_ref` is still `some 7`.
```

`#eval` on the committed tree returns `rateConfirmationRef = some 7` and `destroyed = true`.
No extension is involved, no bypass applies — the episode's one reason is `exhausted` — and
exactly one accepted observation stands behind the destruction. That is what the promise says
cannot happen.

The same shape is reachable through `LDG-62`: an extension clears both facts and writes a future
date but closes no episode, so its machine's queued attempt survives to be claimed after the next
backward derivation arms the reference (also executed: `sweep, extend 100, rateLost,
rateRestored 200, rederive 0 (some 7), claim, fenceTxn, fenceWrite, providerDelete` destroys).

## The two readings

**(a) The reference gates routing, and nothing else.** Then the promise sentence over-claims for
the second time — it was already narrowed on 2026-09-21 for the persistent plausible error — and
should be narrowed again: confirmation protects a machine the sweep would *newly* route, and not
one whose cancellation is already open. The model as committed is correct; what is owed is the
narrowing, a `CNF-99` case recording the bound, and probably a line in `11-open-findings.md`.

**(b) The promise governs.** Then something must hold the worker, and every candidate costs a
sentence somewhere else:

- `OPS-41`'s re-check reads the reference — which contradicts "it reads neither fact except to
  clear them", and has to distinguish the two cancellations `LDG-16` says are "never gated on
  the reference" (`LDG-64`'s bound, the suspended tenant) from the exhaustion it must gate;
- or the arming write invalidates the pending attempt — a new duty on `PRV-13e`'s re-derivation,
  reaching `OPS-39`'s episode and `OPS-48`'s table, on a machine whose episode may be `stalled`
  with a retry admissible;
- or the provider call refuses while the reference is armed, where `pv-vwe.20` already put the
  destruction deadline's check — but `OPS-41`'s 2026-09-09 scope refuses scoping by reason
  ("**any** exposure-reducing cancellation"), and the two bypasses are reasons.

## What is not in question

The setter `pv-vwe.20` built is faithful either way: arming, discharge by acceptance order, the
deadline and the routing predicate are `LDG-16`'s own sentences. What changes between the two
readings is whether anything on the worker's path reads the reference.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The owner picks a reading, and `ADR-0026` records it with the argument
- [ ] `LDG-16` carries it — either the narrowed promise, or the new gate and the sentence it
      amends, with the two bypasses preserved either way
- [ ] `CNF-99` feeds the trace above, whichever way it is answered
- [ ] The formal layer follows: a theorem or a negative control for the chosen reading, on the
      model `pv-vwe.20` landed
close_reason: dissolved by ADR-0027: the rate is a window median, so the trace cannot be built

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Dissolved by ADR-0027 (2026-09-23), not answered. The two readings this ticket offered were both
refused by a four-model panel, and so was a third (close the episode when the machine is funded
again) -- fable: "(a) with a different justification"; opus: OPS-41:755 already refused withdrawing
a queued attempt from the funding side. The owner's answer was upstream of all three: make the rate
the window median of accepted observations, so one observation cannot move a date and the queued
attempt's re-check reads a rate one reading cannot poison. The trace in this ticket cannot be
constructed under that rule; the LDG-62 shape it also names is OPS-41's re-check under a
trustworthy rate, which the set already has.

Two things this ticket's panel found stand on their own and are recorded in the ADR: PRV-13e
still promised persistence "across more than one derivation", the unit ADR-0026 retired, and
LDG-16's three sentences about the worker and the bypasses cannot all hold. Both land with the
ADR's requirements ticket.

title: The setter put LDG-16's deadline in a second home: the provider call, the restore formula, agedWorld
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`). Raised by the two-axis review of `bc08e19`
(`pv-vwe.20`'s setter), 2026-09-22. This is a decision, not a defect to fix blind: the same
shape as `pv-vwe.21`, and it touches the same sentence.

## What was found

Modelling the setter put `LDG-16`'s destruction deadline in a **second normative home**, and one
of `STO-54`'s formulas in two Lean modules. Three sites, in descending order of consequence.

### 1. The deadline moved into the provider call

`Provisiond.Fence.providerDelete` is tagged `@[req "OPS-41"]`. `bc08e19` wraps its fenced branch:

```lean
| .fenced n =>
  if w.deadlinePassed then
    { w with m := { w.m with destroyed := w.m.destroyed || applied }, phase := .dispatched n reply }
  else w
```

and adds `provider_waits_for_deadline`, tagged `@[req "LDG-16"]`, beside it.

`LDG-16` states the deadline as part of the sweep's routing predicate — "The exhaustion sweep MUST
route a machine where its stored `runway_until` has passed, its `rate_confirmation_ref` is null and
its `destroy_not_before` is null or past — and MUST NOT route it otherwise" — and says of the
re-derivation at claim that it "reads neither fact except to clear them". The new gate therefore

- puts an `LDG-16` rule inside an `OPS-41` declaration, which is the second-normative-copy shape
  `AGENTS.md` names ("One rule, one home; everywhere else points at it");
- gates the ordinary sweep path too, not only the two bypasses the docstring cites;
- makes a fenced worker whose deadline is still future a **silent no-op**: `else w` returns the
  world unchanged, so the attempt stays `.fenced` with nothing to advance it;
- rewrites two existing `OPS-42` proofs, `destroyed_only_by_provider_from_fenced` and
  `fenced_waits_for_the_provider`.

It also cuts against `pv-vwe.21`: there the deadline is what a worker re-reads and the reference is
what nothing on its path reads. Settle `pv-vwe.21` first or together, not separately.

### 2. `STO-54`'s restore formula has two homes

`Restore.World` gains `interval`, `boot` takes it as a fourth argument, and
`restore_writes_deadline` proves the deadline is `t.now + t.interval` under `STO-54`'s "the restore
instant plus one re-derivation interval". `Fence.restoreGrace` computes
`some (restoreInstant + w.interval)` for the same sentence. Two modules, one formula.

`pv-vwe.20` owed `Restore.lean` a re-quoting only; the `interval` field, `boot`'s arity and the new
theorem are beyond it. They may well be right — decide whether the formula's home is `Restore` with
`Fence` pointing at it, or the reverse.

### 3. `agedWorld` changed shape, not just its fields

The fixture had to lose `exhaustedSince` with the column. It also gained `enqueue … .exhausted`,
which is a different world, not a renamed one. Lowest stakes of the three; confirm the witness
still traps what it trapped.

## The decision

For each site: keep it and name the rule's one home (amending the requirement that loses it), or
revert it to what `pv-vwe.20` actually asked for. `ADR-0026` is the precedent for writing the
answer down rather than leaving it in the model.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the three sites resolved: kept with its home named, or reverted
- [ ] If `providerDelete`'s gate is kept, the forever-`.fenced` world is either shown unreachable
      or given the event that clears it, with a witness
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: done

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Decided 2026-09-23, with ADR-0027, and this ticket shrinks.

Site 1 -- providerDelete's deadline gate -- was not a second home. LDG-16 says the re-check "reads
neither fact except to clear them", says of the two bypasses "Neither reaches the predicate above",
and says of the same two "Both do respect the destruction deadline". The three cannot all hold: if
the bypasses never reach the sweep's predicate and must respect the deadline, the worker's path
reads the deadline. The gate is the resolution, and ADR-0027 admits it into LDG-16's text. This
ticket's first site is withdrawn as a finding; the reference half of the question is moot, since
the reference itself is withdrawn.

Site 2 -- STO-54's restore formula in both Restore and Fence -- decided: a small dedicated module
that exists for that one formula, which both import. Not Tables or Claim, which own other things;
placing it there for import convenience was the wrong reason.

Site 3 -- agedWorld's shape -- confirm the witness still traps what it trapped, when the formal
ticket of ADR-0027's epic rewrites Fence.lean anyway.

Sites 2 and 3 are absorbed by that formal ticket; this ticket closes when it lands.

title: ci.yml's fence catalogue header names a date range five of its rows fall outside
description:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml:302-303` frames the fence control catalogue as "every guard OPS-41 and
OPS-42 gained by dated amendment between 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-09 is a field of
`Provisiond.Fence.current`". Five of the fifteen `Fence` rows are no longer that: `armWinsFutureClear`,
`confirmationByOrder`, `observationKeepsDeadline` and `backwardCannotConfirm` are `LDG-16` guards
dated 2026-09-21 (`bc08e19`, `ADR-0026`), and `noAgeDischarge` is `LDG-16`'s withdrawn 2026-09-05
age discharge (`59e9ba5`).

The header is a prose summary of a list that has moved twice under it, which is `AGENTS.md`'s "cite
the list; let it hold the number" in its non-numeric form: the sentence restates the list's
membership rule instead of pointing at the list. Pre-existing — it was already wrong by four at
`496e42d`; `pv-vwe.20` made it wrong by five and did not touch it, on the `pv-vwe.22` precedent that
a ticket does not absorb the sites it merely walks past.

Fix: restate the header so it names what the list actually holds (the requirements it draws guards
from, not a closed date range), or drop the range and let the per-row dates carry it. Prose only; no
row, witness or `Params` field changes.

title: Three Fence.lean docstring points left by pv-vwe.20: a third legacyArmedAt under-count, an unnamed pointer, a misattributed frame
description:
Three prose points in `tools/formal/Provisiond/Fence.lean` that survived `pv-vwe.20`. None is read by
any gate: `tools/check_citations.py:43` says "this gate reads `*.md` only", so no gate reads a `.lean`
docstring. All three are wording; none changes what any declaration computes.

**1. A third `legacyArmedAt` sentence still under-counts its readers.** `Fence.lean:373` (`rederive`'s
docstring) reads "`legacyArmedAt` records the arming instant solely to execute the withdrawn age
control" — singular. The instant it writes (`Fence.lean:386-387`) is read by two withdrawn controls:
directly by `World.routed` (`Fence.lean:253`), and through the clock at `Fence.lean:380` by
`rederiveFacts` (`Fence.lean:309`). `pv-vwe.20` fixed this same under-count at `Fence.lean:35-37` and
`Fence.lean:216-217`, which were the two sites its brief named, so the file now says "controls ... in
`rederiveFacts` and `World.routed`" at :35 and "the withdrawn age control" at :373. The load-bearing
claim ("solely ... not a durable fact") survives, which is why this was not sent back for another
Round. `AGENTS.md`'s "one rule, one home" argues :373 should point at the module docstring rather
than restate the count. `DerivationClock`'s sentence at `Fence.lean:274` is correctly singular —
that structure is consumed only by `rederiveFacts` — and is not part of this.

**2. `Fence.lean:217`'s pointer does not name what it points at.** "inert under `current` as described
above" — the description is the module docstring roughly 180 lines earlier. Naming its owner costs
nothing and survives a reordering of the file.

**3. `Fence.lean:244`'s frame verb misattributes a verbatim quote.** It reads "`sweep` is 'routed on
the **stored** date and `LDG-16`'s facts (`World.routed`) and on nothing else'". In `sweep`'s own
sentence (`Fence.lean:459`) the participle attaches to the machine's cancellation, not to `sweep`
itself: "`LDG-14`'s 'At end of runway the machine MUST be cancelled', routed on the **stored** date
...". The quote is verbatim and must stay verbatim — it exists so a future edit to `sweep`'s
docstring visibly breaks this one — but the frame should not read as though the sweep is the thing
routed.

**Considered and deliberately left alone:** the local binding `referenceNull` (`Fence.lean:251-253`)
is `true` for an armed reference that has aged out under `noAgeDischarge := false`, so the name
asserts the reference is null when it is armed. It was reviewed in `pv-vwe.20`'s Round 2 and
accepted: it is true under `current`, which is the rule in force, and strictly better than the
`confirmed` it replaced, which was wrong under `current`. A name true of both positions
(`referenceClear`, `referenceDoesNotBlock`) would be better still. Reopen only if someone is editing
that declaration anyway.

title: The Lean quoted-attribution gate reaches 4% of the quotes, and pv-vwe.18's twelve do not reconcile
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`). Raised by the two-axis review of `cd76988`
(`pv-vwe.18`), 2026-09-22. `pv-vwe.18`'s three acceptance criteria are met as written; what is not
met is the justification the bead argued them from.

## What was measured

`pv-vwe.18` extended the `QUOTED` rule over Lean docstrings. The rule fires only where `ATTRIB`
matches — a speech verb, or `` `X`'s <noun> that ``, in the same `SPLIT` chunk as the quote.

- **30 of the 751 quotes of four words or more in Lean docstrings reach the check**, because only
  33 of 1713 chunks carry an attribution. That is 4% of what the bead called "the largest ungated
  surface in the repository".
- **Demonstrated, not inferred.** In a throwaway copy, `Admission.lean:30`'s
  `` `API-7`'s headline — "**Authentication MUST happen before request-body validation.**" `` was
  rewritten to `"**Authentication MUST happen after the body is parsed and validated.**"`, words
  that appear nowhere in `04-api-contract.md`. `python3 tools/check_citations.py` exits **0**. The
  sentence carries no speech verb, so `ATTRIB` never matches it.

## The bead's own evidence does not reconcile

`pv-vwe.18` justified itself with "a throwaway script run on 2026-09-20 over the `pv-vwe.9` diff
found **twelve** quoted spans that did not appear in the requirement they were attributed to".

- The `pv-vwe.9` tree (`3e28ce7`) was restored, Markdown and Lean, and the new gate run over it:
  **three findings, the same three false positives baselined today. Zero of the twelve.**
- One of the twelve was named in the bead: "one sentence attributed to `API-7` that is `API-40`'s".
  `git log -S` finds it unchanged since `3e28ce7`. The sentence reads
  `` `API-40` … and it says "`API-7`'s ordering applies to authenticated endpoints" ``, and that
  phrase **is** in `API-40`'s body. The prose is correct. The throwaway script blamed `API-7`
  because `API-7` sits inside the quote — the inverted attribution `find()`'s own comment rejects.
  So the headline example was itself a false positive of the script, not a defect in the repo.
- A second class the bead named, "bold markers swallowed into a quote", is unreachable **by
  construction**: `norm()` does `re.sub(r"[*`~]", "", s)`, stripping exactly those markers from
  both sides before comparison.

The honest reading is that the twelve were mostly the script's false positives, and that the
measured defect rate which justified this ticket is unestablished. That does not make the gate
worthless — it closed a real hole, and `1a2af47` and `b373fa8` fixed seven genuine stale docstring
claims by hand in the same session — but it does mean the next decision should not be taken on the
strength of "twelve".

## The decision

Widening `ATTRIB` so a quote needs no speech verb is not a Lean-only change: `ATTRIB` is the
pre-existing rule and the same widening applies to every `*.md` in the repository, where it would
surface an unknown number of findings and would have to be ratcheted. That is a change to a rule
this set already owns, so it is `ADR`-shaped rather than an implementation detail. The alternatives:

1. **Widen `ATTRIB`** — a quote adjacent to a citation is attributed, verb or no verb. Measure the
   Markdown blast radius first; the baseline grows by whatever it finds.
2. **A Lean-only ATTRIB** — docstrings are prose written to explain one declaration, so a quote
   near a citation there is likelier to be an attribution than in requirement prose. Costs a second
   rule with a scope condition, which `AGENTS.md`'s "one rule, one home" argues against.
3. **Accept 4% and say so.** Narrow the gate's own docstring claim from the surface it reads to the
   quotes it can actually check, so no later reader takes green as evidence the docstrings are
   clean. Cheapest, and honest, but leaves the hole `pv-vwe.18` was opened to close.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The chosen option decided with its measurement, not its estimate — for (1), the Markdown
      finding count measured before the rule changes
- [ ] Whatever is chosen, `check_citations.py`'s module docstring states the reach the gate
      actually has, since it is the file's own record of what it does and does not cover
- [ ] A red build for the newly-covered shape, if the reach widens
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: Done in ef16d1a; see the closing comment

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Markdown (`*.md` at the root) | 0 | 194 | 50 |
| Lean docstrings | 3 (baselined) | 598 | 62 |

Markdown findings by file: `11-open-findings.md` 22, `impl-report-01.md` 5, then 4 or fewer each

**Precision is low.** A sample of seven Markdown findings, each read in its sentence, and eleven

in full:

- **Real, one:** `03-operation-lifecycle.md:774` and `:913-914` put "what makes `OPS-33`'s early
  release safe" in quote marks as `OPS-36`'s words. `OPS-36` says "**This is the branch that makes
  `OPS-33`'s early release safe**" (`:553-554`, unchanged since `56a7d56`); the quoted form was
  written by `660cd59` (2026-08-31) and was never verbatim. `:913` also says `OPS-36` "called

  because "calls" is not in `SPEECH`.

title: LDG-38 says the key protects exact replays; a replay that rounds or clamps to nothing escapes it
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe`. Raised by `pv-vwe.16`'s Implementer and by two of its Panel's Reviewers (astra, sol), 2026-09-26.

## What the model shows

`LDG-38` (`12-billing-and-ledger.md`, the high-water paragraph) gives the mark's reason as "without the mark the
deduplication key protects only exact replays, not overlapping ones". That is too generous to the key. `LDG-8`'s key sits on
the entry, and a conflict is a refused insert. An exact replay whose recomputed debit rounds or clamps to nothing inserts no
row (`STO-45`'s "transaction with no ledger entry"), so nothing conflicts, yet `r` moves and, where it clamped, a second
`STO-37` deficiency is booked. Evaluated in `Provisiond.Funding` with `markDiscards := false`:

- `[post 1 (1/2), post 1 (1/2)]` leaves one entry of −1, as the key promises, but moves `r` from 1/2 to 0.
- With 1 sat of commitment left, `[post 7 (7/5), post 7 (7/5)]` books a second deficiency of 1 and moves `r` from 3/5 to 1/5.

Under `Funding.current` the mark refuses all of these (`post_replay_discarded`). So the specified system's behaviour is not in
question; only the sentence's account of what each guard buys is.

## Also

- `Provisiond.Witnesses.remeter_charged_without_the_mark` quotes that sentence over a trace whose first half is an *exact*
  replay the key admits. The quote is verbatim, but its re-meter half is the only part it supports.
- The Panel read `pv-vwe.16`'s brief ("A key collision refuses the whole increment") as requiring the key to refuse whenever it
  is already held, even with no insert. The Manager rejected that: it models a pre-check the specification does not require,
  and a deployment's unique index behaves the way the model does.

## Decide

Whether to amend `LDG-38`'s sentence, for example to "the key protects only replays that write an entry", with a dated note
after the record. Then align the witness's docstring.
close_reason: LDG-38 and LDG-8 say what the key stops (an insert, where the first posting left a key) and that the mark and the start rule stop every replay; STO-45 says a discarded increment moves nothing; CNF-160 carries the case; the witnesses' docstrings moved with the sentences.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Corrections from the Spec axis of the two-axis review of `f166a01` (2026-09-26), checked by `#eval`:

1. **The example wording above is false.** "The key protects only replays that write an entry" does
   not hold: in `remeterTrace` with `discardOff`, the replay of `post 9 (2/5)` DOES write an entry
   (−1 under key k9) and the key does not stop it, because the ORIGINAL posting wrote none. The
   accurate form is "only replays of an increment whose first posting wrote an entry".
2. **`LDG-8` makes the same over-claim, and this ticket names only `LDG-38`.** `LDG-8`'s "derives the
   *same* key and conflicts" (12-billing-and-ledger.md ~127–128) is the sentence
   `increment_replay_refused_by_key` quotes. Any amendment covers both sentences, each with its
   dated note after the record.
3. **`STO-45` leaves the discarded increment implicit.** Its "Every increment updates it" reads as
   universal and does not carve out an increment `LDG-38` discards. The model treats a discard as
   moving nothing, the only reading consistent with "discarded, not posted", but the text never
   says so. Same family; decide it with this one.

Under the rules as they stand the behaviour is not in question: the high-water mark refuses these
replays (`post_replay_discarded`), and under `current` an increment end never posts twice. This is
a wording decision about what the key alone promises.

comments.author: master
comments.text: Decided 2026-10-02 by the owner: say what each one protects. With pv-vwe.30's start rule (an increment starts at the subject's latest high-water mark), the mark and the start rule stop every replay, exact or overlapping; the idempotency key is a backstop only for replays of an increment whose first posting wrote an entry. Amend LDG-38's 'without the mark the deduplication key protects only exact replays, not overlapping ones' and LDG-8's 'derives the *same* key and conflicts', each with its dated note, and STO-45 states that a discarded increment moves nothing. Rejected: a zero-amount entry per increment so the key sees every replay (a row per tick; contradicts LDG-72's 'a mark ahead of every entry is ordinary'). Land with pv-vwe.30: both edit LDG-38.

title: ADR-0025 says rational witnesses close by decide +kernel; two ci.yml row witnesses cannot
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe`. Raised by `pv-vwe.16`'s Implementer, 2026-09-26.

## The conflict

`ADR-0025`'s trust-policy bullet says "Witnesses over rationals close by `decide +kernel`." A refuted `decide +kernel` witness
over `Std.Rat` reports that its instance "did not reduce". `ci.yml`'s Params loop requires the red to read `decide`
"proved that the proposition" false, and fails the row otherwise. So `increment_replay_refused_by_key` and
`mark_discards_what_the_key_admits`, the rows' red witnesses in `pv-vwe.16`, close by `with_unfolding_all decide`. That is
kernel-checked and passes the axiom gate. The exception is recorded in `Witnesses.lean`'s module docstring, a second home
for a rule whose home is the ADR.

## Options

1. Amend `ADR-0025`'s sentence to name `with_unfolding_all decide` for witnesses a `ci.yml` row must see refuted, and cut
   the restatement in `Witnesses.lean` down to a pointer.
2. Widen the loop's check to accept the kernel's "did not reduce" message, and return the two witnesses to `decide +kernel`.
   Risk: the message no longer distinguishes a refuted witness from one that simply fails to evaluate.

`pv-vwe.17` will meet the same question when it adds Params fields.

title: Wire canonicalization and redaction
description:
## Parent

pv-vwe — the formal layer, M2 through M8 (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

`API-12`'s canonical serialization and the fingerprint preimage as functions; `API-21`/`STO-50`'s projections from internal records into public views as explicit functions, so a new internal field cannot leak through generic serialization; `SEC-8`'s foreign-and-absent indistinguishability as a theorem on observable responses. Lean knows nothing about HTTP; parser and transport correspondence is a named assumption.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Canonicalization idempotent and key-order insensitive, proved
- [ ] Fingerprint preimage includes the endpoint, decided on the request-target construction
- [ ] Redaction idempotent; a projection is independent of every field marked private
- [ ] `SEC-8`: equal observable responses for an absent and a foreign-owned machine
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, and every new check's CI negative control asserts the red came from that check.
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff (standards against `AGENTS.md`/`ADR-0025`/the glossary, spec against the cited requirement sentences) applied before the next ticket starts.

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately)

title: LDG-38 places an increment's start only after a rate-change split, so a re-meter spanning the mark charges seconds twice
description:
Raised by the Spec axis of the two-axis review of `f166a01` (`pv-vwe.16`), 2026-09-26, from the model.

## What was found

`LDG-38` discards an increment "at or before" the high-water mark, keyed on the increment's **end**.
Nothing in the set states where an increment **starts**. So a re-meter that re-observes seconds the
mark already covers, in one increment ending after the mark, is admitted whole.

Trace under `Funding.current`, every rule on: `[post 7 (7/5), post 10 2]`, where the second posting
is a re-meter re-observing seconds 0–10. The mark is 7, the second increment ends at 10, so it is
neither discarded by the mark nor refused by the key (k10 is new), and it posts −2 under k10.
Seconds 0–7 are charged twice.

`lean-01.md` (~170–174) asked for exactly this: an increment's start as well as its end. The
model's omission list (`Funding.lean` ~72–93) does not name increment starts either.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

The repair is a requirement's: either `LDG-38` states that an increment starts at the mark (or at
the previous increment's end) and clips the charge to it, or the key carries the start, or the text
argues why a re-observation spanning the mark cannot arise. That choice is the owner's.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `LDG-38` (or its owner) says where an increment starts, or says in its own text why an
      increment spanning the mark cannot be posted, with the argument and not an assertion
- [ ] `Provisiond.Funding` models the start, or names it in the omissions with the reason
close_reason: LDG-38 carries the seed and the start rule (an increment starts at the subject's latest high-water mark, split at every period boundary and rate change; a re-meter overlapping the mark is clipped); LDG-72 says how the latest mark is read; CNF-304, CNF-305; Provisiond.Funding models the start (startsAtMark) and the seed (seedOnBillable), no_second_charged_twice is the theorem, each with a ci.yml row.

description:
Raised by the two-axis review of `bc6a6fd` (`pv-vwe.17`), 2026-09-26. Neither point is a defect in
what is proved; both are about what the witness shows and where a proof lives.

1. **The split witness moves no money.** `straddle_split_at_the_boundary` (`Witnesses.lean`
   ~1282–1294) on `straddleTrace`: split and whole post the same total AND the same per-period sums
   (`[1,1]` both ways); the flip is caught only through period 0's extra `(10, 0)` row, a zero debit
   that `LDG-72` says is written "without a ledger entry". So the `splitAtBoundary` row reds on a
   difference no ledger would show. The Spec reviewer computed stronger traces:
   - `[9→11]` alone: split posts `(10,1) ∣ (11,1)`, total 2; whole posts `– ∣ (11,1)`, total 1.
   - `[5→6, 8→11]` keeps the old period's own credit in play: split posts period 0 as
     `[(6,1),(10,1)]` (the second is ⌈4/5 − 3/5⌉ = 1); per-period sums `[2,1]` split against
     `[1,2]` whole.
   Replace the trace (or add a sibling) so the witness asserts a money difference, keep the row's
   one-word token, and rehearse the row.
2. **Two Meter properties are proved in Period.** `creditAfter_bounds` is purely about
   `Meter.creditAfter`, and `postings_sum_is_ceil` proves what `Meter.debits_sum`'s docstring
   already claims ("With `r_0 = 0` and `0 ≤ r_n < 1`, the integer `Σ d` is `ceil(Σ x)`"). AGENTS.md:
   "Arguments have owners too". Move the Meter-only lemma to `Meter.lean` (a new theorem there is
   not a change to `Meter.postedDebit` or the corruption bound) and have Period use it, or say in
   Period why it lives there.

Also on record, not for this ticket: `bc6a6fd`'s message says `split` "cuts a straddling increment
at each boundary inside it", which holds only with the boundaries in order (the code's own docstring
states the condition, `split_straddles_nothing`).

Done: both points applied or declined with a reason; every `ci.yml` row rehearsed with one scratch
copy; `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped.

title: Only API-63 closes an increment when a subject stops billing; an ordinary stop never charges the last partial interval
description:
Raised by all four readers of the 2026-10-02 panel on `pv-vwe.30` (fable, opus, astra, sol), each
independently. Pre-existing; separate from where an increment starts.

## What was found

Only `API-63` requires a closing increment when a subject stops billing: "post each subject's
closing partial increment against its commitment (`LDG-38`), for the time between its last increment
end and the recording instant" (`04-api-contract.md` ~1251–1252), and only for an account recorded
`terminated`. An ordinary stop — `LDG-74`'s gone observation, a successful delete — has no such
rule; `LDG-32`'s "the machine stops billing" is a precondition, not a posting rule. So a subject
billable for less than one meter interval (`LDG-37`: "at least one transaction per billable subject
per interval") is never charged, and every subject's last partial interval is charged only if a tick
happens to land between its last increment end and its stop. `API-63` itself notes that a debit
after release can be clamped away entirely ("the customer's last minutes would be free").

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `LDG-38` (or `LDG-74`) requires the write that stops a subject's meter to post the closing
      increment from the subject's latest mark to the stop instant, in the same transaction and
      before any commitment release, as `API-63` does for termination
- [ ] A `CNF` case: a machine billable for less than one interval is charged for its billable
      seconds
close_reason: Accepted after Round 2 review. Landed in 815b61bca6acc325905176a59b03fb03c26acb49 and 4e1da999bccc06dd383ed85698ecaa834868247e: exit-owned increment closure, outage/quarantine handling, conformance, arbitrary marked/unmarked lifecycle coverage and close-before-release proofs. Required gates pass; workflow negative-control evidence is in /var/tmp/provisiond-vwe34-control-evidence/final-summary.tsv and /var/tmp/provisiond-r2-controls-_lc96gff/results.json. title: QUOTE mispairs after an unpaired mark: a quotation SPLIT cuts, or a quoted span under 8 characters, hides the quotes after it from every rule
description:
Found by the opus Reviewer of the pv-vwe.25 Run, 2026-10-02, and verified by mutation.

tools/check_citations.py's SPLIT is `(?<=[.!?])\s+|...`. It breaks on a sentence ender followed by whitespace inside a quotation as readily as outside it, so a two-sentence quotation, or a `... ` elision with a space after the period, is cut in two chunks each holding an unpaired quote mark; QUOTE matches neither half and the span is counted by no rule. Corrupting Fence.lean:168's `OPS-41` quote "keyed on the tenant's current state ... and not on the episode's \`reasons\` set" to "current posture" exits 0 with the printed quote count unchanged. `…` (U+2026) and `...,` reach fragments() and are checked.

Measured on the tree at the Run's close: 32 chunks carry an odd number of straight quote marks, about 16 spans across eight files (Fence 10, Tables 8, Wire 4, Admission, Claim, Rehost, Restore, Witnesses 2 each). The module docstring names the limit under "What it cannot see" for both rules.

Changing SPLIT changes QUOTED's reach over Markdown and Lean alike, so it is a measured decision: count the Markdown and Lean findings a quote-aware splitter (one that does not cut inside a paired quotation) surfaces before choosing. Alternative: reword the standing spans so the elision carries no trailing whitespace, which fixes the inventory and not the hole.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Either SPLIT no longer cuts inside a paired quotation, with the Markdown and Lean finding counts measured before the change and the residue disposed of (misquotes fixed, the rest baselined with a reason), or the decision not to is recorded with that measurement
- [ ] If changed: a ci.yml negative control that corrupts a two-sentence or spaced-elision quotation and asserts the named finding
- [ ] nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh green, unpiped
close_reason: Implemented and validated in c834a1d; measurement and acceptance evidence in comments

        result[name] = measure()
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))

title: Concurrent gate runs can expose a truncated formal index to citation and region checks
description:
## Observed failure

During the independent Round-1 review of pv-gip.21 at 8cf2253, Opus's first full gate failed in citations and regions with JSONDecodeError while the same unmodified source passed on rerun. The retained log is /var/tmp/review-3453423-gates-final.log. It reports:

- lake build completed successfully;
- lake exe gate reported 720 tagged declarations and no axiom-policy violations;
- the immediately following wrapper count saw only 42 index lines;
- both consumers failed in check_citations.read_index at json.loads, with "Expecting value: line 1 column 1".

The panel report is .rloop/runs/20261005T142936.630893945Z-3453423/feedback-1-opus.md. It also reports a NUL-filled head in the index, consistent with overlapping truncating writers. The Manager directly checked the retained traceback/count log and the wrapper/consumer source; the particular competing process was not identified. A later complete gate on this same revision passed, as did the Manager's independent gate.

## Source of the race

Current tools/check_formal.sh writes shared build artifacts directly:

    lake exe gate > .lake/index.jsonl
    lake exe render > .lake/regions.jsonl

There is no publication/reader coordination around these writes. check-all.sh orders generation before consumers within one invocation, but a second invocation in the same working tree can truncate the same files while the first reads them. tools/check_citations.py read_index and tools/check_regions.py load_formal consume those paths directly.

The index failure was observed. The regions publication path has the same shape but was not separately reproduced. This is an existing gate failure on unrelated shared output, not a defect in CNF-99 and not a reason to reopen pv-gip.21. It meets the follow-up criterion of a check failing for the wrong reason.

## Required outcome and verification

Ensure overlapping gate invocations on an unchanged working tree cannot expose partially published index/region output to their consumers. Preserve the existing fail-closed handling of generation failure, missing toolchains and invalid formal content; do not turn read failures into skips or certify stale output from a failed generation. Implementation mechanism is deliberately left undecided.

Add a reproducible overlap/interleaving regression that fails under the current publication path for the intended reason and passes with the repair, and exercise generation-failure behavior. Re-run the affected ci.yml negative controls in place with restoration between mutations and the required unpiped full gate. Avoid concurrent tracked-source mutations: this issue concerns competing artifact publication on identical source, not coordinating different edits to one tree.

No specification policy change is requested. Priority is low because serial gate runs pass; the issue affects parallel readers sharing a checkout.

title: Fence core: both commit orderings of OPS-42
description:
## Parent

pv-vwe — the formal layer, M2 through M8 (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

The cancellation fence composed on the claim model. Model state: the machine's commitment, stored `runway_until`, the fence as an optional episode id; events: sweep routing on the stored date, claim, the fence transaction with its funding re-check inside it as a Bool parameter, extension in its own serialization guarded on the fence, provider delete outside the serialization, reply, settlement. `OPS-42`: 'The cancellation and the extension MUST contend for one row, so that one of them provably loses'.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Extension first: the re-check reads the grown commitment and the worker makes no provider call
- [ ] Fence first: the extension is refused, opening no commitment and moving no balance
- [ ] Destruction only after a fence transaction whose re-check read unfunded
- [ ] Witness: re-check outside the fence transaction admits the paid-machine deletion
- [ ] Witness: the fence holding the attempt id refuses a legitimate retry
- [ ] A successful cancellation witness and a successful extension witness
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, and every new check's CI negative control asserts the red came from that check.
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff (standards against `AGENTS.md`/`ADR-0025`/the glossary, spec against the cited requirement sentences) applied before the next ticket starts.

## Blocked by

- pv-vwe.1
close_reason: Fence core landed: Provisiond/Fence.lean, six witnesses, two CI controls; check-all green

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Reading choices the Markdown leaves open, recorded at close (2026-09-16):
1. The lost-race abort ('another actor won') settles as the same terminal transaction as the funded abort and writes the re-derived runway_until; OPS-41 conditions that write on the funded case, OPS-42 says only 'settle as OPS-41 requires'. On a machine read unfunded the stored date it writes is no later than the one it had.
2. 'Destruction only after a fence transaction whose re-check read unfunded' lands as three step-level theorems (destroyed_only_by_provider_from_fenced, fenced_only_by_fence_txn, fenced_waits_for_the_provider) chained by docstring, not one invariant over reachable worlds; pv-vwe.10's 'over all reachable states' criterion is where a Reachable predicate belongs.
3. The sweep routes nothing while an episode is open; joining an open episode (OPS-39) is pv-vwe.10's.
4. Every witness trace carries the split variant's fenceWrite step, inert under current, so one schedule runs both designs and the CI control turns exactly one witness red.
Two-axis review applied: writeDate flag removed from finish (pv-vwe.10's parameter, added early); omissions paragraph extended (abort predicate, date writes, retry-from-stalled, fence-names-open-episode, LDG-62 sizing, resolved_at); LDG-69/OPS-39/LDG-10 assertions turned into quotes; retry docstring re-attributed to OPS-48's row.

title: Reconciliation knowledge
description:
## Parent

## What to build

Knowledge about a resource as its own type — `unknown`, `observed present`, `authoritative absence`, `multiple candidates` — separate from the commitment's open or closed. `OPS-33`: 'the commitment MUST be closed and released in full even though the operation remains open'. Absence evidence as three conjuncts: a complete pass, the effective window elapsed, a direct reread. Two window fields, never one. `OPS-27`'s correlator match as proof an order landed, not that a resource exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Release after the negative window leaves knowledge unchanged, proved
- [ ] `unknown` with a closed commitment is a reachable positive witness
- [ ] Absence requires all three conjuncts; each one dropped admits a witness that stops the meter on a live machine
- [ ] A correlator match alone never yields `observed present`
- [ ] Duplicate candidates across channels count once, keyed by account and external identity

title: OPS-23's worker re-check states a kind and retryable only for a missing field, not a present malformed one (OPS-23, API-13)
description:
Found during the `pv-6p8` drain review (branch `pv-6p8`), 2026-10-22.

**The problem.** `OPS-23` says "Validation that was performed at the API boundary MUST be repeated in the worker before the driver is called". The rules that follow give a kind and a `retryable` only for "a missing required field". A field that is present but fails an `API-13` rule at the worker re-check, such as a record edited in the store or written by an older `api`, has no stated kind, `retryable` or settlement.

`pv-6p8` added a disk-identifier row to `API-13` ("a JSON string, non-empty after normalization (`RSC-46`)"). A stored `layout.drives[].identifier` of `"  "` is present, so the missing-field rules don't reach it. The worker re-check refuses it before the driver is called, so it never reaches `RSC-26`'s `integrity` abort. The gap is not specific to this row: it holds for every `API-13` row.

**Example.** Engine A fails the re-check with `invalid_request` and `retryable: false`, by analogy with the caller-field row. Engine B fails it with `conflict`/`incomplete_record` and `retryable: true`, treating a store edit like an `api`-written field. Engine C skips the re-check for this row and lets the install enter rescue and abort `integrity`. An agent obeys `retryable` differently in each case.

**Question.** What kind, `retryable` and settlement does `OPS-23`'s worker re-check give a present but malformed value, for create, install, power and delete?
close_reason: **Already implemented; close without a new brief.** `OPS-23` now states: “A field that is present but fails this repeated validation fails as its writer's bullet above says, on both the error and the operation view, and settles as these missing-field failures do.” That directly supplies the kind, retryability, and settlement requested in this filing. Keep the separate install-timing ambiguity in `pv-hups`; closing this bead must not claim that timing is resolved.

description: Surfaced by the 2026-09-14 three-reviewer check of pv-vwe.2. On provider_native/provider_catalogue the marker means dispatch only, where a 4xx after dispatch is honestly failed. Decide whether the row should distinguish the two marker meanings (n_r past a bytes-on-disk marker for every kind) or stand. The Lean (tools/formal/Provisiond/Tables.lean, installRow) follows the row as written; a decision changes one arm and the row together.

title: Claim-time create failures state no retryable: OPS-43's price_moved and API-63's account check (DOM-17, WIR-9a, CNF-241, CNF-278)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Two claim-time create failures state no `retryable` value.

- **`price_moved`.** `OPS-43` fails a create at claim "where the provider's price has risen past
  what the reserve covers: `conflict`, `details.reason: "price_moved"`, the shortfall in
  `details`, telling the caller to re-submit". `CNF-241` asserts the kind, the reason and the
  shortfall, but no `retryable`.
- **The account check.** `API-63`'s claim-time conditional write fails "`conflict`, with
  `details.reason: "account_terminated"` where the status is `terminated` and `"state"` for the
  two recoverable statuses", and states no `retryable`. `pv-14b` adds a plain `STO-47` read as the
  first claim step, failing the same way, so this failure becomes more common. `CNF-278` asserts
  the reason only. `WIR-9a`'s values for the same pair do not reach it: they apply to "a create
  account whose collection-snapshot `STO-47` status" is read in the admission tail.

`DOM-17` requires every error to carry "a boolean `retryable`", which "describes whether repeating
the *same request* is safe and sensible" and "is normative guidance to callers (`API-51`)".

Two claim-time refusals do state their value:
- `PRV-40`'s closure: "operation-view `retryable: true`";
- `OPS-43`'s unsellable offer: "`retryable: false` on both the error and the operation view".

`OPS-23`'s missing-field failure will too, once `pv-14b` lands.

Example: a create fails `price_moved`. Engine A reads "telling the caller to re-submit" as
`retryable: true`, so an obedient agent re-sends, and a fresh admission prices the create at the
new price. Engine B reads "the same request" as the one that just failed at this price and sends
`retryable: false`, so the agent stops. Likewise, a create claimed on a `credentials_rejected`
account gets `true` from an engine that copies the purchase-tail table and `false` from one that
doesn't. In both cases the same failure produces opposite caller behaviour.

Question: what `retryable` do `price_moved` and the claim-time account failure (`state`,
`account_terminated`) carry on the error and the operation view, and should `CNF-241` and `CNF-278`
assert them?

Found by panel r55b (fable) for `price_moved`. Panel r55's synthesis records the account case
("No text gives a `retryable` value for `API-63`'s claim-time failure"). Both are in
`docs/research/panels-2026-10/r55/synthesis.md`. Pre-existing: both predate `pv-14b`.

title: PRV-47 does not say which kind a create fails with when one validation rejects a caller value and a system-written value together (PRV-47, OPS-11, WIR-9a)
description:
Found by panel r62c (readers voted 4-0 to file it as a bead), while drafting `pv-gpw` (`docs/research/panels-2026-10/r62/final-form.md`, "File with the drain PR", item 1).

One `PRV-47` validation can reject a caller-supplied value and a value this system wrote in the same create. `PRV-47` gives the caller value `invalid_request` with `retryable: false` and, since `pv-gpw`, the system-written value `internal` with `retryable` from `OPS-11`'s create row (`true`). One reader (unvoted) argued that `internal` should win, "since a caller fix cannot clear a defect". This bead records the gap; it does not decide it.

title: WIR-9a's field pointer does not say what a rejected combination names: trust's exclusive members, an invalid union discriminator, an array element (WIR-9a, WIR-2, WIR-20)
description:
> *Filed 2026-10-22 while judging panel B (pv-7j3, pv-p3k, pv-009, pv-gpw, pv-ss4), from a full read of the set at `1bdf453`.*

`WIR-9a`'s new `details.field` row (pv-ss4, applied to create, install, power and delete by the owner's "Wide: all four ops") orders *several rejected fields*. It does not say which pointer names a rejection of a combination of fields.

- `WIR-9a` (`13:134`): `field` is "an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the request body", and "Where one validation step rejects several fields …, the least escaped pointer, compared by unsigned UTF-16 code units".
- `WIR-20` (`13:693`): the rescue-entering install variants "additionally carry a required `trust` object**, exactly one of three, not two". The three are `{"use_provider_keys": true}`, `{"expected_host_keys": [...]}` and `{"accept_unpinned": true}`.
- `API-13` (`04:976`): "pinned keys and "accept unpinned" MUST be mutually exclusive". `RSC-4` (`06:101`): "Caller-supplied keys and the first-use-trust opt-in MUST be mutually exclusive".

Take a `rootfs_via_rescue` install whose `trust` is `{"expected_host_keys": [...], "accept_unpinned": true}`:
- one engine names the object, `/trust`;
- one treats both members as rejected and names the least, `/trust/accept_unpinned`;
- one names the member it checked second, `/trust/expected_host_keys`.

All three can cite the row.

The same holds for any closed discriminated-union body when the discriminator itself is invalid: install's `strategy`, and `WIR-35`'s `resolution`. One engine names the discriminator. Another treats the variant's own fields as unknown under `WIR-2` and names the least of those.

Nothing says whether a bad array element is named by the array (`/ssh_public_keys`) or the element (`/ssh_public_keys/1`).

Owners: `WIR-9a`, `WIR-2`, `WIR-20`.

title: Apply ADR-0037 Q31: Robot's post-order cancellation read is one attempt with an absorbed failure
description:
Apply ADR-0037's amendment of 2026-10-14 (owner decision Q31): Robot's post-order cancellation read is one
attempt at the create's settlement, and its failure is absorbed. Panel: docs/research/panels-2026-10/r48/.

Read the amendment first; it is the decision. The gap it closes: `PRV-13c` says "order, then **read**" but no
requirement says when that read runs, what writes `machines.earliest_cancellation_date`, or what a failed read
does. Today a failure either sends a delivered create to `needs_reconciliation` (if read inside the accepted
create: `PRV-5` "Known acceptance MUST remain `true` on every later error", `OPS-11`) or silently prices
nothing.

Work order (requirement text and conformance only):
1. `PRV-13c`: the driver reads the per-machine cancellation constraint once, when the create settles, after
   `OPS-27`'s confirming read. A failed read of any kind, `rate_limited` included, does not enter `OPS-11`'s
   classifier and does not change the create's settlement; `PRV-31`'s declared bound remains the priced term;
   `PRV-5`'s alarm is raised; the read is not retried. A later accepted cancellation's response (`PRV-13`)
   supplies the per-machine date. Keep "order, then **read**" and `PRV-13`'s "That separate post-order read
   remains required."
2. `OPS-11`: its read-failure exception (today only `PRV-13`'s accepted dated cancellation read-back) also
   covers this read, by citing `PRV-13c` — one owner, no restatement.
3. `OPS-27` (or wherever create settlement is owned): place the read after the confirming read, by citation.
4. `05-persistence.md` `machines.earliest_cancellation_date`: say what writes it (the post-order read on
   success; the accepted cancellation response) and that it stays null after a failed post-order read.
5. Conformance: `CNF-147` (or `CNF-356`) gains a failed post-order read fixture, `rate_limited` included: the
   create settles as it would have, the declared bound is priced, the alarm is raised, no retry is sent.
6. If `08-provider-notes.md` lists what spends the account's `/server` counter, add the post-order read there
   with ADR-0036's bound (at most about 40 per hour across the two ordering endpoints).

Lean: none, unless an existing model already represents the post-order read (`Runway.lean` says it "does not
derive its cost-through-earliest-date term"); then follow ADR-0025.

Rules: quote, don't restate (AGENTS.md "Cite the owner"); RFC 2119 keywords; rendered regions stay in step;
gates `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` unpiped, exit 0. A question about what a requirement
means that the ADR does not answer is a BLOCK for the owner.

Accepted at c2b5675. Owner follow-ups (operator observed path, writer precedence, declared-bound storage, CNF-147 standard channel) are in this ticket's comments.

Exact old/new text follows, by identifier. Unchanged text in each item remains unchanged.

PRV-13c
OLD: No Q31 paragraph.
NEW:
*Amended 2026-10-14 (`ADR-0037`, Q31).* The driver MUST read the per-machine cancellation
constraint once, when the create settles, after `OPS-27`'s confirming read ("the first row
MUST be confirmed by a direct read before it attaches anything").
A failed post-order read of any kind, `rate_limited` included, MUST NOT enter `OPS-11`'s
classifier and MUST NOT change the create's settlement. On failure, the declared bound
MUST remain the priced term (`PRV-31`: "The declared bound sizes the commitment at create").
Absorbing the failure MUST NOT suppress `PRV-5`'s "raise a monitorable alarm naming the
provider account and request path" where its trigger applies.
The post-order read MUST NOT be retried; no resolution pass, refresh, sweep or later
operation MAY read that machine's cancellation constraint again.
A successful post-order read MUST supply `machines.earliest_cancellation_date`; a later
accepted cancellation's response (`PRV-13`) MUST supply the per-machine date to that column.
These are its only writers. After a failed post-order read, the column MUST remain null
until such a response supplies the date.

OPS-27
OLD: No Q31 paragraph.
NEW:
*Amended 2026-10-14 (`ADR-0037`, Q31).* At every entry point to the landed-order transaction
above, `PRV-13c`'s "once, when the create settles, after `OPS-27`'s confirming read"
places the post-order read after confirmation and before that transaction begins, outside
any store transaction and with no tenant primitive held (`STO-55`: "MUST NOT hold a transaction
open across a provider, rail or rescue-host call"; `LDG-69`: "MUST NOT wait on a running
operation's hold on its machine (`OPS-8`), the completion of a child operation (`API-58`,
`WIR-39`), or any provider call"). The machine row in that transaction carries the returned
date or null under `PRV-13c`'s "A successful post-order read MUST supply
`machines.earliest_cancellation_date`" and "After a failed post-order read, the column MUST
remain null until such a response supplies the date".

OPS-11 exception paragraph

The accepted dated cancellation read-back (`PRV-13`) is an evidence read after a successful
mutating response. Failure of that read alone does not enter this failure classifier; the
settlement for the known accepted date belongs to `PRV-13`. This exception does not reclassify
unknown acceptance or a later failure of the mutating request. *Clarified 2026-10-11
(`ADR-0037`, Q22).*

mutating response. Failure of that read alone does not enter this failure classifier; the

This exception does not reclassify
unknown acceptance or a later failure of the mutating request. *Clarified 2026-10-11
